# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic Basic HTTP authentication. Allowed headers-- Authorization: Basic <api_key> | Authorization: Basic <base64 hash of `api_key:`>

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Bearer HTTP authentication. Allowed headers-- Authorization: Bearer <api_key>

<h1 id="stripe-api-default">Default</h1>

## GetAccount

<a id="opIdGetAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/account \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/account`

<p>Retrieves the details of an account.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## PostAccountLinks

<a id="opIdPostAccountLinks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/account_links \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'account=string&collect=currently_due&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&refresh_url=string&return_url=string&type=account_onboarding'
```

`POST /v1/account_links`

<p>Creates an AccountLink object that includes a single-use Stripe URL that the platform can redirect their user to in order to take them through the Connect Onboarding flow.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account: string
collect: currently_due
expand:
  - string
refresh_url: string
return_url: string
type: account_onboarding
```

<h3 id="postaccountlinks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account|body|string|true|The identifier of the account to create an account link for.|
|» collect|body|string|false|Which information the platform needs to collect from the user. One of `currently_due` or `eventually_due`. Default is `currently_due`.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» refresh_url|body|string|false|The URL the user will be redirected to if the account link is expired, has been previously-visited, or is otherwise invalid. The URL you specify should attempt to generate a new account link with the same parameters used to create the original account link, then redirect the user to the new account link's URL so they can continue with Connect Onboarding. If a new account link cannot be generated or the redirect fails you should display a useful error to the user.|
|» return_url|body|string|false|The URL that the user will be redirected to upon leaving or completing the linked flow.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of account link the user is requesting. Possible values are `account_onboarding` or `account_update`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» collect|currently_due|
|» collect|eventually_due|
|» type|account_onboarding|
|» type|account_update|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "expires_at": 0,
  "object": "account_link",
  "url": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "charge": "string",
    "code": "string",
    "decline_code": "string",
    "doc_url": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "param": "string",
    "payment_intent": {},
    "payment_method": {},
    "payment_method_type": "string",
    "request_log_url": "string",
    "setup_intent": {},
    "source": {},
    "type": "api_error"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="postaccountlinks-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|[account_link](#schemaaccount_link)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## GetAccounts

<a id="opIdGetAccounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/accounts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/accounts`

<p>Returns a list of accounts connected to your platform via <a href="/docs/connect">Connect</a>. If you’re not a platform, the list is empty.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getaccounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h3 id="getaccounts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="getaccounts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[account](#schemaaccount)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|list|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

`POST /v1/accounts`

<p>With <a href="/docs/connect">Connect</a>, you can create Stripe accounts for your users.
To do this, you’ll first need to <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/applications/settings">register your platform</a>.</p>

<p>If you’ve already collected information for your connected accounts, you <a href="/docs/connect/best-practices#onboarding">can pre-fill that information</a> when
creating the account. Connect Onboarding won’t ask for the pre-filled information during account onboarding.
You can pre-fill any information on the account.</p>

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}`

<p>Updates a <a href="/docs/connect/accounts">connected account</a> by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided are
left unchanged.</p>

<p>For Custom accounts, you can update any information on the account. For other accounts, you can update all information until that
account has started to go through Connect Onboarding. Once you create an <a href="/docs/api/account_links">Account Link</a>
for a Standard or Express account, some parameters can no longer be changed. These are marked as <strong>Custom Only</strong> or <strong>Custom and Express</strong>
below.</p>

<p>To update your own account, use the <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/account">Dashboard</a>. Refer to our
<a href="/docs/connect/updating-accounts">Connect</a> documentation to learn more about updating accounts.</p>

## DeleteAccountsAccount

<a id="opIdDeleteAccountsAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/accounts/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /v1/accounts/{account}`

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}/bank_accounts/{id}`

<p>Updates the metadata, account holder name, account holder type of a bank account belonging to a <a href="/docs/connect/custom-accounts">Custom account</a>, and optionally sets it as the default for its currency. Other bank account details are not editable by design.</p>

<p>You can re-enable a disabled bank account by performing an update call without providing any arguments or changes.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account_holder_name: string
account_holder_type: ""
account_type: checking
address_city: string
address_country: string
address_line1: string
address_line2: string
address_state: string
address_zip: string
default_for_currency: true
exp_month: string
exp_year: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
```

|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» account_holder_name|body|string|false|The name of the person or business that owns the bank account.|
|» account_holder_type|body|string|false|The type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`.|
|» account_type|body|string|false|The bank account type. This can only be `checking` or `savings` in most countries. In Japan, this can only be `futsu` or `toza`.|
|» address_city|body|string|false|City/District/Suburb/Town/Village.|
|» address_country|body|string|false|Billing address country, if provided when creating card.|

|» address_state|body|string|false|State/County/Province/Region.|
|» address_zip|body|string|false|ZIP or postal code.|
|» default_for_currency|body|boolean|false|When set to true, this becomes the default external account for its currency.|
|» exp_month|body|string|false|Two digit number representing the card’s expiration month.|
|» exp_year|body|string|false|Four digit number representing the card’s expiration year.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|

|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}/external_accounts/{id}`

<p>Updates the metadata, account holder name, account holder type of a bank account belonging to a <a href="/docs/connect/custom-accounts">Custom account</a>, and optionally sets it as the default for its currency. Other bank account details are not editable by design.</p>

```yaml
account_holder_name: string
account_holder_type: ""
account_type: checking
address_city: string
address_country: string
address_line1: string
address_line2: string
address_state: string
address_zip: string

  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
```

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» account_holder_name|body|string|false|The name of the person or business that owns the bank account.|
|» account_holder_type|body|string|false|The type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`.|

|» default_for_currency|body|boolean|false|When set to true, this becomes the default external account for its currency.|
|» exp_month|body|string|false|Two digit number representing the card’s expiration month.|
|» exp_year|body|string|false|Four digit number representing the card’s expiration year.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|

```bash
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /v1/accounts/{account}/people/{person}`

<p>Deletes an existing person’s relationship to the account’s legal entity. Any person with a relationship for an account can be deleted through the API, except if the person is the <code>account_opener</code>. If your integration is using the <code>executive</code> parameter, you cannot delete the only verified <code>executive</code> on file.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

|person|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|


`GET /v1/accounts/{account}/persons`

<p>Returns a list of people associated with the account’s legal entity. The people are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recent people appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|relationship|query|object|false|Filters on the list of people returned based on the person's relationship to the account's company.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## DeleteAccountsAccountPersonsPerson

<a id="opIdDeleteAccountsAccountPersonsPerson"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/accounts/string/persons/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /v1/accounts/{account}/persons/{person}`

<p>Deletes an existing person’s relationship to the account’s legal entity. Any person with a relationship for an account can be deleted through the API, except if the person is the <code>account_opener</code>. If your integration is using the <code>executive</code> parameter, you cannot delete the only verified <code>executive</code> on file.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|path|string|true|none|
|person|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## PostAccountsAccountReject

<a id="opIdPostAccountsAccountReject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/accounts/string/reject \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&reason=string'
```

`POST /v1/accounts/{account}/reject`

<p>With <a href="/docs/connect">Connect</a>, you may flag accounts as suspicious.</p>

<p>Test-mode Custom and Express accounts can be rejected at any time. Accounts created using live-mode keys may only be rejected once all balances are zero.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
reason: string
```

<h3 id="postaccountsaccountreject-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» reason|body|string|true|The reason for rejecting the account. Can be `fraud`, `terms_of_service`, or `other`.|

## PostApplicationFeesIdRefunds

<a id="opIdPostApplicationFeesIdRefunds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/application_fees/string/refunds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/application_fees/{id}/refunds`

<p>Refunds an application fee that has previously been collected but not yet refunded.
Funds will be refunded to the Stripe account from which the fee was originally collected.</p>

<p>You can optionally refund only part of an application fee.
You can do so multiple times, until the entire fee has been refunded.</p>

<p>Once entirely refunded, an application fee can’t be refunded again.
This method will raise an error when called on an already-refunded application fee,
or when trying to refund more money than is left on an application fee.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
```

<h3 id="postapplicationfeesidrefunds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer, in _cents (or local equivalent)_, representing how much of this fee to refund. Can refund only up to the remaining unrefunded amount of the fee.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

```json
    "property2": "string"
  },

}
```

## PostBillingPortalConfigurations

<a id="opIdPostBillingPortalConfigurations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/billing_portal/configurations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'business_profile=%7B%22headline%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22privacy_policy_url%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22terms_of_service_url%22%3A%22string%22%7D&default_return_url=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&features=%7B%22customer_update%22%3A%7B%22allowed_updates%22%3A%5B%22address%22%5D%2C%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22invoice_history%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22payment_method_update%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22subscription_cancel%22%3A%7B%22cancellation_reason%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22options%22%3A%5B%22customer_service%22%5D%7D%2C%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22mode%22%3A%22at_period_end%22%2C%22proration_behavior%22%3A%22always_invoice%22%7D%2C%22subscription_pause%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22subscription_update%22%3A%7B%22default_allowed_updates%22%3A%5B%22price%22%5D%2C%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22products%22%3A%5B%7B%22prices%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22product%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%2C%22proration_behavior%22%3A%22always_invoice%22%7D%7D&login_page=%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/billing_portal/configurations`

<p>Creates a configuration that describes the functionality and behavior of a PortalSession</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
business_profile:
  headline: string
  privacy_policy_url: string
  terms_of_service_url: string
default_return_url: string
expand:
  - string
features:
  customer_update:
    allowed_updates:
      - address
    enabled: true
  invoice_history:
    enabled: true
  payment_method_update:
    enabled: true
  subscription_cancel:
    cancellation_reason:
      enabled: true
      options:
        - customer_service
    enabled: true
    mode: at_period_end
    proration_behavior: always_invoice
  subscription_pause:
    enabled: true
  subscription_update:
    default_allowed_updates:
      - price
    enabled: true
    products:
      -
        prices:
          - string
        product: string
    proration_behavior: always_invoice
login_page:
  enabled: true
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
```

```yaml
    enabled: true
    products:
      -

login_page:
```

`POST /v1/billing_portal/sessions`

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|transfer_group|query|string|false|Only return charges for this transfer group.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

`POST /v1/charges`

<p>To charge a credit card or other payment source, you create a <code>Charge</code> object. If your API key is in test mode, the supplied payment source (e.g., card) won’t actually be charged, although everything else will occur as if in live mode. (Stripe assumes that the charge would have completed successfully).</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
application_fee: 0
application_fee_amount: 0
capture: true
card:
  address_city: string
  address_country: string
  address_line1: string
  address_line2: string
  address_state: string
  address_zip: string
  cvc: string
  exp_month: 0
  exp_year: 0
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  name: string
  number: string
  object: card
currency: string
customer: string
description: string
destination:
  account: string
  amount: 0
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
on_behalf_of: string
radar_options:
  session: string
receipt_email: string
shipping:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  carrier: string
  name: string
  phone: string
  tracking_number: string
source: string
statement_descriptor: string
statement_descriptor_suffix: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
  destination: string
transfer_group: string
```

<h3 id="postcharges-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Amount intended to be collected by this payment. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).|
|» application_fee|body|integer|false|none|
|» application_fee_amount|body|integer|false|A fee in cents (or local equivalent) that will be applied to the charge and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The request must be made with an OAuth key or the `Stripe-Account` header in order to take an application fee. For more information, see the application fees [documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/direct-charges#collecting-fees).|
|» capture|body|boolean|false|Whether to immediately capture the charge. Defaults to `true`. When `false`, the charge issues an authorization (or pre-authorization), and will need to be [captured](https://stripe.com/docs/api#capture_charge) later. Uncaptured charges expire after a set number of days (7 by default). For more information, see the [authorizing charges and settling later](https://stripe.com/docs/charges/placing-a-hold) documentation.|
|» card|body|object \| string|false|A token, like the ones returned by [Stripe.js](https://stripe.com/docs/js).|

Note that if you use Stripe to send automatic email receipts to your customers, your receipt emails will include the `description` of the charge(s) that they are describing.|

The receipt will not be sent until the charge is paid, and no receipts will be sent for test mode charges. If this charge is for a [Customer](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object), the email address specified here will override the customer's email address. If `receipt_email` is specified for a charge in live mode, a receipt will be sent regardless of your [email settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/emails).|

`GET /v1/charges/search`

<p>Search for charges you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

|next_page|string \| null|false|none|none|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|total_count|integer|false|none|The total number of objects that match the query, only accurate up to 10,000.|
|url|string|true|none|none|

## PostChargesCharge

<a id="opIdPostChargesCharge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/charges/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'customer=string&description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&fraud_details=%7B%22user_report%22%3A%22%22%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&receipt_email=string&shipping=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22carrier%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tracking_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&transfer_group=string'
```

`POST /v1/charges/{charge}`

<p>Updates the specified charge by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided will be left unchanged.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
customer: string
description: string
expand:
  - string
fraud_details:
  user_report: ""
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
receipt_email: string
shipping:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  carrier: string
  name: string
  phone: string
  tracking_number: string
transfer_group: string
```

<h3 id="postchargescharge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» customer|body|string|false|The ID of an existing customer that will be associated with this request. This field may only be updated if there is no existing associated customer with this charge.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string which you can attach to a charge object. It is displayed when in the web interface alongside the charge. Note that if you use Stripe to send automatic email receipts to your customers, your receipt emails will include the `description` of the charge(s) that they are describing.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» fraud_details|body|object|false|A set of key-value pairs you can attach to a charge giving information about its riskiness. If you believe a charge is fraudulent, include a `user_report` key with a value of `fraudulent`. If you believe a charge is safe, include a `user_report` key with a value of `safe`. Stripe will use the information you send to improve our fraud detection algorithms.|
|» » user_report|body|string|true|none|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» receipt_email|body|string|false|This is the email address that the receipt for this charge will be sent to. If this field is updated, then a new email receipt will be sent to the updated address.|
|» shipping|body|object|false|Shipping information for the charge. Helps prevent fraud on charges for physical goods.|
|» » address|body|object|true|none|
|» » » city|body|string|false|none|
|» » » country|body|string|false|none|
|» » » line1|body|string|false|none|
|» » » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » » postal_code|body|string|false|none|
|» » » state|body|string|false|none|
|» » carrier|body|string|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|none|
|» » phone|body|string|false|none|
|» » tracking_number|body|string|false|none|
|» transfer_group|body|string|false|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. `transfer_group` may only be provided if it has not been set. See the [Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » user_report|""|
|» » user_report|fraudulent|
|» » user_report|safe|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

## PostChargesChargeCapture

<a id="opIdPostChargesChargeCapture"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/charges/string/capture \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&application_fee=0&application_fee_amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&receipt_email=string&statement_descriptor=string&statement_descriptor_suffix=string&transfer_data=%7B%22amount%22%3A0%7D&transfer_group=string'
```

`POST /v1/charges/{charge}/capture`

<p>Capture the payment of an existing, uncaptured, charge. This is the second half of the two-step payment flow, where first you <a href="#create_charge">created a charge</a> with the capture option set to false.</p>

<p>Uncaptured payments expire a set number of days after they are created (<a href="/docs/charges/placing-a-hold">7 by default</a>). If they are not captured by that point in time, they will be marked as refunded and will no longer be capturable.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
application_fee: 0
application_fee_amount: 0
expand:
  - string
receipt_email: string
statement_descriptor: string
statement_descriptor_suffix: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
transfer_group: string
```

<h3 id="postchargeschargecapture-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|The amount to capture, which must be less than or equal to the original amount. Any additional amount will be automatically refunded.|
|» application_fee|body|integer|false|An application fee to add on to this charge.|
|» application_fee_amount|body|integer|false|An application fee amount to add on to this charge, which must be less than or equal to the original amount.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» receipt_email|body|string|false|The email address to send this charge's receipt to. This will override the previously-specified email address for this charge, if one was set. Receipts will not be sent in test mode.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|For card charges, use `statement_descriptor_suffix` instead. Otherwise, you can use this value as the complete description of a charge on your customers’ statements. Must contain at least one letter, maximum 22 characters.|
|» statement_descriptor_suffix|body|string|false|Provides information about the charge that customers see on their statements. Concatenated with the prefix (shortened descriptor) or statement descriptor that’s set on the account to form the complete statement descriptor. Maximum 22 characters for the concatenated descriptor.|
|» transfer_data|body|object|false|An optional dictionary including the account to automatically transfer to as part of a destination charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/destination-charges) for details.|
|» » amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» transfer_group|body|string|false|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. `transfer_group` may only be provided if it has not been set. See the [Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

## PostChargesChargeRefund

<a id="opIdPostChargesChargeRefund"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/charges/string/refund \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&instructions_email=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&payment_intent=string&reason=duplicate&refund_application_fee=true&reverse_transfer=true'
```

`POST /v1/charges/{charge}/refund`

<p>When you create a new refund, you must specify a Charge or a PaymentIntent object on which to create it.</p>

<p>Creating a new refund will refund a charge that has previously been created but not yet refunded.
Funds will be refunded to the credit or debit card that was originally charged.</p>

<p>You can optionally refund only part of a charge.
You can do so multiple times, until the entire charge has been refunded.</p>

<p>Once entirely refunded, a charge can’t be refunded again.
This method will raise an error when called on an already-refunded charge,
or when trying to refund more money than is left on a charge.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
expand:
  - string
instructions_email: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
payment_intent: string
reason: duplicate
refund_application_fee: true
reverse_transfer: true
```

<h3 id="getcheckoutsessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Sessions for the Customer specified.|
|customer_details|query|object|false|Only return the Checkout Sessions for the Customer details specified.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|payment_intent|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Session for the PaymentIntent specified.|
|payment_link|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Sessions for the Payment Link specified.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|subscription|query|string|false|Only return the Checkout Session for the subscription specified.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

|» customer|body|string|false|ID of an existing Customer, if one exists. In `payment` mode, the customer’s most recent card<br>payment method will be used to prefill the email, name, card details, and billing address<br>on the Checkout page. In `subscription` mode, the customer’s [default payment method](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/update#update_customer-invoice_settings-default_payment_method)<br>will be used if it’s a card, and otherwise the most recent card will be used. A valid billing address, billing name and billing email are required on the payment method for Checkout to prefill the customer's card details.<br><br>If the Customer already has a valid [email](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-email) set, the email will be prefilled and not editable in Checkout.<br>If the Customer does not have a valid `email`, Checkout will set the email entered during the session on the Customer.<br><br>If blank for Checkout Sessions in `payment` or `subscription` mode, Checkout will create a new Customer object based on information provided during the payment flow.<br><br>You can set [`payment_intent_data.setup_future_usage`](https://stripe.com/docs/api/checkout/sessions/create#create_checkout_session-payment_intent_data-setup_future_usage) to have Checkout automatically attach the payment method to the Customer you pass in for future reuse.|
|» customer_creation|body|string|false|Configure whether a Checkout Session creates a [Customer](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers) during Session confirmation.<br><br>When a Customer is not created, you can still retrieve email, address, and other customer data entered in Checkout<br>with [customer_details](https://stripe.com/docs/api/checkout/sessions/object#checkout_session_object-customer_details).<br><br>Sessions that don't create Customers instead are grouped by [guest customers](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/checkout/guest-customers)<br>in the Dashboard. Promotion codes limited to first time customers will return invalid for these Sessions.<br><br>Can only be set in `payment` and `setup` mode.|
|» customer_email|body|string|false|If provided, this value will be used when the Customer object is created.<br>If not provided, customers will be asked to enter their email address.<br>Use this parameter to prefill customer data if you already have an email<br>on file. To access information about the customer once a session is<br>complete, use the `customer` field.|
|» customer_update|body|object|false|Controls what fields on Customer can be updated by the Checkout Session. Can only be provided when `customer` is provided.|

## PostCheckoutSessionsSessionExpire

<a id="opIdPostCheckoutSessionsSessionExpire"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/checkout/sessions/string/expire \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/checkout/sessions/{session}/expire`

<p>A Session can be expired when it is in one of these statuses: <code>open</code> </p>

<p>After it expires, a customer can’t complete a Session and customers loading the Session see a message saying the Session is expired.</p>

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

## PostCoupons

<a id="opIdPostCoupons"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/coupons \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount_off=0&applies_to=%7B%22products%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%7D&currency=string&currency_options=%7B%22property1%22%3A%7B%22amount_off%22%3A0%7D%2C%22property2%22%3A%7B%22amount_off%22%3A0%7D%7D&duration=forever&duration_in_months=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&id=string&max_redemptions=0&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string&percent_off=0&redeem_by=0'
```

`POST /v1/coupons`

<p>You can create coupons easily via the <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/coupons">coupon management</a> page of the Stripe dashboard. Coupon creation is also accessible via the API if you need to create coupons on the fly.</p>

<p>A coupon has either a <code>percent_off</code> or an <code>amount_off</code> and <code>currency</code>. If you set an <code>amount_off</code>, that amount will be subtracted from any invoice’s subtotal. For example, an invoice with a subtotal of <currency>100</currency> will have a final total of <currency>0</currency> if a coupon with an <code>amount_off</code> of <amount>200</amount> is applied to it and an invoice with a subtotal of <currency>300</currency> will have a final total of <currency>100</currency> if a coupon with an <code>amount_off</code> of <amount>200</amount> is applied to it.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount_off: 0
applies_to:
  products:
    - string
currency: string
currency_options:
  property1:
    amount_off: 0
  property2:
    amount_off: 0
duration: forever
duration_in_months: 0
expand:
  - string
id: string
max_redemptions: 0
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
percent_off: 0
redeem_by: 0
```

<h3 id="postcoupons-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount_off|body|integer|false|A positive integer representing the amount to subtract from an invoice total (required if `percent_off` is not passed).|
|» applies_to|body|object|false|A hash containing directions for what this Coupon will apply discounts to.|
|» » products|body|[string]|false|none|
|» currency|body|string|false|Three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies) of the `amount_off` parameter (required if `amount_off` is passed).|
|» currency_options|body|object|false|Coupons defined in each available currency option (only supported if `amount_off` is passed). Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » amount_off|body|integer|true|none|
|» duration|body|string|false|Specifies how long the discount will be in effect if used on a subscription. Defaults to `once`.|
|» duration_in_months|body|integer|false|Required only if `duration` is `repeating`, in which case it must be a positive integer that specifies the number of months the discount will be in effect.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» id|body|string|false|Unique string of your choice that will be used to identify this coupon when applying it to a customer. If you don't want to specify a particular code, you can leave the ID blank and we'll generate a random code for you.|
|» max_redemptions|body|integer|false|A positive integer specifying the number of times the coupon can be redeemed before it's no longer valid. For example, you might have a 50% off coupon that the first 20 readers of your blog can use.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the coupon displayed to customers on, for instance invoices, or receipts. By default the `id` is shown if `name` is not set.|
|» percent_off|body|number|false|A positive float larger than 0, and smaller or equal to 100, that represents the discount the coupon will apply (required if `amount_off` is not passed).|
|» redeem_by|body|integer(unix-time)|false|Unix timestamp specifying the last time at which the coupon can be redeemed. After the redeem_by date, the coupon can no longer be applied to new customers.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» duration|forever|
|» duration|once|
|» duration|repeating|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

```bash
  -d 'amount=0&credit_amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&invoice=string&lines=%5B%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22invoice_line_item%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%2C%22tax_rates%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22type%22%3A%22custom_line_item%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D&memo=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&out_of_band_amount=0&reason=duplicate&refund=string&refund_amount=0&shipping_cost=%7B%22shipping_rate%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/credit_notes`

<p>Issue a credit note to adjust the amount of a finalized invoice. For a <code>status=open</code> invoice, a credit note reduces
its <code>amount_due</code>. For a <code>status=paid</code> invoice, a credit note does not affect its <code>amount_due</code>. Instead, it can result
in any combination of the following:</p>

<ul>
<li>Refund: create a new refund (using <code>refund_amount</code>) or link an existing refund (using <code>refund</code>).</li>
<li>Customer balance credit: credit the customer’s balance (using <code>credit_amount</code>) which will be automatically applied to their next invoice when it’s finalized.</li>
<li>Outside of Stripe credit: record the amount that is or will be credited outside of Stripe (using <code>out_of_band_amount</code>).</li>
</ul>

<p>For post-payment credit notes the sum of the refund, credit and outside of Stripe amounts must equal the credit note total.</p>

<p>You may issue multiple credit notes for an invoice. Each credit note will increment the invoice’s <code>pre_payment_credit_notes_amount</code>
or <code>post_payment_credit_notes_amount</code> depending on its <code>status</code> at the time of credit note creation.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
credit_amount: 0
expand:
  - string
invoice: string
lines:
  -
    amount: 0
    description: string
    invoice_line_item: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
    type: custom_line_item
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
memo: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
out_of_band_amount: 0
reason: duplicate
refund: string
refund_amount: 0
shipping_cost:
  shipping_rate: string
```

`GET /v1/customers`

<p>Returns a list of your customers. The customers are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recent customers appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getcustomers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|email|query|string|false|A case-sensitive filter on the list based on the customer's `email` field. The value must be a string.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|test_clock|query|string|false|Provides a list of customers that are associated with the specified test clock. The response will not include customers with test clocks if this parameter is not set.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## PostCustomersCustomer

<a id="opIdPostCustomersCustomer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/customers/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'address=%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D&balance=0&bank_account=%7B%22account_holder_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22account_holder_type%22%3A%22company%22%2C%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22object%22%3A%22bank_account%22%2C%22routing_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&card=%7B%22address_city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_state%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22address_zip%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22cvc%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22exp_month%22%3A0%2C%22exp_year%22%3A0%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22object%22%3A%22card%22%7D&cash_balance=%7B%22settings%22%3A%7B%22reconciliation_mode%22%3A%22automatic%22%7D%7D&coupon=string&default_alipay_account=string&default_bank_account=string&default_card=string&default_source=string&description=string&email=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&invoice_prefix=string&invoice_settings=%7B%22custom_fields%22%3A%5B%7B%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22value%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%2C%22default_payment_method%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22footer%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22rendering_options%22%3A%7B%22amount_tax_display%22%3A%22%22%7D%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&name=string&next_invoice_sequence=0&phone=string&preferred_locales=%5B%22string%22%5D&promotion_code=string&shipping=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D&source=string&tax=%7B%22ip_address%22%3A%22string%22%7D&tax_exempt='
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}`

<p>Updates the specified customer by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided will be left unchanged. For example, if you pass the <strong>source</strong> parameter, that becomes the customer’s active source (e.g., a card) to be used for all charges in the future. When you update a customer to a new valid card source by passing the <strong>source</strong> parameter: for each of the customer’s current subscriptions, if the subscription bills automatically and is in the <code>past_due</code> state, then the latest open invoice for the subscription with automatic collection enabled will be retried. This retry will not count as an automatic retry, and will not affect the next regularly scheduled payment for the invoice. Changing the <strong>default_source</strong> for a customer will not trigger this behavior.</p>

<p>This request accepts mostly the same arguments as the customer creation call.</p>

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/bank_accounts`

<p>When you create a new credit card, you must specify a customer or recipient on which to create it.</p>

<p>If the card’s owner has no default card, then the new card will become the default.
However, if the owner already has a default, then it will not change.
To change the default, you should <a href="/docs/api#update_customer">update the customer</a> to have a new <code>default_source</code>.</p>

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/cards`

<p>When you create a new credit card, you must specify a customer or recipient on which to create it.</p>

<p>If the card’s owner has no default card, then the new card will become the default.
However, if the owner already has a default, then it will not change.
To change the default, you should <a href="/docs/api#update_customer">update the customer</a> to have a new <code>default_source</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
alipay_account: string
bank_account:
  account_holder_name: string
  account_holder_type: company
  account_number: string
  country: string
  currency: string
  object: bank_account
  routing_number: string
card:

  address_country: string
  address_line1: string
  address_line2: string
  address_state: string
  address_zip: string
  cvc: string
  exp_month: 0

expand:
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/sources`

<p>When you create a new credit card, you must specify a customer or recipient on which to create it.</p>

<p>If the card’s owner has no default card, then the new card will become the default.
However, if the owner already has a default, then it will not change.
To change the default, you should <a href="/docs/api#update_customer">update the customer</a> to have a new <code>default_source</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
alipay_account: string
bank_account:
  account_holder_name: string
  account_holder_type: company
  account_number: string
  country: string
  currency: string
  object: bank_account
  routing_number: string
card:
  address_city: string
  address_country: string
  address_line1: string
  address_line2: string
  address_state: string
  address_zip: string
  cvc: string
  exp_month: 0
  exp_year: 0
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  name: string
  number: string
  object: card
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
source: string
```

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

```bash
  -d 'amounts=%5B0%5D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/sources/{id}/verify`

<p>Verify a specified bank account for a given customer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amounts:
  - 0
expand:
  - string
```

|» amounts|body|[integer]|false|Two positive integers, in *cents*, equal to the values of the microdeposits sent to the bank account.|

## GetCustomersCustomerSubscriptions

<a id="opIdGetCustomersCustomerSubscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/customers/string/subscriptions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/customers/{customer}/subscriptions`

<p>You can see a list of the customer’s active subscriptions. Note that the 10 most recent active subscriptions are always available by default on the customer object. If you need more than those 10, you can use the limit and starting_after parameters to page through additional subscriptions.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getcustomerscustomersubscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|path|string|true|none|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

`POST /v1/customers/{customer}/subscriptions`

<p>Creates a new subscription on an existing customer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
add_invoice_items:
  -
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
application_fee_percent: 0
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
backdate_start_date: 0
billing_cycle_anchor: 0
billing_thresholds:
  amount_gte: 0
  reset_billing_cycle_anchor: true
cancel_at: 0
cancel_at_period_end: true
collection_method: charge_automatically
coupon: string
currency: string
days_until_due: 0
default_payment_method: string
default_source: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
expand:
  - string
items:
  -
    billing_thresholds:
      usage_gte: 0
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
off_session: true
payment_behavior: allow_incomplete
payment_settings:
  payment_method_options:
    acss_debit:
      mandate_options:
        transaction_type: business
      verification_method: automatic
    bancontact:
      preferred_language: de
    card:
      mandate_options:
        amount: 0
        amount_type: fixed
        description: string
      network: amex
      request_three_d_secure: any
    customer_balance:
      bank_transfer:
        eu_bank_transfer:
          country: string
        type: string
      funding_type: string
    konbini: {}
    us_bank_account:
      financial_connections:
        permissions:
          - balances
      verification_method: automatic
  payment_method_types:
    - ach_credit_transfer
  save_default_payment_method: off
pending_invoice_item_interval:
  interval: day
  interval_count: 0
promotion_code: string
proration_behavior: always_invoice
transfer_data:
  amount_percent: 0
  destination: string
trial_end: now
trial_from_plan: true
trial_period_days: 0
trial_settings:
  end_behavior:
    missing_payment_method: cancel
```

Such as failed payments, [SCA regulation](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/migration/strong-customer-authentication), or collecting a mandate for a bank debit payment method. If the payment intent is not confirmed within 23 hours subscriptions transition to `status=incomplete_expired`, which is a terminal state.<br><br>Use `error_if_incomplete` if you want Stripe to return an HTTP 402 status code if a subscription's first invoice cannot be paid. `POST /v1/customers/{customer}/subscriptions/{subscription_exposed_id}`

<p>Updates an existing subscription on a customer to match the specified parameters. When changing plans or quantities, we will optionally prorate the price we charge next month to make up for any price changes. To preview how the proration will be calculated, use the <a href="#upcoming_invoice">upcoming invoice</a> endpoint.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
add_invoice_items:
  -
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
application_fee_percent: 0
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
billing_cycle_anchor: now
billing_thresholds:
  amount_gte: 0
  reset_billing_cycle_anchor: true
cancel_at: 0
cancel_at_period_end: true
cancellation_details:
  comment: string
  feedback: ""
collection_method: charge_automatically
coupon: string
days_until_due: 0
default_payment_method: string
default_source: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
expand:
  - string
items:
  -
    billing_thresholds:
      usage_gte: 0
    clear_usage: true
    deleted: true
    id: string
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
off_session: true
pause_collection:
  behavior: keep_as_draft
  resumes_at: 0
payment_behavior: allow_incomplete
payment_settings:
  payment_method_options:
    acss_debit:
      mandate_options:
        transaction_type: business
      verification_method: automatic
    bancontact:
      preferred_language: de
    card:
      mandate_options:
        amount: 0
        amount_type: fixed
        description: string
      network: amex
      request_three_d_secure: any
    customer_balance:
      bank_transfer:
        eu_bank_transfer:
          country: string
        type: string
      funding_type: string
    konbini: {}
    us_bank_account:
      financial_connections:
        permissions:
          - balances
      verification_method: automatic
  payment_method_types:
    - ach_credit_transfer
  save_default_payment_method: off
pending_invoice_item_interval:
  interval: day
  interval_count: 0
promotion_code: string
proration_behavior: always_invoice
proration_date: 0
transfer_data:
  amount_percent: 0
  destination: string
trial_end: now
trial_from_plan: true
trial_settings:
  end_behavior:
    missing_payment_method: cancel
```

<h3 id="postcustomerscustomersubscriptionssubscriptionexposedid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|path|string|true|none|
|subscription_exposed_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» add_invoice_items|body|[object]|false|A list of prices and quantities that will generate invoice items appended to the next invoice for this subscription. You may pass up to 20 items.|
|» » price|body|string|false|none|
|» » price_data|body|object|false|none|
|» » » currency|body|string|true|none|
|» » » product|body|string|true|none|
|» » » tax_behavior|body|string|false|none|
|» » » unit_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » unit_amount_decimal|body|string(decimal)|false|none|
|» » quantity|body|integer|false|none|
|» » tax_rates|body|[string] \| string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» application_fee_percent|body|number|false|A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice subtotal that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The request must be made by a platform account on a connected account in order to set an application fee percentage. For more information, see the application fees [documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/subscriptions#collecting-fees-on-subscriptions).|
|» automatic_tax|body|object|false|Automatic tax settings for this subscription. We recommend you only include this parameter when the existing value is being changed.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» billing_cycle_anchor|body|string|false|Either `now` or `unchanged`. Setting the value to `now` resets the subscription's billing cycle anchor to the current time. For more information, see the billing cycle [documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/billing-cycle).|
|» billing_thresholds|body|object \| string|false|Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the subscription advanced to a new billing period. Pass an empty string to remove previously-defined thresholds.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » amount_gte|body|integer|false|none|
|» » reset_billing_cycle_anchor|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» cancel_at|body|integer(unix-time) \| string|false|A timestamp at which the subscription should cancel. If set to a date before the current period ends, this will cause a proration if prorations have been enabled using `proration_behavior`. If set during a future period, this will always cause a proration for that period.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» cancel_at_period_end|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether this subscription should cancel at the end of the current period.|
|» cancellation_details|body|object|false|Details about why this subscription was cancelled|
|» » comment|body|string|false|none|
|» » feedback|body|string|false|none|
|» collection_method|body|string|false|Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay this subscription at the end of the cycle using the default source attached to the customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`. Defaults to `charge_automatically`.|
|» coupon|body|string|false|The ID of the coupon to apply to this subscription. A coupon applied to a subscription will only affect invoices created for that particular subscription.|
|» days_until_due|body|integer|false|Number of days a customer has to pay invoices generated by this subscription. Valid only for subscriptions where `collection_method` is set to `send_invoice`.|
|» default_payment_method|body|string|false|ID of the default payment method for the subscription. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription. This takes precedence over `default_source`. If neither are set, invoices will use the customer's [invoice_settings.default_payment_method](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-invoice_settings-default_payment_method) or [default_source](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-default_source).|
|» default_source|body|string|false|ID of the default payment source for the subscription. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription and be in a chargeable state. If `default_payment_method` is also set, `default_payment_method` will take precedence. If neither are set, invoices will use the customer's [invoice_settings.default_payment_method](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-invoice_settings-default_payment_method) or [default_source](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-default_source).|
|» default_tax_rates|body|[string] \| string|false|The tax rates that will apply to any subscription item that does not have `tax_rates` set. Invoices created will have their `default_tax_rates` populated from the subscription. Pass an empty string to remove previously-defined tax rates.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|

## DeleteCustomersCustomerSubscriptionsSubscriptionExposedId

<a id="opIdDeleteCustomersCustomerSubscriptionsSubscriptionExposedId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/customers/string/subscriptions/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&invoice_now=true&prorate=true'
```

`DELETE /v1/customers/{customer}/subscriptions/{subscription_exposed_id}`

<p>Cancels a customer’s subscription. If you set the <code>at_period_end</code> parameter to <code>true</code>, the subscription will remain active until the end of the period, at which point it will be canceled and not renewed. Otherwise, with the default <code>false</code> value, the subscription is terminated immediately. In either case, the customer will not be charged again for the subscription.</p>

<p>Note, however, that any pending invoice items that you’ve created will still be charged for at the end of the period, unless manually <a href="#delete_invoiceitem">deleted</a>. If you’ve set the subscription to cancel at the end of the period, any pending prorations will also be left in place and collected at the end of the period. But if the subscription is set to cancel immediately, pending prorations will be removed.</p>

<p>By default, upon subscription cancellation, Stripe will stop automatic collection of all finalized invoices for the customer. This is intended to prevent unexpected payment attempts after the customer has canceled a subscription. However, you can resume automatic collection of the invoices manually after subscription cancellation to have us proceed. Or, you could check for unpaid invoices before allowing the customer to cancel the subscription at all.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
invoice_now: true
prorate: true
```

<h3 id="deletecustomerscustomersubscriptionssubscriptionexposedid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|path|string|true|none|
|subscription_exposed_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» invoice_now|body|boolean|false|Can be set to `true` if `at_period_end` is not set to `true`. Will generate a final invoice that invoices for any un-invoiced metered usage and new/pending proration invoice items.|
|» prorate|body|boolean|false|Can be set to `true` if `at_period_end` is not set to `true`. Will generate a proration invoice item that credits remaining unused time until the subscription period end.|


`POST /v1/disputes/{dispute}`

<p>When you get a dispute, contacting your customer is always the best first step. If that doesn’t work, you can submit evidence to help us resolve the dispute in your favor. You can do this in your <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/disputes">dashboard</a>, but if you prefer, you can use the API to submit evidence programmatically.</p>

<p>Depending on your dispute type, different evidence fields will give you a better chance of winning your dispute. To figure out which evidence fields to provide, see our <a href="/docs/disputes/categories">guide to dispute types</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
evidence:
  access_activity_log: string
  billing_address: string
  cancellation_policy: string
  cancellation_policy_disclosure: string
  cancellation_rebuttal: string
  customer_communication: string
  customer_email_address: string
  customer_name: string
  customer_purchase_ip: string
  customer_signature: string
  duplicate_charge_documentation: string
  duplicate_charge_explanation: string
  duplicate_charge_id: string
  product_description: string
  receipt: string
  refund_policy: string
  refund_policy_disclosure: string
  refund_refusal_explanation: string
  service_date: string
  service_documentation: string
  shipping_address: string
  shipping_carrier: string
  shipping_date: string
  shipping_documentation: string
  shipping_tracking_number: string
  uncategorized_file: string
  uncategorized_text: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
submit: true
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

`POST /v1/disputes/{dispute}/close`

<p>Closing the dispute for a charge indicates that you do not have any evidence to submit and are essentially dismissing the dispute, acknowledging it as lost.</p>

<p>The status of the dispute will change from <code>needs_response</code> to <code>lost</code>. <em>Closing a dispute is irreversible</em>.</p>

## GetEvents

<a id="opIdGetEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/events \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/events`

<p>List events, going back up to 30 days. Each event data is rendered according to Stripe API version at its creation time, specified in <a href="/docs/api/events/object">event object</a> <code>api_version</code> attribute (not according to your current Stripe API version or <code>Stripe-Version</code> header).</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getevents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|delivery_success|query|boolean|false|Filter events by whether all webhooks were successfully delivered. If false, events which are still pending or have failed all delivery attempts to a webhook endpoint will be returned.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|type|query|string|false|A string containing a specific event name, or group of events using * as a wildcard. The list will be filtered to include only events with a matching event property.|
|types|query|[string]|false|An array of up to 20 strings containing specific event names. The list will be filtered to include only events with a matching event property. You may pass either `type` or `types`, but not both.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "account": "string",
```

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/files \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -F 'expand=["string"]' \
  -F 'file=string' \
  -F 'file_link_data={"create":true,"expires_at":0,"metadata":{"property1":"string","property2":"string"}}' \
  -F 'purpose=account_requirement'
```

`POST /v1/files`

<p>To upload a file to Stripe, you’ll need to send a request of type <code>multipart/form-data</code>. The request should contain the file you would like to upload, as well as the parameters for creating a file.</p>

<p>All of Stripe’s officially supported Client libraries should have support for sending <code>multipart/form-data</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
file: string
file_link_data:
  create: true
  expires_at: 0
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
purpose: account_requirement
```

<h3 id="postfiles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» file|body|string|true|A file to upload. The file should follow the specifications of RFC 2388 (which defines file transfers for the `multipart/form-data` protocol).|
|» file_link_data|body|object|false|Optional parameters to automatically create a [file link](https://stripe.com/docs/api#file_links) for the newly created file.|
|» » create|body|boolean|true|none|
|» » expires_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|none|
|» » metadata|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» purpose|body|string|true|The [purpose](https://stripe.com/docs/file-upload#uploading-a-file) of the uploaded file.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » *anyOf*|""|
|» purpose|account_requirement|
|» purpose|additional_verification|
|» purpose|business_icon|
|» purpose|business_logo|
|» purpose|customer_signature|
|» purpose|dispute_evidence|
|» purpose|identity_document|
|» purpose|pci_document|
|» purpose|tax_document_user_upload|
|» purpose|terminal_reader_splashscreen|

> Example responses

```json
  "created": 0,
  "expires_at": 0,
  "filename": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "links": {
    "data": [
      {}
    ],
    "has_more": true,
    "object": "list",
    "url": "string"
  },
  "object": "file",

}
```

`POST /v1/financial_connections/sessions`

```yaml
  - string

  - balances
```

<h3 id="postfinancialconnectionssessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account_holder|body|object|true|The account holder to link accounts for.|
|» » account|body|string|false|none|

## PostIdentityVerificationSessions

<a id="opIdPostIdentityVerificationSessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/identity/verification_sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&options=%7B%22document%22%3A%7B%22allowed_types%22%3A%5B%22driving_license%22%5D%2C%22require_id_number%22%3Atrue%2C%22require_live_capture%22%3Atrue%2C%22require_matching_selfie%22%3Atrue%7D%7D&return_url=string&type=document'
```

`POST /v1/identity/verification_sessions`

<p>Creates a VerificationSession object.</p>

<p>After the VerificationSession is created, display a verification modal using the session <code>client_secret</code> or send your users to the session’s <code>url</code>.</p>

<p>If your API key is in test mode, verification checks won’t actually process, though everything else will occur as if in live mode.</p>

<p>Related guide: <a href="/docs/identity/verify-identity-documents">Verify your users’ identity documents</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
options:
  document:
    allowed_types:
      - driving_license
    require_id_number: true
    require_live_capture: true
    require_matching_selfie: true
return_url: string
type: document
```

This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|

|» » document|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » allowed_types|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » » require_id_number|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » require_live_capture|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » require_matching_selfie|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» return_url|body|string|false|The URL that the user will be redirected to upon completing the verification flow.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of [verification check](https://stripe.com/docs/identity/verification-checks) to be performed.|

#### Enumerated Values
