## PostIdentityVerificationSessionsSessionRedact

<a id="opIdPostIdentityVerificationSessionsSessionRedact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/identity/verification_sessions/string/redact \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/identity/verification_sessions/{session}/redact`

<p>Redact a VerificationSession to remove all collected information from Stripe. This will redact
the VerificationSession and all objects related to it, including VerificationReports, Events,
request logs, etc.</p>

<p>A VerificationSession object can be redacted when it is in <code>requires_input</code> or <code>verified</code>
<a href="/docs/identity/how-sessions-work">status</a>. Redacting a VerificationSession in <code>requires_action</code>
state will automatically cancel it.</p>

<p>The redaction process may take up to four days. When the redaction process is in progress, the
VerificationSession’s <code>redaction.status</code> field will be set to <code>processing</code>; when the process is
finished, it will change to <code>redacted</code> and an <code>identity.verification_session.redacted</code> event
will be emitted.</p>

<p>Redaction is irreversible. Redacted objects are still accessible in the Stripe API, but all the
fields that contain personal data will be replaced by the string <code>[redacted]</code> or a similar
placeholder. The <code>metadata</code> field will also be erased. Redacted objects cannot be updated or
used for any purpose.</p>

<p><a href="/docs/identity/verification-sessions#redact">Learn more</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postidentityverificationsessionssessionredact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## GetInvoiceitems

<a id="opIdGetInvoiceitems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/invoiceitems \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/invoiceitems`

<p>Returns a list of your invoice items. Invoice items are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recently created invoice items appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getinvoiceitems-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|customer|query|string|false|The identifier of the customer whose invoice items to return. If none is provided, all invoice items will be returned.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|invoice|query|string|false|Only return invoice items belonging to this invoice. If none is provided, all invoice items will be returned. If specifying an invoice, no customer identifier is needed.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|pending|query|boolean|false|Set to `true` to only show pending invoice items, which are not yet attached to any invoices. Set to `false` to only show invoice items already attached to invoices. If unspecified, no filter is applied.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

`POST /v1/invoiceitems`

<p>Creates an item to be added to a draft invoice (up to 250 items per invoice). If no invoice is specified, the item will be on the next invoice created for the customer specified.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
customer: string
description: string
discountable: true
discounts:
  -
    coupon: string
    discount: string
expand:
  - string
invoice: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
period:
  end: 0
  start: 0
price: string
price_data:
  currency: string
  product: string
  tax_behavior: exclusive
  unit_amount: 0
  unit_amount_decimal: string
quantity: 0
subscription: string
tax_behavior: exclusive
tax_code: string
tax_rates:
  - string
unit_amount: 0
unit_amount_decimal: string
```

## GetInvoices

<a id="opIdGetInvoices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/invoices \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/invoices`

<p>You can list all invoices, or list the invoices for a specific customer. The invoices are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recently created invoices appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getinvoices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collection_method|query|string|false|The collection method of the invoice to retrieve. Either `charge_automatically` or `send_invoice`.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|customer|query|string|false|Only return invoices for the customer specified by this customer ID.|
|due_date|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|The status of the invoice, one of `draft`, `open`, `paid`, `uncollectible`, or `void`. [Learn more](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/invoices/workflow#workflow-overview)|
|subscription|query|string|false|Only return invoices for the subscription specified by this subscription ID.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

|collection_method|charge_automatically|
|collection_method|send_invoice|
|status|draft|
|status|open|
|status|paid|
|status|uncollectible|
|status|void|

`POST /v1/invoices`

<p>This endpoint creates a draft invoice for a given customer. The invoice remains a draft until you <a href="#finalize_invoice">finalize</a> the invoice, which allows you to <a href="#pay_invoice">pay</a> or <a href="#send_invoice">send</a> the invoice to your customers.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account_tax_ids:
  - string
application_fee_amount: 0
auto_advance: true
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
collection_method: charge_automatically
currency: string
custom_fields:
  -
    name: string
    value: string
customer: string
days_until_due: 0
default_payment_method: string
default_source: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
description: string
discounts:
  -
    coupon: string
    discount: string
due_date: 0
expand:
  - string
footer: string
from_invoice:
  action: revision
  invoice: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
on_behalf_of: string
payment_settings:
  default_mandate: string
  payment_method_options:
    acss_debit:
      mandate_options:
        transaction_type: business
      verification_method: automatic
    bancontact:
      preferred_language: de
    card:
      installments:
        enabled: true
        plan:
          count: 0
          interval: month
          type: fixed_count
      request_three_d_secure: any
    customer_balance:
      bank_transfer:
        eu_bank_transfer:
          country: string
        type: string
      funding_type: string
    konbini: {}
    us_bank_account:
      financial_connections:
        permissions:
          - balances
      verification_method: automatic
  payment_method_types:
    - ach_credit_transfer
pending_invoice_items_behavior: exclude
rendering_options:
  amount_tax_display: ""
shipping_cost:
  shipping_rate: string
  shipping_rate_data:
    delivery_estimate:
      maximum:
        unit: business_day
        value: 0
      minimum:
        unit: business_day
        value: 0
    display_name: string
    fixed_amount:
      amount: 0
      currency: string
      currency_options:
        property1:
          amount: 0
          tax_behavior: exclusive
        property2:
          amount: 0
          tax_behavior: exclusive
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    tax_behavior: exclusive
    tax_code: string
    type: fixed_amount
shipping_details:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  name: string
  phone: string
statement_descriptor: string
subscription: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
  destination: string
```

<h3 id="postinvoices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» account_tax_ids|body|[string] \| string|false|The account tax IDs associated with the invoice. Only editable when the invoice is a draft.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» application_fee_amount|body|integer|false|A fee in cents (or local equivalent) that will be applied to the invoice and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The request must be made with an OAuth key or the Stripe-Account header in order to take an application fee. For more information, see the application fees [documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/invoices/connect#collecting-fees).|
|» auto_advance|body|boolean|false|Controls whether Stripe will perform [automatic collection](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/invoices/workflow/#auto_advance) of the invoice. When `false`, the invoice's state will not automatically advance without an explicit action.|
|» automatic_tax|body|object|false|Settings for automatic tax lookup for this invoice.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» collection_method|body|string|false|Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay this invoice using the default source attached to the customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email this invoice to the customer with payment instructions. Defaults to `charge_automatically`.|
|» currency|body|string|false|The currency to create this invoice in. Defaults to that of `customer` if not specified.|
|» custom_fields|body|[object] \| string|false|A list of up to 4 custom fields to be displayed on the invoice.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[object]|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» value|body|string|true|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» customer|body|string|false|The ID of the customer who will be billed.|
|» days_until_due|body|integer|false|The number of days from when the invoice is created until it is due. Valid only for invoices where `collection_method=send_invoice`.|
|» default_payment_method|body|string|false|ID of the default payment method for the invoice. It must belong to the customer associated with the invoice. If not set, defaults to the subscription's default payment method, if any, or to the default payment method in the customer's invoice settings.|
|» default_source|body|string|false|ID of the default payment source for the invoice. It must belong to the customer associated with the invoice and be in a chargeable state. If not set, defaults to the subscription's default source, if any, or to the customer's default source.|
|» default_tax_rates|body|[string]|false|The tax rates that will apply to any line item that does not have `tax_rates` set.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Referenced as 'memo' in the Dashboard.|
|» discounts|body|[object] \| string|false|The coupons to redeem into discounts for the invoice. If not specified, inherits the discount from the invoice's customer. Pass an empty string to avoid inheriting any discounts.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[object]|false|none|
|» coupon|body|string|false|none|
|» discount|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

## GetInvoicesSearch

<a id="opIdGetInvoicesSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/v1/invoices/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/invoices/search`

<p>Search for invoices you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getinvoicessearch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://stripe.com/docs/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for invoices](https://stripe.com/docs/search#query-fields-for-invoices).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## GetInvoicesUpcoming

<a id="opIdGetInvoicesUpcoming"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/invoices/upcoming \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/invoices/upcoming`

<p>At any time, you can preview the upcoming invoice for a customer. This will show you all the charges that are pending, including subscription renewal charges, invoice item charges, etc. It will also show you any discounts that are applicable to the invoice.</p>

<p>Note that when you are viewing an upcoming invoice, you are simply viewing a preview – the invoice has not yet been created. As such, the upcoming invoice will not show up in invoice listing calls, and you cannot use the API to pay or edit the invoice. If you want to change the amount that your customer will be billed, you can add, remove, or update pending invoice items, or update the customer’s discount.</p>

<p>You can preview the effects of updating a subscription, including a preview of what proration will take place. To ensure that the actual proration is calculated exactly the same as the previewed proration, you should pass a <code>proration_date</code> parameter when doing the actual subscription update. The value passed in should be the same as the <code>subscription_proration_date</code> returned on the upcoming invoice resource. The recommended way to get only the prorations being previewed is to consider only proration line items where <code>period[start]</code> is equal to the <code>subscription_proration_date</code> on the upcoming invoice resource.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getinvoicesupcoming-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|automatic_tax|query|object|false|Settings for automatic tax lookup for this invoice preview.|
|coupon|query|string|false|The code of the coupon to apply. If `subscription` or `subscription_items` is provided, the invoice returned will preview updating or creating a subscription with that coupon. Otherwise, it will preview applying that coupon to the customer for the next upcoming invoice from among the customer's subscriptions. The invoice can be previewed without a coupon by passing this value as an empty string.|
|currency|query|string|false|The currency to preview this invoice in. Defaults to that of `customer` if not specified.|
|customer|query|string|false|The identifier of the customer whose upcoming invoice you'd like to retrieve.|
|customer_details|query|object|false|Details about the customer you want to invoice or overrides for an existing customer.|
|discounts|query|[object] \| string|false|The coupons to redeem into discounts for the invoice preview. If not specified, inherits the discount from the customer or subscription. This only works for coupons directly applied to the invoice. To apply a coupon to a subscription, you must use the `coupon` parameter instead. Pass an empty string to avoid inheriting any discounts. To preview the upcoming invoice for a subscription that hasn't been created, use `coupon` instead.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|invoice_items|query|[object]|false|List of invoice items to add or update in the upcoming invoice preview.|
|schedule|query|string|false|The identifier of the unstarted schedule whose upcoming invoice you'd like to retrieve. Cannot be used with subscription or subscription fields.|
|subscription|query|string|false|The identifier of the subscription for which you'd like to retrieve the upcoming invoice. If not provided, but a `subscription_items` is provided, you will preview creating a subscription with those items. If neither `subscription` nor `subscription_items` is provided, you will retrieve the next upcoming invoice from among the customer's subscriptions.|
|subscription_billing_cycle_anchor|query|string \| integer(unix-time)|false|For new subscriptions, a future timestamp to anchor the subscription's [billing cycle](https://stripe.com/docs/subscriptions/billing-cycle). This is used to determine the date of the first full invoice, and, for plans with `month` or `year` intervals, the day of the month for subsequent invoices. For existing subscriptions, the value can only be set to `now` or `unchanged`.|
|subscription_cancel_at|query|integer(unix-time) \| string|false|Timestamp indicating when the subscription should be scheduled to cancel. Will prorate if within the current period and prorations have been enabled using `proration_behavior`.|
|subscription_cancel_at_period_end|query|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether this subscription should cancel at the end of the current period.|
|subscription_cancel_now|query|boolean|false|This simulates the subscription being canceled or expired immediately.|
|subscription_default_tax_rates|query|[string] \| string|false|If provided, the invoice returned will preview updating or creating a subscription with these default tax rates. The default tax rates will apply to any line item that does not have `tax_rates` set.|
|subscription_items|query|[object]|false|A list of up to 20 subscription items, each with an attached price.|
|subscription_proration_behavior|query|string|false|Determines how to handle [prorations](https://stripe.com/docs/subscriptions/billing-cycle#prorations) when the billing cycle changes (e.g., when switching plans, resetting `billing_cycle_anchor=now`, or starting a trial), or if an item's `quantity` changes. The default value is `create_prorations`.|
|subscription_proration_date|query|integer(unix-time)|false|If previewing an update to a subscription, and doing proration, `subscription_proration_date` forces the proration to be calculated as though the update was done at the specified time. The time given must be within the current subscription period and within the current phase of the schedule backing this subscription, if the schedule exists. If set, `subscription`, and one of `subscription_items`, or `subscription_trial_end` are required. Also, `subscription_proration_behavior` cannot be set to 'none'.|
|subscription_resume_at|query|string|false|For paused subscriptions, setting `subscription_resume_at` to `now` will preview the invoice that will be generated if the subscription is resumed.|
|subscription_start_date|query|integer(unix-time)|false|Date a subscription is intended to start (can be future or past)|
|subscription_trial_end|query|string \| integer(unix-time)|false|If provided, the invoice returned will preview updating or creating a subscription with that trial end. If set, one of `subscription_items` or `subscription` is required.|
|subscription_trial_from_plan|query|boolean|false|Indicates if a plan's `trial_period_days` should be applied to the subscription. Setting `subscription_trial_end` per subscription is preferred, and this defaults to `false`. Setting this flag to `true` together with `subscription_trial_end` is not allowed. See [Using trial periods on subscriptions](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/trials) to learn more.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|subscription_proration_behavior|always_invoice|
|subscription_proration_behavior|create_prorations|
|subscription_proration_behavior|none|
|subscription_resume_at|now|

`GET /v1/invoices/upcoming/lines`

<p>When retrieving an upcoming invoice, you’ll get a <strong>lines</strong> property containing the total count of line items and the first handful of those items. There is also a URL where you can retrieve the full (paginated) list of line items.</p>

<a id="opIdPostInvoicesInvoice"></a>

curl https://example.com/v1/invoices/string \

'account_tax_ids=%5B%22string%22%5D&application_fee_amount=0&auto_advance=true&automatic_tax=%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D&collection_method=charge_automatically&custom_fields=%5B%7B%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22value%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D&days_until_due=0&default_payment_method=string&default_source=string&default_tax_rates=%5B%22string%22%5D&description=string&discounts=%5B%7B%22coupon%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22discount%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D&due_date=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&footer=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&on_behalf_of=string&payment_settings=%7B%22default_mandate%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22payment_method_options%22%3A%7B%22acss_debit%22%3A%7B%22mandate_options%22%3A%7B%22transaction_type%22%3A%22business%22%7D%2C%22verification_method%22%3A%22automatic%22%7D%2C%22bancontact%22%3A%7B%22preferred_language%22%3A%22de%22%7D%2C%22card%22%3A%7B%22installments%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22plan%22%3A%7B%22count%22%3A0%2C%22interval%22%3A%22month%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22fixed_count%22%7D%7D%2C%22request_three_d_secure%22%3A%22any%22%7D%2C%22customer_balance%22%3A%7B%22bank_transfer%22%3A%7B%22eu_bank_transfer%22%3A%7B%22country%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22type%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22funding_type%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22konbini%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22us_bank_account%22%3A%7B%22financial_connections%22%3A%7B%22permissions%22%3A%5B%22balances%22%5D%7D%2C%22verification_method%22%3A%22automatic%22%7D%7D%2C%22payment_method_types%22%3A%5B%22ach_credit_transfer%22%5D%7D&rendering_options=%7B%22amount_tax_display%22%3A%22%22%7D&shipping_cost=%7B%22shipping_rate%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22shipping_rate_data%22%3A%7B%22delivery_estimate%22%3A%7B%22maximum%22%3A%7B%22unit%22%3A%22business_day%22%2C%22value%22%3A0%7D%2C%22minimum%22%3A%7B%22unit%22%3A%22business_day%22%2C%22value%22%3A0%7D%7D%2C%22display_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22fixed_amount%22%3A%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22currency_options%22%3A% ```

`POST /v1/invoices/{invoice}`

<p>Draft invoices are fully editable. Once an invoice is <a href="/docs/billing/invoices/workflow#finalized">finalized</a>,
monetary values, as well as <code>collection_method</code>, become uneditable.</p>

<p>If you would like to stop the Stripe Billing engine from automatically finalizing, reattempting payments on,
sending reminders for, or <a href="/docs/billing/invoices/reconciliation">automatically reconciling</a> invoices, pass
<code>auto_advance=false</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
account_tax_ids:
  - string
application_fee_amount: 0
auto_advance: true
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
collection_method: charge_automatically
custom_fields:
  -
    name: string
    value: string
days_until_due: 0
default_payment_method: string
default_source: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
description: string
discounts:
  -
    coupon: string
    discount: string
due_date: 0
expand:
  - string
footer: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
on_behalf_of: string
payment_settings:
  default_mandate: string
  payment_method_options:
    acss_debit:
      mandate_options:
        transaction_type: business
      verification_method: automatic
    bancontact:
      preferred_language: de
    card:
      installments:
        enabled: true
        plan:
          count: 0
          interval: month
          type: fixed_count
      request_three_d_secure: any
    customer_balance:
      bank_transfer:
        eu_bank_transfer:
          country: string
        type: string
      funding_type: string
    konbini: {}
    us_bank_account:
      financial_connections:
        permissions:
          - balances
      verification_method: automatic
  payment_method_types:
    - ach_credit_transfer
rendering_options:
  amount_tax_display: ""
shipping_cost:
  shipping_rate: string
  shipping_rate_data:
    delivery_estimate:
      maximum:
        unit: business_day
        value: 0
      minimum:
        unit: business_day
        value: 0
    display_name: string
    fixed_amount:
      amount: 0
      currency: string
      currency_options:
        property1:
          amount: 0
          tax_behavior: exclusive
        property2:
          amount: 0
          tax_behavior: exclusive
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    tax_behavior: exclusive
    tax_code: string
    type: fixed_amount
shipping_details:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  name: string
  phone: string
statement_descriptor: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
  destination: string
```

## DeleteInvoicesInvoice

<a id="opIdDeleteInvoicesInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/invoices/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /v1/invoices/{invoice}`

<p>Permanently deletes a one-off invoice draft. This cannot be undone. Attempts to delete invoices that are no longer in a draft state will fail; once an invoice has been finalized or if an invoice is for a subscription, it must be <a href="#void_invoice">voided</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="deleteinvoicesinvoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|invoice|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "deleted": true,
  "id": "string",
  "object": "invoice"
}
```

## PostInvoicesInvoiceFinalize

<a id="opIdPostInvoicesInvoiceFinalize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/invoices/string/finalize \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'auto_advance=true&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/invoices/{invoice}/finalize`

<p>Stripe automatically finalizes drafts before sending and attempting payment on invoices. However, if you’d like to finalize a draft invoice manually, you can do so using this method.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
auto_advance: true
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postinvoicesinvoicefinalize-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|invoice|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» auto_advance|body|boolean|false|Controls whether Stripe will perform [automatic collection](https://stripe.com/docs/invoicing/automatic-charging) of the invoice. When `false`, the invoice's state will not automatically advance without an explicit action.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## GetInvoicesInvoiceLines

<a id="opIdGetInvoicesInvoiceLines"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/invoices/string/lines \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/invoices/{invoice}/lines`

<p>When retrieving an invoice, you’ll get a <strong>lines</strong> property containing the total count of line items and the first handful of those items. There is also a URL where you can retrieve the full (paginated) list of line items.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getinvoicesinvoicelines-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|invoice|path|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## PostInvoicesInvoicePay

<a id="opIdPostInvoicesInvoicePay"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/invoices/string/pay \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&forgive=true&mandate=string&off_session=true&paid_out_of_band=true&payment_method=string&source=string'
```

`POST /v1/invoices/{invoice}/pay`

<p>Stripe automatically creates and then attempts to collect payment on invoices for customers on subscriptions according to your <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/billing/automatic">subscriptions settings</a>. However, if you’d like to attempt payment on an invoice out of the normal collection schedule or for some other reason, you can do so.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
forgive: true
mandate: string
off_session: true
paid_out_of_band: true
payment_method: string
source: string
```

<h3 id="postinvoicesinvoicepay-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|invoice|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» forgive|body|boolean|false|In cases where the source used to pay the invoice has insufficient funds, passing `forgive=true` controls whether a charge should be attempted for the full amount available on the source, up to the amount to fully pay the invoice. This effectively forgives the difference between the amount available on the source and the amount due. <br><br>Passing `forgive=false` will fail the charge if the source hasn't been pre-funded with the right amount. An example for this case is with ACH Credit Transfers and wires: if the amount wired is less than the amount due by a small amount, you might want to forgive the difference. Defaults to `false`.|
|» mandate|body|string|false|ID of the mandate to be used for this invoice. It must correspond to the payment method used to pay the invoice, including the payment_method param or the invoice's default_payment_method or default_source, if set.|
|» off_session|body|boolean|false|Indicates if a customer is on or off-session while an invoice payment is attempted. Defaults to `true` (off-session).|
|» paid_out_of_band|body|boolean|false|Boolean representing whether an invoice is paid outside of Stripe. This will result in no charge being made. Defaults to `false`.|
|» payment_method|body|string|false|A PaymentMethod to be charged. The PaymentMethod must be the ID of a PaymentMethod belonging to the customer associated with the invoice being paid.|
|» source|body|string|false|A payment source to be charged. The source must be the ID of a source belonging to the customer associated with the invoice being paid.|

## PostInvoicesInvoiceSend

<a id="opIdPostInvoicesInvoiceSend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/invoices/string/send \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/invoices/{invoice}/send`

<p>Stripe will automatically send invoices to customers according to your <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/billing/automatic">subscriptions settings</a>. However, if you’d like to manually send an invoice to your customer out of the normal schedule, you can do so. When sending invoices that have already been paid, there will be no reference to the payment in the email.</p>

<p>Requests made in test-mode result in no emails being sent, despite sending an <code>invoice.sent</code> event.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|false|none|

## PostInvoicesInvoiceVoid

<a id="opIdPostInvoicesInvoiceVoid"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/invoices/string/void \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/invoices/{invoice}/void`

<p>Mark a finalized invoice as void. This cannot be undone. Voiding an invoice is similar to <a href="#delete_invoice">deletion</a>, however it only applies to finalized invoices and maintains a papertrail where the invoice can still be found.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postinvoicesinvoicevoid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|invoice|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## GetIssuingAuthorizations

<a id="opIdGetIssuingAuthorizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/issuing/authorizations \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/issuing/authorizations`

<p>Returns a list of Issuing <code>Authorization</code> objects. The objects are sorted in descending order by creation date, with the most recently created object appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getissuingauthorizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card|query|string|false|Only return authorizations that belong to the given card.|
|cardholder|query|string|false|Only return authorizations that belong to the given cardholder.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return authorizations that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|Only return authorizations with the given status. One of `pending`, `closed`, or `reversed`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|closed|
|status|pending|
|status|reversed|

## GetIssuingCardholders

<a id="opIdGetIssuingCardholders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/issuing/cardholders \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/issuing/cardholders`

<p>Returns a list of Issuing <code>Cardholder</code> objects. The objects are sorted in descending order by creation date, with the most recently created object appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getissuingcardholders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return cardholders that were created during the given date interval.|
|email|query|string|false|Only return cardholders that have the given email address.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|phone_number|query|string|false|Only return cardholders that have the given phone number.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|Only return cardholders that have the given status. One of `active`, `inactive`, or `blocked`.|
|type|query|string|false|Only return cardholders that have the given type. One of `individual` or `company`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|status|active|
|status|blocked|
|status|inactive|
|type|company|
|type|individual|

```

`POST /v1/issuing/cardholders`

<p>Creates a new Issuing <code>Cardholder</code> object that can be issued cards.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
billing:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
company:
  tax_id: string
email: string
expand:
  - string
individual:
  dob:
    day: 0
    month: 0
    year: 0
  first_name: string
  last_name: string
  verification:
    document:
      back: string
      front: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
name: string
phone_number: string
spending_controls:
  allowed_categories:
    - ac_refrigeration_repair
  blocked_categories:
    - ac_refrigeration_repair
  spending_limits:
    -
      amount: 0
      categories:
        - ac_refrigeration_repair
      interval: all_time
  spending_limits_currency: string
status: active
type: company
```

|» » » city|body|string|true|none|

|» » » postal_code|body|string|true|none|
|» » » state|body|string|false|none|
|» company|body|object|false|Additional information about a `company` cardholder.|
|» » tax_id|body|string|false|none|
|» email|body|string|false|The cardholder's email address.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» individual|body|object|false|Additional information about an `individual` cardholder.|
|» » dob|body|object|false|none|
|» » » day|body|integer|true|none|
|» » » month|body|integer|true|none|
|» » » year|body|integer|true|none|
|» » first_name|body|string|false|none|
|» » last_name|body|string|false|none|
|» » verification|body|object|false|none|
|» » » document|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » back|body|string|false|none|

## PostIssuingCardholdersCardholder

<a id="opIdPostIssuingCardholdersCardholder"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/issuing/cardholders/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'billing=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D&company=%7B%22tax_id%22%3A%22string%22%7D&email=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&individual=%7B%22dob%22%3A%7B%22day%22%3A0%2C%22month%22%3A0%2C%22year%22%3A0%7D%2C%22first_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22last_name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22verification%22%3A%7B%22document%22%3A%7B%22back%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22front%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&phone_number=string&spending_controls=%7B%22allowed_categories%22%3A%5B%22ac_refrigeration_repair%22%5D%2C%22blocked_categories%22%3A%5B%22ac_refrigeration_repair%22%5D%2C%22spending_limits%22%3A%5B%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22categories%22%3A%5B%22ac_refrigeration_repair%22%5D%2C%22interval%22%3A%22all_time%22%7D%5D%2C%22spending_limits_currency%22%3A%22string%22%7D&status=active'
```

`POST /v1/issuing/cardholders/{cardholder}`

<p>Updates the specified Issuing <code>Cardholder</code> object by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided will be left unchanged.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
billing:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
company:
  tax_id: string
email: string
expand:
  - string
individual:
  dob:
    day: 0
    month: 0
    year: 0
  first_name: string
  last_name: string
  verification:
    document:
      back: string
      front: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
phone_number: string
spending_controls:
  allowed_categories:
    - ac_refrigeration_repair
  blocked_categories:
    - ac_refrigeration_repair
  spending_limits:
    -
      amount: 0
      categories:
        - ac_refrigeration_repair
      interval: all_time
  spending_limits_currency: string
status: active
```

## GetIssuingCards

<a id="opIdGetIssuingCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/issuing/cards \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/issuing/cards`

<p>Returns a list of Issuing <code>Card</code> objects. The objects are sorted in descending order by creation date, with the most recently created object appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getissuingcards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cardholder|query|string|false|Only return cards belonging to the Cardholder with the provided ID.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return cards that were issued during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|exp_month|query|integer|false|Only return cards that have the given expiration month.|
|exp_year|query|integer|false|Only return cards that have the given expiration year.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|last4|query|string|false|Only return cards that have the given last four digits.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|Only return cards that have the given status. One of `active`, `inactive`, or `canceled`.|
|type|query|string|false|Only return cards that have the given type. One of `virtual` or `physical`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|canceled|
|status|inactive|
|type|physical|
|type|virtual|

## PostIssuingCards

<a id="opIdPostIssuingCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/issuing/cards \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'cardholder=string&currency=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&financial_account=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&replacement_for=string&replacement_reason=damaged&shipping=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22customs%22%3A%7B%22eori_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22require_signature%22%3Atrue%2C%22service%22%3A%22express%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22bulk%22%7D&spending_controls=%7B%22allowed_categories%22%3A%5B%22ac_refrigeration_repair%22%5D%2C%22blocked_categories%22%3A%5B%22ac_refrigeration_repair%22%5D%2C%22spending_limits%22%3A%5B%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22categories%22%3A%5B%22ac_refrigeration_repair%22%5D%2C%22interval%22%3A%22all_time%22%7D%5D%7D&status=active&type=physical'
```

`POST /v1/issuing/cards`

<p>Creates an Issuing <code>Card</code> object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
cardholder: string
currency: string
expand:
  - string
financial_account: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
replacement_for: string
replacement_reason: damaged
shipping:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  customs:
    eori_number: string
  name: string
  phone_number: string
  require_signature: true
  service: express
  type: bulk
spending_controls:
  allowed_categories:
    - ac_refrigeration_repair
  blocked_categories:
    - ac_refrigeration_repair
  spending_limits:
    -
      amount: 0
      categories:
        - ac_refrigeration_repair
      interval: all_time
status: active
type: physical
```

<h3 id="postissuingcards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» cardholder|body|string|false|The [Cardholder](https://stripe.com/docs/api#issuing_cardholder_object) object with which the card will be associated.|

## PostIssuingCardsCard

<a id="opIdPostIssuingCardsCard"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/issuing/cards/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'cancellation_reason=lost&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&pin=%7B%22encrypted_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&spending_controls=%7B%22allowed_categories%22%3A%5B%22ac_refrigeration_repair%22%5D%2C%22blocked_categories%22%3A%5B%22ac_refrigeration_repair%22%5D%2C%22spending_limits%22%3A%5B%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22categories%22%3A%5B%22ac_refrigeration_repair%22%5D%2C%22interval%22%3A%22all_time%22%7D%5D%7D&status=active'
```

`POST /v1/issuing/cards/{card}`

<p>Updates the specified Issuing <code>Card</code> object by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided will be left unchanged.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
cancellation_reason: lost
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
pin:
  encrypted_number: string
spending_controls:
  allowed_categories:
    - ac_refrigeration_repair
  blocked_categories:
    - ac_refrigeration_repair
  spending_limits:
    -
      amount: 0
      categories:
        - ac_refrigeration_repair
      interval: all_time
status: active
```

<h3 id="postissuingcardscard-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» cancellation_reason|body|string|false|Reason why the `status` of this card is `canceled`.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» pin|body|object|false|The desired new PIN for this card.|
|» » encrypted_number|body|string|false|none|
|» spending_controls|body|object|false|Rules that control spending for this card. Refer to our [documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/issuing/controls/spending-controls) for more details.|
|» » allowed_categories|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » blocked_categories|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » spending_limits|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » amount|body|integer|true|none|
|» » » categories|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » » interval|body|string|true|none|
|» status|body|string|false|Dictates whether authorizations can be approved on this card. May be blocked from activating cards depending on past-due Cardholder requirements. Defaults to `inactive`. If this card is being canceled because it was lost or stolen, this information should be provided as `cancellation_reason`.|

## GetIssuingDisputes

<a id="opIdGetIssuingDisputes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/issuing/disputes \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/issuing/disputes`

<p>Returns a list of Issuing <code>Dispute</code> objects. The objects are sorted in descending order by creation date, with the most recently created object appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getissuingdisputes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Select Issuing disputes that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|Select Issuing disputes with the given status.|
|transaction|query|string|false|Select the Issuing dispute for the given transaction.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|expired|
|status|lost|
|status|submitted|
|status|unsubmitted|
|status|won|

## PostIssuingDisputes

<a id="opIdPostIssuingDisputes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/issuing/disputes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \

`POST /v1/issuing/disputes`

<p>Creates an Issuing <code>Dispute</code> object. Individual pieces of evidence within the <code>evidence</code> object are optional at this point. Stripe only validates that required evidence is present during submission. Refer to <a href="/docs/issuing/purchases/disputes#dispute-reasons-and-evidence">Dispute reasons and evidence</a> for more details about evidence requirements.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
evidence:
  canceled:
    additional_documentation: string
    canceled_at: 0
    cancellation_policy_provided: true
    cancellation_reason: string
    expected_at: 0
    explanation: string
    product_description: string
    product_type: ""
    return_status: ""
    returned_at: 0
  duplicate:
    additional_documentation: string
    card_statement: string
    cash_receipt: string
    check_image: string
    explanation: string
    original_transaction: string
  fraudulent:
    additional_documentation: string
    explanation: string
  merchandise_not_as_described:
    additional_documentation: string
    explanation: string
    received_at: 0
    return_description: string
    return_status: ""
    returned_at: 0
  not_received:
    additional_documentation: string
    expected_at: 0
    explanation: string
    product_description: string
    product_type: ""
  other:
    additional_documentation: string
    explanation: string
    product_description: string
    product_type: ""
  reason: canceled
  service_not_as_described:
    additional_documentation: string
    canceled_at: 0
    cancellation_reason: string
    explanation: string
    received_at: 0
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
transaction: string
treasury:
  received_debit: string

## GetIssuingSettlements

<a id="opIdGetIssuingSettlements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/issuing/settlements \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/issuing/settlements`

<p>Returns a list of Issuing <code>Settlement</code> objects. The objects are sorted in descending order by creation date, with the most recently created object appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getissuingsettlements-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return issuing settlements that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return transactions that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|type|query|string|false|Only return transactions that have the given type. One of `capture` or `refund`.|

```

`GET /v1/linked_accounts`

<p>Returns a list of Financial Connections <code>Account</code> objects.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getlinkedaccounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_holder|query|object|false|If present, only return accounts that belong to the specified account holder. `account_holder[customer]` and `account_holder[account]` are mutually exclusive.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|

<h3 id="getpaymentintents-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="getpaymentintents-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)]|true|none|none|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|list|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

`POST /v1/payment_intents`

<p>Creates a PaymentIntent object.</p>

<p>After the PaymentIntent is created, attach a payment method and <a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/confirm">confirm</a>
to continue the payment. You can read more about the different payment flows
available via the Payment Intents API <a href="/docs/payments/payment-intents">here</a>.</p>

<p>When <code>confirm=true</code> is used during creation, it is equivalent to creating
and confirming the PaymentIntent in the same call. You may use any parameters
available in the <a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/confirm">confirm API</a> when <code>confirm=true</code>
is supplied.</p>

|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount intended to be collected by this PaymentIntent. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).|
|» application_fee_amount|body|integer|false|The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The amount of the application fee collected will be capped at the total payment amount. For more information, see the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/connected-accounts).|

|» transfer_data|body|object|false|The parameters used to automatically create a Transfer when the payment succeeds.<br>For more information, see the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/connected-accounts).|
|» » amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » destination|body|string|true|none|
|» transfer_group|body|string|false|A string that identifies the resulting payment as part of a group. See the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/connected-accounts) for details.|
|» use_stripe_sdk|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` only when using manual confirmation and the iOS or Android SDKs to handle additional authentication steps.|

## GetPaymentIntentsSearch

<a id="opIdGetPaymentIntentsSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/v1/payment_intents/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_intents/search`

<p>Search for PaymentIntents you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getpaymentintentssearch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://stripe.com/docs/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for payment intents](https://stripe.com/docs/search#query-fields-for-payment-intents).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## GetPaymentIntentsIntent

<a id="opIdGetPaymentIntentsIntent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_intents/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_intents/{intent}`

<p>Retrieves the details of a PaymentIntent that has previously been created. </p>

<p>Client-side retrieval using a publishable key is allowed when the <code>client_secret</code> is provided in the query string. </p>

<p>When retrieved with a publishable key, only a subset of properties will be returned. Please refer to the <a href="#payment_intent_object">payment intent</a> object reference for more details.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getpaymentintentsintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_secret|query|string|false|The client secret of the PaymentIntent. Required if a publishable key is used to retrieve the source.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}`

<p>Updates properties on a PaymentIntent object without confirming.</p>

<p>Depending on which properties you update, you may need to confirm the
PaymentIntent again. For example, updating the <code>payment_method</code> will
always require you to confirm the PaymentIntent again. If you prefer to
update and confirm at the same time, we recommend updating properties via
the <a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/confirm">confirm API</a> instead.</p>

<h3 id="postpaymentintentsintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Amount intended to be collected by this PaymentIntent. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).|
|» application_fee_amount|body|integer \| string|false|The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The amount of the application fee collected will be capped at the total payment amount. For more information, see the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/connected-accounts).|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

|» currency|body|string|false|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» customer|body|string|false|ID of the Customer this PaymentIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this PaymentIntent.<br><br>If present in combination with [setup_future_usage](https://stripe.com/docs/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage), this PaymentIntent's payment method will be attached to the Customer after the PaymentIntent has been confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|

If no Customer was provided, the payment method can still be [attached](https://stripe.com/docs/api/payment_methods/attach) to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe also uses `setup_future_usage` to dynamically optimize your payment flow and comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](https://stripe.com/docs/strong-customer-authentication).<br><br>If `setup_future_usage` is already set and you are performing a request using a publishable key, you may only update the value from `on_session` to `off_session`.|

## PostPaymentIntentsIntentApplyCustomerBalance

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentApplyCustomerBalance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_intents/string/apply_customer_balance \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/apply_customer_balance`

<p>Manually reconcile the remaining amount for a customer_balance PaymentIntent.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postpaymentintentsintentapplycustomerbalance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Amount intended to be applied to this PaymentIntent from the customer’s cash balance.<br><br>A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency).<br><br>The maximum amount is the amount of the PaymentIntent.<br><br>When omitted, the amount defaults to the remaining amount requested on the PaymentIntent.|
|» currency|body|string|false|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## PostPaymentIntentsIntentCancel

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_intents/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'cancellation_reason=abandoned&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/cancel`

<p>A PaymentIntent object can be canceled when it is in one of these statuses: <code>requires_payment_method</code>, <code>requires_capture</code>, <code>requires_confirmation</code>, <code>requires_action</code> or, <a href="/docs/payments/intents">in rare cases</a>, <code>processing</code>. </p>

<p>Once canceled, no additional charges will be made by the PaymentIntent and any operations on the PaymentIntent will fail with an error. For PaymentIntents with <code>status=’requires_capture’</code>, the remaining <code>amount_capturable</code> will automatically be refunded. </p>

<p>You cannot cancel the PaymentIntent for a Checkout Session. <a href="/docs/api/checkout/sessions/expire">Expire the Checkout Session</a> instead.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
cancellation_reason: abandoned
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postpaymentintentsintentcancel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» cancellation_reason|body|string|false|Reason for canceling this PaymentIntent. Possible values are `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `requested_by_customer`, or `abandoned`|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cancellation_reason|abandoned|
|» cancellation_reason|duplicate|
|» cancellation_reason|fraudulent|
|» cancellation_reason|requested_by_customer|

## PostPaymentIntentsIntentCapture

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentCapture"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_intents/string/capture \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount_to_capture=0&application_fee_amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&statement_descriptor=string&statement_descriptor_suffix=string&transfer_data=%7B%22amount%22%3A0%7D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/capture`

<p>Capture the funds of an existing uncaptured PaymentIntent when its status is <code>requires_capture</code>.</p>

<p>Uncaptured PaymentIntents will be canceled a set number of days after they are created (7 by default).</p>

<p>Learn more about <a href="/docs/payments/capture-later">separate authorization and capture</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount_to_capture: 0
application_fee_amount: 0
expand:
  - string
statement_descriptor: string
statement_descriptor_suffix: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
```

<h3 id="postpaymentintentsintentcapture-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount_to_capture|body|integer|false|The amount to capture from the PaymentIntent, which must be less than or equal to the original amount. Any additional amount will be automatically refunded. Defaults to the full `amount_capturable` if not provided.|
|» application_fee_amount|body|integer|false|The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The amount of the application fee collected will be capped at the total payment amount. For more information, see the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/connected-accounts).|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|For non-card charges, you can use this value as the complete description that appears on your customers’ statements. Must contain at least one letter, maximum 22 characters.|
|» statement_descriptor_suffix|body|string|false|Provides information about a card payment that customers see on their statements. Concatenated with the prefix (shortened descriptor) or statement descriptor that’s set on the account to form the complete statement descriptor. Maximum 22 characters for the concatenated descriptor.|
|» transfer_data|body|object|false|The parameters used to automatically create a Transfer when the payment<br>is captured. For more information, see the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/connected-accounts).|
|» » amount|body|integer|false|none|

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/confirm`

<p>Confirm that your customer intends to pay with current or provided
payment method. Upon confirmation, the PaymentIntent will attempt to initiate
a payment.
If the selected payment method requires additional authentication steps, the
PaymentIntent will transition to the <code>requires_action</code> status and
suggest additional actions via <code>next_action</code>. If payment fails,
the PaymentIntent will transition to the <code>requires_payment_method</code> status. If
payment succeeds, the PaymentIntent will transition to the <code>succeeded</code>
status (or <code>requires_capture</code>, if <code>capture_method</code> is set to <code>manual</code>).
If the <code>confirmation_method</code> is <code>automatic</code>, payment may be attempted
using our <a href="/docs/stripe-js/reference#stripe-handle-card-payment">client SDKs</a>
and the PaymentIntent’s <a href="#payment_intent_object-client_secret">client_secret</a>.
After <code>next_action</code>s are handled by the client, no additional
confirmation is required to complete the payment.
If the <code>confirmation_method</code> is <code>manual</code>, all payment attempts must be
initiated using a secret key.
If any actions are required for the payment, the PaymentIntent will
return to the <code>requires_confirmation</code> state
after those actions are completed. Your server needs to then
explicitly re-confirm the PaymentIntent to initiate the next payment
attempt. Read the <a href="/docs/payments/payment-intents/web-manual">expanded documentation</a>
to learn more about manual confirmation.</p>
