<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, bearerAuth
</aside>

## PostPaymentIntentsIntentIncrementAuthorization

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentIncrementAuthorization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_intents/string/increment_authorization \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&application_fee_amount=0&description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&statement_descriptor=string&transfer_data=%7B%22amount%22%3A0%7D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/increment_authorization`

<p>Perform an incremental authorization on an eligible
<a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/object">PaymentIntent</a>. To be eligible, the
PaymentIntent’s status must be <code>requires_capture</code> and
<a href="/docs/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-incremental_authorization_supported">incremental_authorization_supported</a>
must be <code>true</code>.</p>

<p>Incremental authorizations attempt to increase the authorized amount on
your customer’s card to the new, higher <code>amount</code> provided. As with the
initial authorization, incremental authorizations may be declined. A
single PaymentIntent can call this endpoint multiple times to further
increase the authorized amount.</p>

<p>If the incremental authorization succeeds, the PaymentIntent object is
returned with the updated
<a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/object#payment_intent_object-amount">amount</a>.
If the incremental authorization fails, a
<a href="/docs/error-codes#card-declined">card_declined</a> error is returned, and no
fields on the PaymentIntent or Charge are updated. The PaymentIntent
object remains capturable for the previously authorized amount.</p>

<p>Each PaymentIntent can have a maximum of 10 incremental authorization attempts, including declines.
Once captured, a PaymentIntent can no longer be incremented.</p>

<p>Learn more about <a href="/docs/terminal/features/incremental-authorizations">incremental authorizations</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
application_fee_amount: 0
description: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
statement_descriptor: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
```

<h3 id="postpaymentintentsintentincrementauthorization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|The updated total amount you intend to collect from the cardholder. This amount must be greater than the currently authorized amount.|
|» application_fee_amount|body|integer|false|The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The amount of the application fee collected will be capped at the total payment amount. For more information, see the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/connected-accounts).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|For non-card charges, you can use this value as the complete description that appears on your customers’ statements. Must contain at least one letter, maximum 22 characters.|
|» transfer_data|body|object|false|The parameters used to automatically create a Transfer when the payment is captured.<br>For more information, see the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/connected-accounts).|
|» » amount|body|integer|false|none|

## PostPaymentIntentsIntentVerifyMicrodeposits

<a id="opIdPostPaymentIntentsIntentVerifyMicrodeposits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_intents/string/verify_microdeposits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amounts=%5B0%5D&client_secret=string&descriptor_code=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_intents/{intent}/verify_microdeposits`

<p>Verifies microdeposits on a PaymentIntent object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amounts:
  - 0
client_secret: string
descriptor_code: string
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postpaymentintentsintentverifymicrodeposits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amounts|body|[integer]|false|Two positive integers, in *cents*, equal to the values of the microdeposits sent to the bank account.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The client secret of the PaymentIntent.|
|» descriptor_code|body|string|false|A six-character code starting with SM present in the microdeposit sent to the bank account.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|

|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|

## PostPaymentLinksPaymentLink

<a id="opIdPostPaymentLinksPaymentLink"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_links/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'active=true&after_completion=%7B%22hosted_confirmation%22%3A%7B%22custom_message%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22redirect%22%3A%7B%22url%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22type%22%3A%22hosted_confirmation%22%7D&allow_promotion_codes=true&automatic_tax=%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D&billing_address_collection=auto&custom_fields=%5B%7B%22dropdown%22%3A%7B%22options%22%3A%5B%7B%22label%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22value%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%7D%2C%22key%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22label%22%3A%7B%22custom%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22custom%22%7D%2C%22optional%22%3Atrue%2C%22type%22%3A%22dropdown%22%7D%5D&custom_text=%7B%22shipping_address%22%3A%7B%22message%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22submit%22%3A%7B%22message%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D&customer_creation=always&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&invoice_creation=%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22invoice_data%22%3A%7B%22account_tax_ids%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%2C%22custom_fields%22%3A%5B%7B%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22value%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D%2C%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22footer%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22rendering_options%22%3A%7B%22amount_tax_display%22%3A%22%22%7D%7D%7D&line_items=%5B%7B%22adjustable_quantity%22%3A%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22maximum%22%3A0%2C%22minimum%22%3A0%7D%2C%22id%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%7D%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&payment_method_collection=always&payment_method_types=%5B%22affirm%22%5D&shipping_address_collection=%7B%22allowed_countries%22%3A%5B%22AC%22%5D%7D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_links/{payment_link}`

<p>Updates a payment link.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
after_completion:
  hosted_confirmation:
    custom_message: string
  redirect:
    url: string
  type: hosted_confirmation
allow_promotion_codes: true
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
billing_address_collection: auto
custom_fields:
  -
    dropdown:
      options:
        -
          label: string
          value: string
    key: string
    label:
      custom: string
      type: custom
    optional: true
    type: dropdown
custom_text:
  shipping_address:
    message: string
  submit:
    message: string
customer_creation: always
expand:
  - string
invoice_creation:
  enabled: true
  invoice_data:
    account_tax_ids:
      - string
    custom_fields:
      -
        name: string
        value: string
    description: string
    footer: string
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    rendering_options:
      amount_tax_display: ""
line_items:
  -
    adjustable_quantity:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
    id: string
    quantity: 0
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
payment_method_collection: always
payment_method_types:
  - affirm
shipping_address_collection:
  allowed_countries:
    - AC
```

<h3 id="postpaymentlinkspaymentlink-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Whether the payment link's `url` is active. If `false`, customers visiting the URL will be shown a page saying that the link has been deactivated.|
|» after_completion|body|object|false|Behavior after the purchase is complete.|
|» » hosted_confirmation|body|object|false|none|

|» automatic_tax|body|object|false|Configuration for automatic tax collection.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» billing_address_collection|body|string|false|Configuration for collecting the customer's billing address.|
|» custom_fields|body|[object] \| string|false|Collect additional information from your customer using custom fields. Up to 2 fields are supported.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[object]|false|none|
|» dropdown|body|object|false|none|

|» » shipping_address|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

## GetPaymentLinksPaymentLinkLineItems

<a id="opIdGetPaymentLinksPaymentLinkLineItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_links/string/line_items \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_links/{payment_link}/line_items`

<p>When retrieving a payment link, there is an includable <strong>line_items</strong> property containing the first handful of those items. There is also a URL where you can retrieve the full (paginated) list of line items.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getpaymentlinkspaymentlinklineitems-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|payment_link|path|string|true|none|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## GetPaymentMethods

<a id="opIdGetPaymentMethods"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_methods \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payment_methods`

<p>Returns a list of PaymentMethods for Treasury flows. If you want to list the PaymentMethods attached to a Customer for payments, you should use the <a href="/docs/api/payment_methods/customer_list">List a Customer’s PaymentMethods</a> API instead.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getpaymentmethods-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|query|string|false|The ID of the customer whose PaymentMethods will be retrieved.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|type|query|string|false|An optional filter on the list, based on the object `type` field. Without the filter, the list includes all current and future payment method types. If your integration expects only one type of payment method in the response, make sure to provide a type value in the request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|acss_debit|

<h3 id="getpaymentmethods-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

## PostPaymentMethods

<a id="opIdPostPaymentMethods"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_methods \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'acss_debit=%7B%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22institution_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22transit_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&affirm=%7B%7D&afterpay_clearpay=%7B%7D&alipay=%7B%7D&au_becs_debit=%7B%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22bsb_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&bacs_debit=%7B%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22sort_code%22%3A%22string%22%7D&bancontact=%7B%7D&billing_details=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D&blik=%7B%7D&boleto=%7B%22tax_id%22%3A%22string%22%7D&card=%7B%22cvc%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22exp_month%22%3A0%2C%22exp_year%22%3A0%2C%22number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&customer=string&customer_balance=%7B%7D&eps=%7B%22bank%22%3A%22arzte_und_apotheker_bank%22%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&fpx=%7B%22bank%22%3A%22affin_bank%22%7D&giropay=%7B%7D&grabpay=%7B%7D&ideal=%7B%22bank%22%3A%22abn_amro%22%7D&interac_present=%7B%7D&klarna=%7B%22dob%22%3A%7B%22day%22%3A0%2C%22month%22%3A0%2C%22year%22%3A0%7D%7D&konbini=%7B%7D&link=%7B%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&oxxo=%7B%7D&p24=%7B%22bank%22%3A%22alior_bank%22%7D&payment_method=string&paynow=%7B%7D&pix=%7B%7D&promptpay=%7B%7D&radar_options=%7B%22session%22%3A%22string%22%7D&sepa_debit=%7B%22iban%22%3A%22string%22%7D&sofort=%7B%22country%22%3A%22AT%22%7D&type=acss_debit&us_bank_account=%7B%22account_holder_type%22%3A%22company%22%2C%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22account_type%22%3A%22checking%22%2C%22financial_connections_account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22routing_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D&wechat_pay=%7B%7D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_methods`

<p>Creates a PaymentMethod object. Read the <a href="/docs/stripe-js/reference#stripe-create-payment-method">Stripe.js reference</a> to learn how to create PaymentMethods via Stripe.js.</p>

<p>Instead of creating a PaymentMethod directly, we recommend using the <a href="/docs/payments/accept-a-payment">PaymentIntents</a> API to accept a payment immediately or the <a href="/docs/payments/save-and-reuse">SetupIntent</a> API to collect payment method details ahead of a future payment.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
acss_debit:
  account_number: string
  institution_number: string
  transit_number: string
affirm: {}
afterpay_clearpay: {}
alipay: {}
au_becs_debit:
  account_number: string
  bsb_number: string
bacs_debit:
  account_number: string
  sort_code: string
bancontact: {}
billing_details:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
blik: {}
boleto:
  tax_id: string
card:
  cvc: string
  exp_month: 0
  exp_year: 0
  number: string
customer: string
customer_balance: {}
eps:
  bank: arzte_und_apotheker_bank
expand:
  - string
fpx:
  bank: affin_bank
giropay: {}
grabpay: {}
ideal:
  bank: abn_amro
interac_present: {}
klarna:
  dob:
    day: 0
    month: 0
    year: 0
konbini: {}
link: {}
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
oxxo: {}

payment_method: string

pix: {}
promptpay: {}

  session: string
sepa_debit:

sofort:
  country: AT
type: acss_debit
us_bank_account:
  account_holder_type: company
  account_number: string
  account_type: checking
  financial_connections_account: string
  routing_number: string
wechat_pay: {}
```

<a id="opIdPostPaymentMethodsPaymentMethod"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_methods/string \

  -d 'billing_details=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D&card=%7B%22exp_month%22%3A0%2C%22exp_year%22%3A0%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&link=%7B%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&us_bank_account=%7B%22account_holder_type%22%3A%22company%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_methods/{payment_method}`

<p>Updates a PaymentMethod object. A PaymentMethod must be attached a customer to be updated.</p>

```yaml

  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
card:
  exp_month: 0
  exp_year: 0
expand:
  - string
link: {}
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
us_bank_account:
  account_holder_type: company
```

## PostPaymentMethodsPaymentMethodAttach

<a id="opIdPostPaymentMethodsPaymentMethodAttach"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment_methods/string/attach \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'customer=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/payment_methods/{payment_method}/attach`

<p>Attaches a PaymentMethod object to a Customer.</p>

<p>To attach a new PaymentMethod to a customer for future payments, we recommend you use a <a href="/docs/api/setup_intents">SetupIntent</a>
or a PaymentIntent with <a href="/docs/api/payment_intents/create#create_payment_intent-setup_future_usage">setup_future_usage</a>.
These approaches will perform any necessary steps to set up the PaymentMethod for future payments. Using the <code>/v1/payment_methods/:id/attach</code>
endpoint without first using a SetupIntent or PaymentIntent with <code>setup_future_usage</code> does not optimize the PaymentMethod for
future use, which makes later declines and payment friction more likely.
See <a href="/docs/payments/payment-intents#future-usage">Optimizing cards for future payments</a> for more information about setting up
future payments.</p>

<p>To use this PaymentMethod as the default for invoice or subscription payments,
set <a href="/docs/api/customers/update#update_customer-invoice_settings-default_payment_method"><code>invoice_settings.default_payment_method</code></a>,
on the Customer to the PaymentMethod’s ID.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
customer: string
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postpaymentmethodspaymentmethodattach-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payment_method|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» customer|body|string|true|The ID of the customer to which to attach the PaymentMethod.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

## GetPayouts

<a id="opIdGetPayouts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payouts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/payouts`

<p>Returns a list of existing payouts sent to third-party bank accounts or that Stripe has sent you. The payouts are returned in sorted order, with the most recently created payouts appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter


## PostPayouts

<a id="opIdPostPayouts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payouts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&description=string&destination=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&method=instant&source_type=bank_account&statement_descriptor=string'
```

`POST /v1/payouts`

<p>To send funds to your own bank account, you create a new payout object. Your <a href="#balance">Stripe balance</a> must be able to cover the payout amount, or you’ll receive an “Insufficient Funds” error.</p>

<p>If your API key is in test mode, money won’t actually be sent, though everything else will occur as if in live mode.</p>

<p>If you are creating a manual payout on a Stripe account that uses multiple payment source types, you’ll need to specify the source type balance that the payout should draw from. The <a href="#balance_object">balance object</a> details available and pending amounts by source type.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
description: string
destination: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
method: instant
source_type: bank_account
statement_descriptor: string
```

<h3 id="postpayouts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|A positive integer in cents representing how much to payout.|
|» currency|body|string|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» destination|body|string|false|The ID of a bank account or a card to send the payout to. If no destination is supplied, the default external account for the specified currency will be used.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» method|body|string|false|The method used to send this payout, which can be `standard` or `instant`. `instant` is only supported for payouts to debit cards. (See [Instant payouts for marketplaces for more information](https://stripe.com/blog/instant-payouts-for-marketplaces).)|
|» source_type|body|string|false|The balance type of your Stripe balance to draw this payout from. Balances for different payment sources are kept separately. You can find the amounts with the balances API. One of `bank_account`, `card`, or `fpx`.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|A string to be displayed on the recipient's bank or card statement. This may be at most 22 characters. Attempting to use a `statement_descriptor` longer than 22 characters will return an error. Note: Most banks will truncate this information and/or display it inconsistently. Some may not display it at all.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» method|instant|
|» method|standard|
|» source_type|bank_account|
|» source_type|card|
|» source_type|fpx|

`POST /v1/payouts/{payout}/reverse`

<p>Reverses a payout by debiting the destination bank account. Only payouts for connected accounts to US bank accounts may be reversed at this time. If the payout is in the <code>pending</code> status, <code>/v1/payouts/:id/cancel</code> should be used instead.</p>

<p>By requesting a reversal via <code>/v1/payouts/:id/reverse</code>, you confirm that the authorized signatory of the selected bank account has authorized the debit on the bank account and that no other authorization is required.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
```

```bash
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'active=true&aggregate_usage=last_during_period&amount=0&amount_decimal=string&billing_scheme=per_unit&currency=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&id=string&interval=day&interval_count=0&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&nickname=string&product=%7B%22active%22%3Atrue%2C%22id%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22statement_descriptor%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tax_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22unit_label%22%3A%22string%22%7D&tiers=%5B%7B%22flat_amount%22%3A0%2C%22flat_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22up_to%22%3A%22inf%22%7D%5D&tiers_mode=graduated&transform_usage=%7B%22divide_by%22%3A0%2C%22round%22%3A%22down%22%7D&trial_period_days=0&usage_type=licensed'
```

`POST /v1/plans`

<p>You can now model subscriptions more flexibly using the <a href="#prices">Prices API</a>. It replaces the Plans API and is backwards compatible to simplify your migration.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
aggregate_usage: last_during_period
amount: 0
amount_decimal: string
billing_scheme: per_unit
currency: string
expand:
  - string
id: string
interval: day
interval_count: 0
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
nickname: string
product:
  active: true
  id: string
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  name: string
  statement_descriptor: string
  tax_code: string
  unit_label: string
tiers:
  -
    flat_amount: 0
    flat_amount_decimal: string
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
    up_to: inf
tiers_mode: graduated
transform_usage:
  divide_by: 0
  round: down
trial_period_days: 0
usage_type: licensed
```

<h3 id="postplans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Whether the plan is currently available for new subscriptions. Defaults to `true`.|
|» aggregate_usage|body|string|false|Specifies a usage aggregation strategy for plans of `usage_type=metered`. Allowed values are `sum` for summing up all usage during a period, `last_during_period` for using the last usage record reported within a period, `last_ever` for using the last usage record ever (across period bounds) or `max` which uses the usage record with the maximum reported usage during a period. Defaults to `sum`.|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer in cents (or local equivalent) (or 0 for a free plan) representing how much to charge on a recurring basis.|
|» amount_decimal|body|string(decimal)|false|Same as `amount`, but accepts a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places. Only one of `amount` and `amount_decimal` can be set.|
|» billing_scheme|body|string|false|Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `amount`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for plans with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for plans with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes.|
|» currency|body|string|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» id|body|string|false|An identifier randomly generated by Stripe. Used to identify this plan when subscribing a customer. You can optionally override this ID, but the ID must be unique across all plans in your Stripe account. You can, however, use the same plan ID in both live and test modes.|
|» interval|body|string|true|Specifies billing frequency. Either `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`.|
|» interval_count|body|integer|false|The number of intervals between subscription billings. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months. Maximum of one year interval allowed (1 year, 12 months, or 52 weeks).|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» nickname|body|string|false|A brief description of the plan, hidden from customers.|
|» product|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|The product whose pricing the created plan will represent. This can either be the ID of an existing product, or a dictionary containing fields used to create a [service product](https://stripe.com/docs/api#product_object-type).|
|» » active|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|none|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|none|
|» » statement_descriptor|body|string|false|none|
|» » tax_code|body|string|false|none|
|» » unit_label|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|The ID of the product whose pricing the created plan will represent.|
|» tiers|body|[object]|false|Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`.|
|» » flat_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » flat_amount_decimal|body|string(decimal)|false|none|
|» » unit_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » unit_amount_decimal|body|string(decimal)|false|none|
|» » up_to|body|string \| integer|true|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» tiers_mode|body|string|false|Defines if the tiering price should be `graduated` or `volume` based. In `volume`-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price, in `graduated` tiering pricing can successively change as the quantity grows.|
|» transform_usage|body|object|false|Apply a transformation to the reported usage or set quantity before computing the billed price. Cannot be combined with `tiers`.|
|» » divide_by|body|integer|true|none|
|» » round|body|string|true|none|
|» trial_period_days|body|integer|false|Default number of trial days when subscribing a customer to this plan using [`trial_from_plan=true`](https://stripe.com/docs/api#create_subscription-trial_from_plan).|
|» usage_type|body|string|false|Configures how the quantity per period should be determined. Can be either `metered` or `licensed`. `licensed` automatically bills the `quantity` set when adding it to a subscription. `metered` aggregates the total usage based on usage records. Defaults to `licensed`.|

|» aggregate_usage|last_ever|
|» aggregate_usage|max|
|» aggregate_usage|sum|

|» billing_scheme|tiered|

|» tiers_mode|graduated|

|» » round|up|
|» usage_type|licensed|
|» usage_type|metered|

`POST /v1/plans/{plan}`

<p>Updates the specified plan by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided are left unchanged. By design, you cannot change a plan’s ID, amount, currency, or billing cycle.</p>

```yaml
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
nickname: string
product: string
trial_period_days: 0
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» product|body|string|false|The product the plan belongs to. This cannot be changed once it has been used in a subscription or subscription schedule.|
|» trial_period_days|body|integer|false|Default number of trial days when subscribing a customer to this plan using [`trial_from_plan=true`](https://stripe.com/docs/api#create_subscription-trial_from_plan).|

|recurring|query|object|false|Only return prices with these recurring fields.|

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|type|query|string|false|Only return prices of type `recurring` or `one_time`.|

g'

`POST /v1/prices`

<p>Creates a new price for an existing product. The price can be recurring or one-time.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
billing_scheme: per_unit
currency: string
currency_options:
  property1:
    custom_unit_amount:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
      preset: 0
    tax_behavior: exclusive
    tiers:
      -
        flat_amount: 0
        flat_amount_decimal: string
        unit_amount: 0
        unit_amount_decimal: string
        up_to: inf
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
  property2:
    custom_unit_amount:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
      preset: 0
    tax_behavior: exclusive
    tiers:
      -
        flat_amount: 0
        flat_amount_decimal: string
        unit_amount: 0
        unit_amount_decimal: string
        up_to: inf
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
custom_unit_amount:
  enabled: true
  maximum: 0
  minimum: 0
  preset: 0
expand:
  - string
lookup_key: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
nickname: string
product: string
product_data:
  active: true
  id: string
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  name: string
  statement_descriptor: string
  tax_code: string
  unit_label: string
recurring:
  aggregate_usage: last_during_period
  interval: day
  interval_count: 0
  usage_type: licensed
tax_behavior: exclusive
tiers:
  -
    flat_amount: 0
    flat_amount_decimal: string
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
    up_to: inf
tiers_mode: graduated
transfer_lookup_key: true
transform_quantity:
  divide_by: 0
  round: down
unit_amount: 0
unit_amount_decimal: string
```

<h3 id="postprices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|» active|body|boolean|false|Whether the price can be used for new purchases. Defaults to `true`.|
|» billing_scheme|body|string|false|Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `unit_amount` or `unit_amount_decimal`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for prices with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for prices with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes.|

|» currency_options|body|object|false|Prices defined in each available currency option. Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|

conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

`POST /v1/prices/{price}`

<p>Updates the specified price by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided are left unchanged.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
currency_options:
  property1:
    custom_unit_amount:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
      preset: 0
    tax_behavior: exclusive
    tiers:
      -
        flat_amount: 0
        flat_amount_decimal: string
        unit_amount: 0
        unit_amount_decimal: string
        up_to: inf
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
  property2:
    custom_unit_amount:
      enabled: true
      maximum: 0
      minimum: 0
      preset: 0
    tax_behavior: exclusive
    tiers:
      -
        flat_amount: 0
        flat_amount_decimal: string
        unit_amount: 0
        unit_amount_decimal: string
        up_to: inf
    unit_amount: 0
    unit_amount_decimal: string
expand:
  - string
lookup_key: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
nickname: string
tax_behavior: exclusive
transfer_lookup_key: true
```

## GetProducts

<a id="opIdGetProducts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/products \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/products`

<p>Returns a list of your products. The products are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recently created products appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getproducts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|query|boolean|false|Only return products that are active or inactive (e.g., pass `false` to list all inactive products).|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|Only return products that were created during the given date interval.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|ids|query|[string]|false|Only return products with the given IDs. Cannot be used with [starting_after](https://stripe.com/docs/api#list_products-starting_after) or [ending_before](https://stripe.com/docs/api#list_products-ending_before).|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|shippable|query|boolean|false|Only return products that can be shipped (i.e., physical, not digital products).|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|url|query|string|false|Only return products with the given url.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## GetProductsSearch

<a id="opIdGetProductsSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/v1/products/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/products/search`

<p>Search for products you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getproductssearch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://stripe.com/docs/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for products](https://stripe.com/docs/search#query-fields-for-products).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|


`POST /v1/promotion_codes`

<p>A promotion code points to a coupon. You can optionally restrict the code to a specific customer, redemption limit, and expiration date.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
code: string
coupon: string
customer: string
expand:
  - string
expires_at: 0
max_redemptions: 0
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
restrictions:
  currency_options:
    property1:
      minimum_amount: 0
    property2:
      minimum_amount: 0
  first_time_transaction: true
  minimum_amount: 0
  minimum_amount_currency: string
```

<h3 id="postpromotioncodes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Whether the promotion code is currently active.|
|» code|body|string|false|The customer-facing code. Regardless of case, this code must be unique across all active promotion codes for a specific customer. If left blank, we will generate one automatically.|
|» coupon|body|string|true|The coupon for this promotion code.|
|» customer|body|string|false|The customer that this promotion code can be used by. If not set, the promotion code can be used by all customers.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» expires_at|body|integer(unix-time)|false|The timestamp at which this promotion code will expire. If the coupon has specified a `redeems_by`, then this value cannot be after the coupon's `redeems_by`.|
|» max_redemptions|body|integer|false|A positive integer specifying the number of times the promotion code can be redeemed. If the coupon has specified a `max_redemptions`, then this value cannot be greater than the coupon's `max_redemptions`.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» restrictions|body|object|false|Settings that restrict the redemption of the promotion code.|
|» » currency_options|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » minimum_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » first_time_transaction|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » minimum_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » minimum_amount_currency|body|string|false|none|

## PostQuotes

<a id="opIdPostQuotes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/quotes \

  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'application_fee_amount=0&application_fee_percent=0&automatic_tax=%7B%22enabled%22%3Atrue%7D&collection_method=charge_automatically&customer=string&default_tax_rates=%5B%22string%22%5D&description=string&discounts=%5B%7B%22coupon%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22discount%22%3A%22string%22%7D%5D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&expires_at=0&footer=string&from_quote=%7B%22is_revision%22%3Atrue%2C%22quote%22%3A%22string%22%7D&header=string&invoice_settings=%7B%22days_until_due%22%3A0%7D&line_items=%5B%7B%22price%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22price_data%22%3A%7B%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22recurring%22%3A%7B%22interval%22%3A%22day%22%2C%22interval_count%22%3A0%7D%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%2C%22tax_rates%22%3A%5B%22string%22%5D%7D%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&on_behalf_of=string&subscription_data=%7B%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22effective_date%22%3A%22current_period_end%22%2C%22trial_period_days%22%3A0%7D&test_clock=string&transfer_data=%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22amount_percent%22%3A0%2C%22destination%22%3A%22string%22%7D'
```

`POST /v1/quotes`

<p>A quote models prices and services for a customer. Default options for <code>header</code>, <code>description</code>, <code>footer</code>, and <code>expires_at</code> can be set in the dashboard via the <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/billing/quote">quote template</a>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
application_fee_amount: 0
application_fee_percent: 0
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
collection_method: charge_automatically
customer: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
description: string
discounts:
  -
    coupon: string
    discount: string
expand:
  - string
expires_at: 0
footer: string
from_quote:
  is_revision: true
  quote: string
header: string
invoice_settings:
  days_until_due: 0
line_items:
  -
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
on_behalf_of: string
subscription_data:
  description: string
  effective_date: current_period_end
  trial_period_days: 0
test_clock: string
transfer_data:
  amount: 0
  amount_percent: 0
  destination: string
```

|payment_method|query|string|false|Only return SetupIntents associated with the specified payment method.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. `POST /v1/setup_intents`

<p>Creates a SetupIntent object.</p>

<p>After the SetupIntent is created, attach a payment method and <a href="/docs/api/setup_intents/confirm">confirm</a>
to collect any required permissions to charge the payment method later.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
attach_to_self: true
confirm: true
customer: string
description: string
expand:
  - string
flow_directions:
  - inbound
mandate_data:
  customer_acceptance:
    accepted_at: 0
    offline: {}
    online:
      ip_address: string
      user_agent: string
    type: offline
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
on_behalf_of: string
payment_method: string
payment_method_data:
  acss_debit:
    account_number: string
    institution_number: string
    transit_number: string
  affirm: {}
  afterpay_clearpay: {}
  alipay: {}
  au_becs_debit:
    account_number: string
    bsb_number: string
  bacs_debit:
    account_number: string
    sort_code: string
  bancontact: {}
  billing_details:
    address:
      city: string
      country: string
      line1: string
      line2: string
      postal_code: string
      state: string
    email: string
    name: string
    phone: string
  blik: {}
  boleto:
    tax_id: string
  customer_balance: {}
  eps:
    bank: arzte_und_apotheker_bank
  fpx:
    bank: affin_bank
  giropay: {}
  grabpay: {}
  ideal:
    bank: abn_amro
  interac_present: {}
  klarna:
    dob:
      day: 0
      month: 0
      year: 0
  konbini: {}
  link: {}
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  oxxo: {}
  p24:
    bank: alior_bank
  paynow: {}
  pix: {}
  promptpay: {}
  radar_options:
    session: string
  sepa_debit:
    iban: string
  sofort:
    country: AT
  type: acss_debit
  us_bank_account:
    account_holder_type: company
    account_number: string
    account_type: checking
    financial_connections_account: string
    routing_number: string
  wechat_pay: {}
payment_method_options:
  acss_debit:
    currency: cad
    mandate_options:
      custom_mandate_url: string
      default_for:
        - invoice
      interval_description: string
      payment_schedule: combined
      transaction_type: business
    verification_method: automatic
  blik:
    code: string
  card:
    mandate_options:
      amount: 0
      amount_type: fixed
      currency: string

      end_date: 0
      interval: day

      reference: string

        - india
    network: amex
    request_three_d_secure: any
  link:

    mandate_options: {}
  us_bank_account:

      permissions:
        - balances
      return_url: string
    networks:
      requested:
        - ach
    verification_method: automatic

  - string

  amount: 0
  currency: string
usage: off_session
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» attach_to_self|body|boolean|false|If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account.<br><br>It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer.|
|» confirm|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to attempt to confirm this SetupIntent immediately. This parameter defaults to `false`. If the payment method attached is a card, a return_url may be provided in case additional authentication is required.|
|» customer|body|string|false|ID of the Customer this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Customer on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this SetupIntent.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» flow_directions|body|[string]|false|Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used.<br><br>Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes.|
|» mandate_data|body|object|false|This hash contains details about the Mandate to create. This parameter can only be used with [`confirm=true`](https://stripe.com/docs/api/setup_intents/create#create_setup_intent-confirm).|

## GetSetupIntentsIntent

<a id="opIdGetSetupIntentsIntent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/setup_intents/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/setup_intents/{intent}`

<p>Retrieves the details of a SetupIntent that has previously been created. </p>

<p>Client-side retrieval using a publishable key is allowed when the <code>client_secret</code> is provided in the query string. </p>

<p>When retrieved with a publishable key, only a subset of properties will be returned. Please refer to the <a href="#setup_intent_object">SetupIntent</a> object reference for more details.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getsetupintentsintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_secret|query|string|false|The client secret of the SetupIntent. Required if a publishable key is used to retrieve the SetupIntent.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

<h3 id="postsetupintentsintent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» attach_to_self|body|boolean|false|If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account.<br><br>It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer.|
|» customer|body|string|false|ID of the Customer this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Customer on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this SetupIntent.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» flow_directions|body|[string]|false|Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used.<br><br>Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|

## PostSetupIntentsIntentCancel

<a id="opIdPostSetupIntentsIntentCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/setup_intents/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'cancellation_reason=abandoned&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/setup_intents/{intent}/cancel`

<p>A SetupIntent object can be canceled when it is in one of these statuses: <code>requires_payment_method</code>, <code>requires_confirmation</code>, or <code>requires_action</code>. </p>

<p>Once canceled, setup is abandoned and any operations on the SetupIntent will fail with an error.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
cancellation_reason: abandoned
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postsetupintentsintentcancel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» cancellation_reason|body|string|false|Reason for canceling this SetupIntent. Possible values are `abandoned`, `requested_by_customer`, or `duplicate`|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cancellation_reason|abandoned|
|» cancellation_reason|duplicate|
|» cancellation_reason|requested_by_customer|

`POST /v1/setup_intents/{intent}/confirm`

<p>Confirm that your customer intends to set up the current or
provided payment method. For example, you would confirm a SetupIntent
when a customer hits the “Save” button on a payment method management
page on your website.</p>

<p>If the selected payment method does not require any additional
steps from the customer, the SetupIntent will transition to the
<code>succeeded</code> status.</p>

<p>Otherwise, it will transition to the <code>requires_action</code> status and
suggest additional actions via <code>next_action</code>. If setup fails,
the SetupIntent will transition to the
<code>requires_payment_method</code> status.</p>

## PostSetupIntentsIntentVerifyMicrodeposits

<a id="opIdPostSetupIntentsIntentVerifyMicrodeposits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/setup_intents/string/verify_microdeposits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amounts=%5B0%5D&client_secret=string&descriptor_code=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/setup_intents/{intent}/verify_microdeposits`

<p>Verifies microdeposits on a SetupIntent object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amounts:
  - 0
client_secret: string
descriptor_code: string
expand:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postsetupintentsintentverifymicrodeposits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|intent|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amounts|body|[integer]|false|Two positive integers, in *cents*, equal to the values of the microdeposits sent to the bank account.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The client secret of the SetupIntent.|
|» descriptor_code|body|string|false|A six-character code starting with SM present in the microdeposit sent to the bank account.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|


`POST /v1/shipping_rates`

<p>Creates a new shipping rate object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
delivery_estimate:
  maximum:
    unit: business_day
    value: 0
  minimum:
    unit: business_day
    value: 0
display_name: string
expand:
  - string
fixed_amount:
  amount: 0
  currency: string
  currency_options:
    property1:
      amount: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
    property2:
      amount: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
tax_behavior: exclusive
tax_code: string
type: fixed_amount
```

|» » » unit|body|string|true|none|

|» » minimum|body|object|false|none|
|» » » unit|body|string|true|none|
|» » » value|body|integer|true|none|

|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|

|» » amount|body|integer|true|none|
|» » currency|body|string|true|none|

All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

|» tax_code|body|string|false|A [tax code](https://stripe.com/docs/tax/tax-categories) ID. The Shipping tax code is `txcd_92010001`.|

`POST /v1/sources`

<p>Creates a new source object.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
customer: string
expand:
  - string
flow: code_verification
mandate:
  acceptance:
    date: 0
    ip: string
    offline:
      contact_email: string
    online:
      date: 0
      ip: string
      user_agent: string
    status: accepted
    type: offline
    user_agent: string
  amount: 0
  currency: string
  interval: one_time
  notification_method: deprecated_none
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
original_source: string
owner:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
receiver:
  refund_attributes_method: email
redirect:
  return_url: string
source_order:
  items:
    -
      amount: 0
      currency: string
      description: string
      parent: string
      quantity: 0
      type: discount
  shipping:
    address:
      city: string
      country: string
      line1: string
      line2: string
      postal_code: string
      state: string
    carrier: string
    name: string
    phone: string
    tracking_number: string
statement_descriptor: string
token: string
type: string
usage: reusable
```

<h3 id="postsources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Amount associated with the source. This is the amount for which the source will be chargeable once ready. Required for `single_use` sources. Not supported for `receiver` type sources, where charge amount may not be specified until funds land.|
|» currency|body|string|false|Three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies) associated with the source. This is the currency for which the source will be chargeable once ready.|
|» customer|body|string|false|The `Customer` to whom the original source is attached to. Must be set when the original source is not a `Source` (e.g., `Card`).|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» flow|body|string|false|The authentication `flow` of the source to create. `flow` is one of `redirect`, `receiver`, `code_verification`, `none`. It is generally inferred unless a type supports multiple flows.|
|» mandate|body|object|false|Information about a mandate possibility attached to a source object (generally for bank debits) as well as its acceptance status.|

## PostSourcesSource

<a id="opIdPostSourcesSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/sources/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&mandate=%7B%22acceptance%22%3A%7B%22date%22%3A0%2C%22ip%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22offline%22%3A%7B%22contact_email%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22online%22%3A%7B%22date%22%3A0%2C%22ip%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22user_agent%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22status%22%3A%22accepted%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22offline%22%2C%22user_agent%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22interval%22%3A%22one_time%22%2C%22notification_method%22%3A%22deprecated_none%22%7D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&owner=%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D&source_order=%7B%22items%22%3A%5B%7B%22amount%22%3A0%2C%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22description%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22parent%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22quantity%22%3A0%2C%22type%22%3A%22discount%22%7D%5D%2C%22shipping%22%3A%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22carrier%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22tracking_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D'
```

`POST /v1/sources/{source}`

<p>Updates the specified source by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided will be left unchanged.</p>

<p>This request accepts the <code>metadata</code> and <code>owner</code> as arguments. It is also possible to update type specific information for selected payment methods. Please refer to our <a href="/docs/sources">payment method guides</a> for more detail.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
expand:
  - string
mandate:
  acceptance:
    date: 0
    ip: string
    offline:
      contact_email: string
    online:
      date: 0
      ip: string
      user_agent: string
    status: accepted
    type: offline
    user_agent: string
  amount: 0
  currency: string
  interval: one_time
  notification_method: deprecated_none
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
owner:
  address:
    city: string
    country: string
    line1: string
    line2: string
    postal_code: string
    state: string
  email: string
  name: string
  phone: string
source_order:
  items:
    -
      amount: 0
      currency: string
      description: string
      parent: string
      quantity: 0
      type: discount
  shipping:
    address:
      city: string
      country: string
      line1: string
      line2: string
      postal_code: string
      state: string
    carrier: string
    name: string
    phone: string
    tracking_number: string
```

|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|

|body|body|object|false|none|

## PostSubscriptionItems

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/subscription_items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'billing_thresholds=%7B%22usage_gte%22%3A0%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&payment_behavior=allow_incomplete&price=string&price_data=%7B%22currency%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22product%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22recurring%22%3A%7B%22interval%22%3A%22day%22%2C%22interval_count%22%3A0%7D%2C%22tax_behavior%22%3A%22exclusive%22%2C%22unit_amount%22%3A0%2C%22unit_amount_decimal%22%3A%22string%22%7D&proration_behavior=always_invoice&proration_date=0&quantity=0&subscription=string&tax_rates=%5B%22string%22%5D'
```

`POST /v1/subscription_items`

<p>Adds a new item to an existing subscription. No existing items will be changed or replaced.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
billing_thresholds:
  usage_gte: 0
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
payment_behavior: allow_incomplete
price: string
price_data:
  currency: string
  product: string
  recurring:
    interval: day
    interval_count: 0
  tax_behavior: exclusive
  unit_amount: 0
  unit_amount_decimal: string
proration_behavior: always_invoice
proration_date: 0
quantity: 0
subscription: string
tax_rates:
  - string
```

<h3 id="postsubscriptionitems-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» billing_thresholds|body|object \| string|false|Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the subscription advanced to a new billing period. When updating, pass an empty string to remove previously-defined thresholds.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » usage_gte|body|integer|true|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» payment_behavior|body|string|false|Use `allow_incomplete` to transition the subscription to `status=past_due` if a payment is required but cannot be paid. This allows you to manage scenarios where additional user actions are needed to pay a subscription's invoice. For example, SCA regulation may require 3DS authentication to complete payment. See the [SCA Migration Guide](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/migration/strong-customer-authentication) for Billing to learn more. This is the default behavior.<br><br>Use `default_incomplete` to transition the subscription to `status=past_due` when payment is required and await explicit confirmation of the invoice's payment intent. This allows simpler management of scenarios where additional user actions are needed to pay a subscription’s invoice. Such as failed payments, [SCA regulation](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/migration/strong-customer-authentication), or collecting a mandate for a bank debit payment method.<br><br>Use `pending_if_incomplete` to update the subscription using [pending updates](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/pending-updates). When you use `pending_if_incomplete` you can only pass the parameters [supported by pending updates](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/pending-updates-reference#supported-attributes).<br><br>Use `error_if_incomplete` if you want Stripe to return an HTTP 402 status code if a subscription's invoice cannot be paid. For example, if a payment method requires 3DS authentication due to SCA regulation and further user action is needed, this parameter does not update the subscription and returns an error instead. This was the default behavior for API versions prior to 2019-03-14. See the [changelog](https://stripe.com/docs/upgrades#2019-03-14) to learn more.|
|» price|body|string|false|The ID of the price object.|
|» price_data|body|object|false|Data used to generate a new [Price](https://stripe.com/docs/api/prices) object inline.|
|» » currency|body|string|true|none|
|» » product|body|string|true|none|
|» » recurring|body|object|true|none|
|» » » interval|body|string|true|none|
|» » » interval_count|body|integer|false|none|
|» » tax_behavior|body|string|false|none|
|» » unit_amount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » unit_amount_decimal|body|string(decimal)|false|none|
|» proration_behavior|body|string|false|Determines how to handle [prorations](https://stripe.com/docs/subscriptions/billing-cycle#prorations) when the billing cycle changes (e.g., when switching plans, resetting `billing_cycle_anchor=now`, or starting a trial), or if an item's `quantity` changes. The default value is `create_prorations`.|
|» proration_date|body|integer(unix-time)|false|If set, the proration will be calculated as though the subscription was updated at the given time. This can be used to apply the same proration that was previewed with the [upcoming invoice](https://stripe.com/docs/api#retrieve_customer_invoice) endpoint.|
|» quantity|body|integer|false|The quantity you'd like to apply to the subscription item you're creating.|
|» subscription|body|string|true|The identifier of the subscription to modify.|
|» tax_rates|body|[string] \| string|false|A list of [Tax Rate](https://stripe.com/docs/api/tax_rates) ids. These Tax Rates will override the [`default_tax_rates`](https://stripe.com/docs/api/subscriptions/create#create_subscription-default_tax_rates) on the Subscription. When updating, pass an empty string to remove previously-defined tax rates.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|""|
|» payment_behavior|allow_incomplete|
|» payment_behavior|default_incomplete|
|» payment_behavior|error_if_incomplete|
|» payment_behavior|pending_if_incomplete|
|» » » interval|day|
|» » » interval|month|
|» » » interval|week|
|» » » interval|year|
|» » tax_behavior|exclusive|
|» » tax_behavior|inclusive|
|» » tax_behavior|unspecified|
|» proration_behavior|always_invoice|
|» proration_behavior|create_prorations|
|» proration_behavior|none|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

## GetSubscriptionItemsSubscriptionItemUsageRecordSummaries

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/subscription_items/{subscription_item}/usage_record_summaries`

<p>For the specified subscription item, returns a list of summary objects. Each object in the list provides usage information that’s been summarized from multiple usage records and over a subscription billing period (e.g., 15 usage records in the month of September).</p>

<p>The list is sorted in reverse-chronological order (newest first). The first list item represents the most current usage period that hasn’t ended yet. Since new usage records can still be added, the returned summary information for the subscription item’s ID should be seen as unstable until the subscription billing period ends.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|subscription_item|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## PostSubscriptionItemsSubscriptionItemUsageRecords

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionItemsSubscriptionItemUsageRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/subscription_items/string/usage_records \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'action=increment&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&quantity=0&timestamp=now'
```

`POST /v1/subscription_items/{subscription_item}/usage_records`

<p>Creates a usage record for a specified subscription item and date, and fills it with a quantity.</p>

<p>Usage records provide <code>quantity</code> information that Stripe uses to track how much a customer is using your service. With usage information and the pricing model set up by the <a href="https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/metered-billing">metered billing</a> plan, Stripe helps you send accurate invoices to your customers.</p>

<p>The default calculation for usage is to add up all the <code>quantity</code> values of the usage records within a billing period. You can change this default behavior with the billing plan’s <code>aggregate_usage</code> <a href="/docs/api/plans/create#create_plan-aggregate_usage">parameter</a>. When there is more than one usage record with the same timestamp, Stripe adds the <code>quantity</code> values together. In most cases, this is the desired resolution, however, you can change this behavior with the <code>action</code> parameter.</p>

<p>The default pricing model for metered billing is <a href="/docs/api/plans/object#plan_object-billing_scheme">per-unit pricing</a>. For finer granularity, you can configure metered billing to have a <a href="https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/tiers">tiered pricing</a> model.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
action: increment
expand:
  - string
quantity: 0
timestamp: now
```

<h3 id="postsubscriptionitemssubscriptionitemusagerecords-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_item|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» action|body|string|false|Valid values are `increment` (default) or `set`. When using `increment` the specified `quantity` will be added to the usage at the specified timestamp. The `set` action will overwrite the usage quantity at that timestamp. If the subscription has [billing thresholds](https://stripe.com/docs/api/subscriptions/object#subscription_object-billing_thresholds), `increment` is the only allowed value.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» quantity|body|integer|true|The usage quantity for the specified timestamp.|
|» timestamp|body|string \| integer|false|The timestamp for the usage event. This timestamp must be within the current billing period of the subscription of the provided `subscription_item`, and must not be in the future. When passing `"now"`, Stripe records usage for the current time. Default is `"now"` if a value is not provided.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|increment|
|» action|set|
|» » *anyOf*|now|

```json
  "id": "string",

  "subscription_item": "string",
  "timestamp": 0
}
```
