`POST /v1/subscription_schedules`

<p>Creates a new subscription schedule object. Each customer can have up to 500 active or scheduled subscriptions.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
customer: string
default_settings:
  application_fee_percent: 0
  automatic_tax:
    enabled: true
  billing_cycle_anchor: automatic
  billing_thresholds:
    amount_gte: 0
    reset_billing_cycle_anchor: true
  collection_method: charge_automatically
  default_payment_method: string
  description: string
  invoice_settings:
    days_until_due: 0
  on_behalf_of: string
  transfer_data:
    amount_percent: 0
    destination: string
end_behavior: cancel
expand:
  - string
from_subscription: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
phases:
  -
    add_invoice_items:
      -
        price: string
        price_data:
          currency: string
          product: string
          tax_behavior: exclusive
          unit_amount: 0
          unit_amount_decimal: string
        quantity: 0
        tax_rates:
          - string
    application_fee_percent: 0
    automatic_tax:
      enabled: true
    billing_cycle_anchor: automatic
    billing_thresholds:
      amount_gte: 0
      reset_billing_cycle_anchor: true
    collection_method: charge_automatically
    coupon: string
    currency: string
    default_payment_method: string
    default_tax_rates:
      - string
    description: string
    end_date: 0
    invoice_settings:
      days_until_due: 0
    items:
      -
        billing_thresholds:
          usage_gte: 0
        metadata:
          property1: string
          property2: string
        price: string
        price_data:
          currency: string
          product: string
          recurring:
            interval: day
            interval_count: 0
          tax_behavior: exclusive
          unit_amount: 0
          unit_amount_decimal: string
        quantity: 0
        tax_rates:
          - string
    iterations: 0
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    on_behalf_of: string
    proration_behavior: always_invoice
    transfer_data:
      amount_percent: 0
      destination: string
    trial: true
    trial_end: 0
start_date: 0
```

## PostSubscriptionSchedulesScheduleCancel

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionSchedulesScheduleCancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/subscription_schedules/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&invoice_now=true&prorate=true'
```

`POST /v1/subscription_schedules/{schedule}/cancel`

<p>Cancels a subscription schedule and its associated subscription immediately (if the subscription schedule has an active subscription). A subscription schedule can only be canceled if its status is <code>not_started</code> or <code>active</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
invoice_now: true
prorate: true
```

<h3 id="postsubscriptionschedulesschedulecancel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|schedule|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» invoice_now|body|boolean|false|If the subscription schedule is `active`, indicates if a final invoice will be generated that contains any un-invoiced metered usage and new/pending proration invoice items. Defaults to `true`.|
|» prorate|body|boolean|false|If the subscription schedule is `active`, indicates if the cancellation should be prorated. Defaults to `true`.|

## PostSubscriptionSchedulesScheduleRelease

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionSchedulesScheduleRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/subscription_schedules/string/release \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&preserve_cancel_date=true'
```

`POST /v1/subscription_schedules/{schedule}/release`

<p>Releases the subscription schedule immediately, which will stop scheduling of its phases, but leave any existing subscription in place. A schedule can only be released if its status is <code>not_started</code> or <code>active</code>. If the subscription schedule is currently associated with a subscription, releasing it will remove its <code>subscription</code> property and set the subscription’s ID to the <code>released_subscription</code> property.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
preserve_cancel_date: true
```

<h3 id="postsubscriptionschedulesschedulerelease-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|schedule|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» preserve_cancel_date|body|boolean|false|Keep any cancellation on the subscription that the schedule has set|

## GetSubscriptions

<a id="opIdGetSubscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/subscriptions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/subscriptions`

<p>By default, returns a list of subscriptions that have not been canceled. In order to list canceled subscriptions, specify <code>status=canceled</code>.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getsubscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collection_method|query|string|false|The collection method of the subscriptions to retrieve. Either `charge_automatically` or `send_invoice`.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|current_period_end|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|current_period_start|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|customer|query|string|false|The ID of the customer whose subscriptions will be retrieved.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|price|query|string|false|Filter for subscriptions that contain this recurring price ID.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|The status of the subscriptions to retrieve. Passing in a value of `canceled` will return all canceled subscriptions, including those belonging to deleted customers. Pass `ended` to find subscriptions that are canceled and subscriptions that are expired due to [incomplete payment](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/overview#subscription-statuses). Passing in a value of `all` will return subscriptions of all statuses. If no value is supplied, all subscriptions that have not been canceled are returned.|
|test_clock|query|string|false|Filter for subscriptions that are associated with the specified test clock. The response will not include subscriptions with test clocks if this and the customer parameter is not set.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|collection_method|charge_automatically|
|collection_method|send_invoice|
|status|active|
|status|all|
|status|canceled|
|status|ended|
|status|incomplete|
|status|incomplete_expired|
|status|past_due|
|status|paused|
|status|trialing|
|status|unpaid|

`POST /v1/subscriptions`

<p>Creates a new subscription on an existing customer. Each customer can have up to 500 active or scheduled subscriptions.</p>

<p>When you create a subscription with <code>collection_method=charge_automatically</code>, the first invoice is finalized as part of the request.
The <code>payment_behavior</code> parameter determines the exact behavior of the initial payment.</p>

<p>To start subscriptions where the first invoice always begins in a <code>draft</code> status, use <a href="/docs/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules#managing">subscription schedules</a> instead.
Schedules provide the flexibility to model more complex billing configurations that change over time.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
add_invoice_items:
  -
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
application_fee_percent: 0
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
backdate_start_date: 0
billing_cycle_anchor: 0
billing_thresholds:
  amount_gte: 0
  reset_billing_cycle_anchor: true
cancel_at: 0
cancel_at_period_end: true
collection_method: charge_automatically
coupon: string
currency: string
customer: string
days_until_due: 0
default_payment_method: string
default_source: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
description: string
expand:
  - string
items:
  -
    billing_thresholds:
      usage_gte: 0
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
off_session: true
on_behalf_of: string
payment_behavior: allow_incomplete
payment_settings:
  payment_method_options:
    acss_debit:
      mandate_options:
        transaction_type: business
      verification_method: automatic
    bancontact:
      preferred_language: de
    card:
      mandate_options:
        amount: 0
        amount_type: fixed
        description: string
      network: amex
      request_three_d_secure: any
    customer_balance:
      bank_transfer:
        eu_bank_transfer:
          country: string
        type: string
      funding_type: string
    konbini: {}
    us_bank_account:
      financial_connections:
        permissions:
          - balances
      verification_method: automatic
  payment_method_types:
    - ach_credit_transfer
  save_default_payment_method: off
pending_invoice_item_interval:
  interval: day
  interval_count: 0
promotion_code: string
proration_behavior: always_invoice
transfer_data:
  amount_percent: 0
  destination: string
trial_end: now
trial_from_plan: true
trial_period_days: 0
trial_settings:
  end_behavior:
    missing_payment_method: cancel
```

## GetSubscriptionsSearch

<a id="opIdGetSubscriptionsSearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/v1/subscriptions/search?query=string' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/subscriptions/search`

<p>Search for subscriptions you’ve previously created using Stripe’s <a href="/docs/search#search-query-language">Search Query Language</a>.
Don’t use search in read-after-write flows where strict consistency is necessary. Under normal operating
conditions, data is searchable in less than a minute. Occasionally, propagation of new or updated data can be up
to an hour behind during outages. Search functionality is not available to merchants in India.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="getsubscriptionssearch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|page|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination across multiple pages of results. Don't include this parameter on the first call. Use the next_page value returned in a previous response to request subsequent results.|
|query|query|string|true|The search query string. See [search query language](https://stripe.com/docs/search#search-query-language) and the list of supported [query fields for subscriptions](https://stripe.com/docs/search#query-fields-for-subscriptions).|
|body|body|object|false|none|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|


`POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_exposed_id}`

<p>Updates an existing subscription on a customer to match the specified parameters. When changing plans or quantities, we will optionally prorate the price we charge next month to make up for any price changes. To preview how the proration will be calculated, use the <a href="#upcoming_invoice">upcoming invoice</a> endpoint.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
add_invoice_items:
  -
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
application_fee_percent: 0
automatic_tax:
  enabled: true
billing_cycle_anchor: now
billing_thresholds:
  amount_gte: 0
  reset_billing_cycle_anchor: true
cancel_at: 0
cancel_at_period_end: true
cancellation_details:
  comment: string
  feedback: ""
collection_method: charge_automatically
coupon: string
days_until_due: 0
default_payment_method: string
default_source: string
default_tax_rates:
  - string
description: string
expand:
  - string
items:
  -
    billing_thresholds:
      usage_gte: 0
    clear_usage: true
    deleted: true
    id: string
    metadata:
      property1: string
      property2: string
    price: string
    price_data:
      currency: string
      product: string
      recurring:
        interval: day
        interval_count: 0
      tax_behavior: exclusive
      unit_amount: 0
      unit_amount_decimal: string
    quantity: 0
    tax_rates:
      - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
off_session: true
on_behalf_of: string
pause_collection:
  behavior: keep_as_draft
  resumes_at: 0
payment_behavior: allow_incomplete
payment_settings:
  payment_method_options:
    acss_debit:
      mandate_options:
        transaction_type: business
      verification_method: automatic
    bancontact:
      preferred_language: de
    card:
      mandate_options:
        amount: 0
        amount_type: fixed
        description: string
      network: amex
      request_three_d_secure: any
    customer_balance:
      bank_transfer:
        eu_bank_transfer:
          country: string
        type: string
      funding_type: string
    konbini: {}
    us_bank_account:
      financial_connections:
        permissions:
          - balances
      verification_method: automatic
  payment_method_types:
    - ach_credit_transfer
  save_default_payment_method: off
pending_invoice_item_interval:
  interval: day
  interval_count: 0
promotion_code: string
proration_behavior: always_invoice
proration_date: 0
transfer_data:
  amount_percent: 0
  destination: string
trial_end: now
trial_from_plan: true
trial_settings:
  end_behavior:
    missing_payment_method: cancel
```

## DeleteSubscriptionsSubscriptionExposedId

<a id="opIdDeleteSubscriptionsSubscriptionExposedId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/subscriptions/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'cancellation_details=%7B%22comment%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22feedback%22%3A%22%22%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&invoice_now=true&prorate=true'
```

`DELETE /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_exposed_id}`

<p>Cancels a customer’s subscription immediately. The customer will not be charged again for the subscription.</p>

<p>Note, however, that any pending invoice items that you’ve created will still be charged for at the end of the period, unless manually <a href="#delete_invoiceitem">deleted</a>. If you’ve set the subscription to cancel at the end of the period, any pending prorations will also be left in place and collected at the end of the period. But if the subscription is set to cancel immediately, pending prorations will be removed.</p>

<p>By default, upon subscription cancellation, Stripe will stop automatic collection of all finalized invoices for the customer. This is intended to prevent unexpected payment attempts after the customer has canceled a subscription. However, you can resume automatic collection of the invoices manually after subscription cancellation to have us proceed. Or, you could check for unpaid invoices before allowing the customer to cancel the subscription at all.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
cancellation_details:
  comment: string
  feedback: ""
expand:
  - string
invoice_now: true
prorate: true
```

<h3 id="deletesubscriptionssubscriptionexposedid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_exposed_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» cancellation_details|body|object|false|Details about why this subscription was cancelled|
|» » comment|body|string|false|none|
|» » feedback|body|string|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» invoice_now|body|boolean|false|Will generate a final invoice that invoices for any un-invoiced metered usage and new/pending proration invoice items.|
|» prorate|body|boolean|false|Will generate a proration invoice item that credits remaining unused time until the subscription period end.|

|» » feedback|""|
|» » feedback|customer_service|

|» » feedback|missing_features|
|» » feedback|other|
|» » feedback|switched_service|
|» » feedback|too_complex|
|» » feedback|too_expensive|
|» » feedback|unused|

## PostSubscriptionsSubscriptionResume

<a id="opIdPostSubscriptionsSubscriptionResume"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/subscriptions/string/resume \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'billing_cycle_anchor=now&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&proration_behavior=always_invoice&proration_date=0'
```

`POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscription}/resume`

<p>Initiates resumption of a paused subscription, optionally resetting the billing cycle anchor and creating prorations. If a resumption invoice is generated, it must be paid or marked uncollectible before the subscription will be unpaused. If payment succeeds the subscription will become <code>active</code>, and if payment fails the subscription will be <code>past_due</code>. The resumption invoice will void automatically if not paid by the expiration date.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
billing_cycle_anchor: now
expand:
  - string
proration_behavior: always_invoice
proration_date: 0
```

<h3 id="postsubscriptionssubscriptionresume-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» billing_cycle_anchor|body|string|false|Either `now` or `unchanged`. Setting the value to `now` resets the subscription's billing cycle anchor to the current time (in UTC). Setting the value to `unchanged` advances the subscription's billing cycle anchor to the period that surrounds the current time. For more information, see the billing cycle [documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/billing-cycle).|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» proration_behavior|body|string|false|Determines how to handle [prorations](https://stripe.com/docs/subscriptions/billing-cycle#prorations) when the billing cycle changes (e.g., when switching plans, resetting `billing_cycle_anchor=now`, or starting a trial), or if an item's `quantity` changes. The default value is `create_prorations`.|
|» proration_date|body|integer(unix-time)|false|If set, the proration will be calculated as though the subscription was resumed at the given time. This can be used to apply exactly the same proration that was previewed with [upcoming invoice](https://stripe.com/docs/api#retrieve_customer_invoice) endpoint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» billing_cycle_anchor|now|
|» billing_cycle_anchor|unchanged|
|» proration_behavior|always_invoice|
|» proration_behavior|create_prorations|
|» proration_behavior|none|

|inclusive|query|boolean|false|Optional flag to filter by tax rates that are inclusive (or those that are not inclusive).|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|

## PostTaxRates

<a id="opIdPostTaxRates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/tax_rates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'active=true&country=string&description=string&display_name=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&inclusive=true&jurisdiction=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&percentage=0&state=st&tax_type=gst'
```

`POST /v1/tax_rates`

<p>Creates a new tax rate.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
active: true
country: string
description: string
display_name: string
expand:
  - string
inclusive: true
jurisdiction: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
percentage: 0
state: st
tax_type: gst
```

<h3 id="posttaxrates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Flag determining whether the tax rate is active or inactive (archived). Inactive tax rates cannot be used with new applications or Checkout Sessions, but will still work for subscriptions and invoices that already have it set.|
|» country|body|string|false|Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the tax rate for your internal use only. It will not be visible to your customers.|
|» display_name|body|string|true|The display name of the tax rate, which will be shown to users.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» inclusive|body|boolean|true|This specifies if the tax rate is inclusive or exclusive.|
|» jurisdiction|body|string|false|The jurisdiction for the tax rate. You can use this label field for tax reporting purposes. It also appears on your customer’s invoice.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» percentage|body|number|true|This represents the tax rate percent out of 100.|
|» state|body|string|false|[ISO 3166-2 subdivision code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2:US), without country prefix. For example, "NY" for New York, United States.|
|» tax_type|body|string|false|The high-level tax type, such as `vat` or `sales_tax`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» tax_type|gst|
|» tax_type|hst|
|» tax_type|igst|
|» tax_type|jct|
|» tax_type|lease_tax|
|» tax_type|pst|
|» tax_type|qst|
|» tax_type|rst|
|» tax_type|sales_tax|
|» tax_type|vat|

```bash
  -d 'expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&location=string'
```

`POST /v1/terminal/connection_tokens`

<p>To connect to a reader the Stripe Terminal SDK needs to retrieve a short-lived connection token from Stripe, proxied through your server. On your backend, add an endpoint that creates and returns a connection token.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
expand:
  - string
location: string
```

<h3 id="postterminalconnectiontokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» location|body|string|false|The id of the location that this connection token is scoped to. If specified the connection token will only be usable with readers assigned to that location, otherwise the connection token will be usable with all readers. Note that location scoping only applies to internet-connected readers. For more details, see [the docs on scoping connection tokens](https://stripe.com/docs/terminal/fleet/locations#connection-tokens).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "location": "string",
  "object": "terminal.connection_token",
  "secret": "string"
}
```

```json
    "message": "string",
    "param": "string",
    "payment_intent": {},
    "payment_method": {},
    "payment_method_type": "string",
    "request_log_url": "string",
    "setup_intent": {},
    "source": {},
    "type": "api_error"
  }
}
```

```bash
  -d 'amount=0&charge=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&payment_intent=string&refund_application_fee=true&reverse_transfer=true'
```

`POST /v1/terminal/readers/{reader}/refund_payment`

<p>Initiates a refund on a Reader</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
charge: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
payment_intent: string
refund_application_fee: true
reverse_transfer: true
```

<h3 id="postterminalreadersreaderrefundpayment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|reader|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer in __cents__ representing how much of this charge to refund.|
|» charge|body|string|false|ID of the Charge to refund.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» payment_intent|body|string|false|ID of the PaymentIntent to refund.|
|» refund_application_fee|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the application fee should be refunded when refunding this charge. If a full charge refund is given, the full application fee will be refunded. Otherwise, the application fee will be refunded in an amount proportional to the amount of the charge refunded. An application fee can be refunded only by the application that created the charge.|
|» reverse_transfer|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the transfer should be reversed when refunding this charge. The transfer will be reversed proportionally to the amount being refunded (either the entire or partial amount). A transfer can be reversed only by the application that created the charge.|

`POST /v1/test_helpers/customers/{customer}/fund_cash_balance`

<p>Create an incoming testmode bank transfer</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
expand:
  - string
reference: string
```

<h3 id="posttesthelperscustomerscustomerfundcashbalance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount to be used for this test cash balance transaction. A positive integer representing how much to fund in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to fund $1.00 or 100 to fund ¥100, a zero-decimal currency).|
|» currency|body|string|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» reference|body|string|false|A description of the test funding. This simulates free-text references supplied by customers when making bank transfers to their cash balance. You can use this to test how Stripe's [reconciliation algorithm](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/customer-balance/reconciliation) applies to different user inputs.|

`POST /v1/test_helpers/treasury/received_credits`

`POST /v1/tokens`

<p>Creates a single-use token that represents a bank account’s details.
This token can be used with any API method in place of a bank account dictionary. This token can be used only once, by attaching it to a <a href="#accounts">Custom account</a>.</p>

## GetTopups

<a id="opIdGetTopups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/topups \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/topups`

<p>Returns a list of top-ups.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="gettopups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|query|object \| integer|false|A positive integer representing how much to transfer.|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|A filter on the list, based on the object `created` field. The value can be a string with an integer Unix timestamp, or it can be a dictionary with a number of different query options.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|status|query|string|false|Only return top-ups that have the given status. One of `canceled`, `failed`, `pending` or `succeeded`.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|canceled|
|status|failed|
|status|pending|
|status|succeeded|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|A positive integer representing how much to transfer.|
|» currency|body|string|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» source|body|string|false|The ID of a source to transfer funds from. For most users, this should be left unspecified which will use the bank account that was set up in the dashboard for the specified currency. In test mode, this can be a test bank token (see [Testing Top-ups](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/testing#testing-top-ups)).|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|Extra information about a top-up for the source's bank statement. Limited to 15 ASCII characters.|
|» transfer_group|body|string|false|A string that identifies this top-up as part of a group.|

|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

`POST /v1/topups/{topup}`

## GetTransfers

<a id="opIdGetTransfers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/transfers \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/transfers`

<p>Returns a list of existing transfers sent to connected accounts. The transfers are returned in sorted order, with the most recently created transfers appearing first.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml

```

<h3 id="gettransfers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|query|object \| integer|false|none|
|destination|query|string|false|Only return transfers for the destination specified by this account ID.|
|ending_before|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|limit|query|integer|false|A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.|
|transfer_group|query|string|false|Only return transfers with the specified transfer group.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "amount": 0,
      "amount_reversed": 0,
      "balance_transaction": "string",
      "created": 0,
      "currency": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "destination": "string",
      "destination_payment": "string",
      "id": "string",
      "livemode": true,
      "metadata": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "object": "transfer",
      "reversals": {
        "data": [
          {}
        ],
        "has_more": true,
        "object": "list",
        "url": "string"
      },
      "reversed": true,
      "source_transaction": "string",
      "source_type": "string",
      "transfer_group": "string"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "object": "list",
  "url": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "charge": "string",
    "code": "string",
    "decline_code": "string",
    "doc_url": "string",
    "message": "string",
```

<h3 id="gettransfers-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error response.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="gettransfers-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[transfer](#schematransfer)]|true|none|Details about each object.|
|has_more|boolean|true|none|True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL where this list can be accessed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|list|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

```bash
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&description=string&destination=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&source_transaction=string&source_type=bank_account&transfer_group=string'
```

`POST /v1/transfers`

<p>To send funds from your Stripe account to a connected account, you create a new transfer object. Your <a href="#balance">Stripe balance</a> must be able to cover the transfer amount, or you’ll receive an “Insufficient Funds” error.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
description: string
destination: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
source_transaction: string
source_type: bank_account
transfer_group: string
```

<h3 id="posttransfers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer in cents (or local equivalent) representing how much to transfer.|
|» currency|body|string|true|3-letter [ISO code for currency](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» destination|body|string|true|The ID of a connected Stripe account. <a href="/docs/connect/charges-transfers">See the Connect documentation</a> for details.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» source_transaction|body|string|false|You can use this parameter to transfer funds from a charge before they are added to your available balance. A pending balance will transfer immediately but the funds will not become available until the original charge becomes available. [See the Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers#transfer-availability) for details.|
|» source_type|body|string|false|The source balance to use for this transfer. One of `bank_account`, `card`, or `fpx`. For most users, this will default to `card`.|
|» transfer_group|body|string|false|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. See the [Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» source_type|bank_account|
|» source_type|card|
|» source_type|fpx|

## PostTransfersIdReversals

<a id="opIdPostTransfersIdReversals"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/transfers/string/reversals \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&description=string&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&refund_application_fee=true'
```

`POST /v1/transfers/{id}/reversals`

<p>When you create a new reversal, you must specify a transfer to create it on.</p>

<p>When reversing transfers, you can optionally reverse part of the transfer. You can do so as many times as you wish until the entire transfer has been reversed.</p>

<p>Once entirely reversed, a transfer can’t be reversed again. This method will return an error when called on an already-reversed transfer, or when trying to reverse more money than is left on a transfer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
description: string
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
refund_application_fee: true
```

<h3 id="posttransfersidreversals-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|A positive integer in cents (or local equivalent) representing how much of this transfer to reverse. Can only reverse up to the unreversed amount remaining of the transfer. Partial transfer reversals are only allowed for transfers to Stripe Accounts. Defaults to the entire transfer amount.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string which you can attach to a reversal object. It is displayed alongside the reversal in the Dashboard. This will be unset if you POST an empty value.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» refund_application_fee|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the application fee should be refunded when reversing this transfer. If a full transfer reversal is given, the full application fee will be refunded. Otherwise, the application fee will be refunded with an amount proportional to the amount of the transfer reversed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|""|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "balance_transaction": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "destination_payment_refund": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "transfer_reversal",
  "source_refund": "string",
  "transfer": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "charge": "string",
    "code": "string",
    "decline_code": "string",
    "doc_url": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "param": "string",
```

## PostTreasuryOutboundPayments

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/treasury/outbound_payments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&customer=string&description=string&destination_payment_method=string&destination_payment_method_data=%7B%22billing_details%22%3A%7B%22address%22%3A%7B%22city%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22country%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22line2%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22postal_code%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22state%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22email%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22phone%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22financial_account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22metadata%22%3A%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D%2C%22type%22%3A%22financial_account%22%2C%22us_bank_account%22%3A%7B%22account_holder_type%22%3A%22company%22%2C%22account_number%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22account_type%22%3A%22checking%22%2C%22financial_connections_account%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22routing_number%22%3A%22string%22%7D%7D&destination_payment_method_options=%7B%22us_bank_account%22%3A%7B%22network%22%3A%22ach%22%7D%7D&end_user_details=%7B%22ip_address%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22present%22%3Atrue%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&financial_account=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&statement_descriptor=string'
```

`POST /v1/treasury/outbound_payments`

<p>Creates an OutboundPayment.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
customer: string
description: string
destination_payment_method: string
destination_payment_method_data:
  billing_details:
    address:
      city: string
      country: string
      line1: string
      line2: string
      postal_code: string
      state: string
    email: string
    name: string
    phone: string
  financial_account: string
  metadata:
    property1: string
    property2: string
  type: financial_account
  us_bank_account:
    account_holder_type: company
    account_number: string
    account_type: checking
    financial_connections_account: string
    routing_number: string
destination_payment_method_options:
  us_bank_account:
    network: ach
end_user_details:
  ip_address: string
  present: true
expand:
  - string
financial_account: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
statement_descriptor: string
```

<h3 id="posttreasuryoutboundpayments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount (in cents) to be transferred.|
|» currency|body|string|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» customer|body|string|false|ID of the customer to whom the OutboundPayment is sent. Must match the Customer attached to the `destination_payment_method` passed in.|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» destination_payment_method|body|string|false|The PaymentMethod to use as the payment instrument for the OutboundPayment. Exclusive with `destination_payment_method_data`.|
|» destination_payment_method_data|body|object|false|Hash used to generate the PaymentMethod to be used for this OutboundPayment. Exclusive with `destination_payment_method`.|
|» » billing_details|body|object|false|none|
|» » » address|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » city|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » country|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » line1|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » postal_code|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » state|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » email|body|string|false|none|

|» » » name|body|string|false|none|

|» » financial_account|body|string|false|none|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » us_bank_account|body|object|false|none|
|» » » account_holder_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » » account_number|body|string|false|none|
|» » » account_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » » financial_connections_account|body|string|false|none|

|» » us_bank_account|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » network|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» financial_account|body|string|true|The FinancialAccount to pull funds from.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|The description that appears on the receiving end for this OutboundPayment (for example, bank statement for external bank transfer). Maximum 10 characters for `ach` payments, 140 characters for `wire` payments, or 500 characters for `stripe` network transfers. The default value is `payment`.|

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/treasury/outbound_transfers \

  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'amount=0&currency=string&description=string&destination_payment_method=string&destination_payment_method_options=%7B%22us_bank_account%22%3A%7B%22network%22%3A%22ach%22%7D%7D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&financial_account=string&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&statement_descriptor=string'
```

`POST /v1/treasury/outbound_transfers`

<p>Creates an OutboundTransfer.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
amount: 0
currency: string
description: string
destination_payment_method: string
destination_payment_method_options:
  us_bank_account:
    network: ach
expand:
  - string
financial_account: string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
statement_descriptor: string
```

<h3 id="posttreasuryoutboundtransfers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Amount (in cents) to be transferred.|
|» currency|body|string|true|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|» description|body|string|false|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|» destination_payment_method|body|string|false|The PaymentMethod to use as the payment instrument for the OutboundTransfer.|
|» destination_payment_method_options|body|object|false|Hash describing payment method configuration details.|
|» » us_bank_account|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » network|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» financial_account|body|string|true|The FinancialAccount to pull funds from.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string|false|Statement descriptor to be shown on the receiving end of an OutboundTransfer. Maximum 10 characters for `ach` transfers or 140 characters for `wire` transfers. The default value is `transfer`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » network|ach|
|» » » network|us_domestic_wire|
|» » » *anyOf*|""|

## PostWebhookEndpoints

<a id="opIdPostWebhookEndpoints"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/webhook_endpoints \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'api_version=2011-01-01&connect=true&description=string&enabled_events=%5B%22*%22%5D&expand=%5B%22string%22%5D&metadata=%7B%22property1%22%3A%22string%22%2C%22property2%22%3A%22string%22%7D&url=string'
```

`POST /v1/webhook_endpoints`

<p>A webhook endpoint must have a <code>url</code> and a list of <code>enabled_events</code>. You may optionally specify the Boolean <code>connect</code> parameter. If set to true, then a Connect webhook endpoint that notifies the specified <code>url</code> about events from all connected accounts is created; otherwise an account webhook endpoint that notifies the specified <code>url</code> only about events from your account is created. You can also create webhook endpoints in the <a href="https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/webhooks">webhooks settings</a> section of the Dashboard.</p>

> Body parameter

```yaml
api_version: "2011-01-01"
connect: true
description: string
enabled_events:
  - "*"
expand:
  - string
metadata:
  property1: string
  property2: string
url: string
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» api_version|body|string|false|Events sent to this endpoint will be generated with this Stripe Version instead of your account's default Stripe Version.|
|» connect|body|boolean|false|Whether this endpoint should receive events from connected accounts (`true`), or from your account (`false`). Defaults to `false`.|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional description of what the webhook is used for.|
|» enabled_events|body|[string]|true|The list of events to enable for this endpoint. You may specify `['*']` to enable all events, except those that require explicit selection.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Specifies which fields in the response should be expanded.|
|» metadata|body|object \| string|false|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

<a id="opIdDeleteWebhookEndpointsWebhookEndpoint"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/webhook_endpoints/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

```json
        "user_agent": "string"
      }
    }
  },
  "tos_acceptance": {
    "date": 0,
    "ip": "string",
    "service_agreement": "string",
    "user_agent": "string"
  },
  "type": "custom"
}
```

This is an object representing a Stripe account. You can retrieve it to see
properties on the account like its current requirements or if the account is
enabled to make live charges or receive payouts.

For Custom accounts, the properties below are always returned. For other accounts, some properties are returned until that
account has started to go through Connect Onboarding. Once you create an [Account Link](https://stripe.com/docs/api/account_links)
for a Standard or Express account, some parameters are no longer returned. These are marked as **Custom Only** or **Custom and Express**
below. Learn about the differences [between accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/accounts).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|business_profile|[account_business_profile](#schemaaccount_business_profile) \| null|false|none|Business information about the account.|
|business_type|string \| null|false|none|The business type.|
|capabilities|[account_capabilities](#schemaaccount_capabilities)|false|none|none|
|charges_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the account can create live charges.|
|company|[legal_entity_company](#schemalegal_entity_company)|false|none|none|
|controller|[account_unification_account_controller](#schemaaccount_unification_account_controller)|false|none|none|
|country|string|false|none|The account's country.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|false|none|Time at which the account was connected. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|default_currency|string|false|none|Three-letter ISO currency code representing the default currency for the account. This must be a currency that [Stripe supports in the account's country](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts).|
|details_submitted|boolean|false|none|Whether account details have been submitted. Standard accounts cannot receive payouts before this is true.|
|email|string \| null|false|none|An email address associated with the account. You can treat this as metadata: it is not used for authentication or messaging account holders.|
|external_accounts|object|false|none|External accounts (bank accounts and debit cards) currently attached to this account|
|future_requirements|[account_future_requirements](#schemaaccount_future_requirements)|false|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|individual|[person](#schemaperson)|false|none|This is an object representing a person associated with a Stripe account.<br><br>A platform cannot access a Standard or Express account's persons after the account starts onboarding, such as after generating an account link for the account.<br>See the [Standard onboarding](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/standard-accounts) or [Express onboarding documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/express-accounts) for information about platform pre-filling and account onboarding steps.<br><br>Related guide: [Handling Identity Verification with the API](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/identity-verification-api#person-information).|
|metadata|object|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payouts_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether Stripe can send payouts to this account.|
|requirements|[account_requirements](#schemaaccount_requirements)|false|none|none|
|settings|[account_settings](#schemaaccount_settings) \| null|false|none|Options for customizing how the account functions within Stripe.|
|tos_acceptance|[account_tos_acceptance](#schemaaccount_tos_acceptance)|false|none|none|
|type|string|false|none|The Stripe account type. Can be `standard`, `express`, or `custom`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|business_type|company|
|business_type|government_entity|
|business_type|individual|
|business_type|non_profit|
|object|account|
|type|custom|
|type|express|
|type|standard|

<h2 id="tocS_account_capability_future_requirements">account_capability_future_requirements</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccount_capability_future_requirements"></a>
<a id="schema_account_capability_future_requirements"></a>
<a id="tocSaccount_capability_future_requirements"></a>

```json
{
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "alternative_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ],
      "original_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "current_deadline": 0,
  "currently_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "disabled_reason": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "invalid_address_city_state_postal_code",
      "reason": "string",
      "requirement": "string"
    }
  ],
  "eventually_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "past_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "pending_verification": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alternatives|[[account_requirements_alternative](#schemaaccount_requirements_alternative)]|false|none|Fields that are due and can be satisfied by providing the corresponding alternative fields instead.|
|current_deadline|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date on which `future_requirements` merges with the main `requirements` hash and `future_requirements` becomes empty. After the transition, `currently_due` requirements may immediately become `past_due`, but the account may also be given a grace period depending on the capability's enablement state prior to transitioning.|
|currently_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that need to be collected to keep the capability enabled. If not collected by `future_requirements[current_deadline]`, these fields will transition to the main `requirements` hash.|
|disabled_reason|string \| null|false|none|This is typed as a string for consistency with `requirements.disabled_reason`, but it safe to assume `future_requirements.disabled_reason` is empty because fields in `future_requirements` will never disable the account.|
|errors|[[account_requirements_error](#schemaaccount_requirements_error)]|true|none|Fields that are `currently_due` and need to be collected again because validation or verification failed.|
|eventually_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that need to be collected assuming all volume thresholds are reached. As they become required, they appear in `currently_due` as well.|
|past_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that weren't collected by `requirements.current_deadline`. These fields need to be collected to enable the capability on the account. New fields will never appear here; `future_requirements.past_due` will always be a subset of `requirements.past_due`.|
|pending_verification|[string]|true|none|Fields that may become required depending on the results of verification or review. Will be an empty array unless an asynchronous verification is pending. If verification fails, these fields move to `eventually_due` or `currently_due`.|

```json
  ],

      "reason": "string",
      "requirement": "string"
    }
  ],

  ],
  "past_due": [
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alternatives|[[account_requirements_alternative](#schemaaccount_requirements_alternative)]|false|none|Fields that are due and can be satisfied by providing the corresponding alternative fields instead.|
|current_deadline|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date by which the fields in `currently_due` must be collected to keep the capability enabled for the account. These fields may disable the capability sooner if the next threshold is reached before they are collected.|
|currently_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that need to be collected to keep the capability enabled. If not collected by `current_deadline`, these fields appear in `past_due` as well, and the capability is disabled.|
|disabled_reason|string \| null|false|none|If the capability is disabled, this string describes why. Can be `requirements.past_due`, `requirements.pending_verification`, `listed`, `platform_paused`, `rejected.fraud`, `rejected.listed`, `rejected.terms_of_service`, `rejected.other`, `under_review`, or `other`.<br><br>`rejected.unsupported_business` means that the account's business is not supported by the capability. For example, payment methods may restrict the businesses they support in their terms of service:<br><br>- [Afterpay Clearpay's terms of service](/afterpay-clearpay/legal#restricted-businesses)<br><br>If you believe that the rejection is in error, please contact support at https://support.stripe.com/contact/ for assistance.|
|errors|[[account_requirements_error](#schemaaccount_requirements_error)]|true|none|Fields that are `currently_due` and need to be collected again because validation or verification failed.|
|eventually_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that need to be collected assuming all volume thresholds are reached. As they become required, they appear in `currently_due` as well, and `current_deadline` becomes set.|
|past_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that weren't collected by `current_deadline`. These fields need to be collected to enable the capability on the account.|
|pending_verification|[string]|true|none|Fields that may become required depending on the results of verification or review. Will be an empty array unless an asynchronous verification is pending. If verification fails, these fields move to `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, or `past_due`.|

<h2 id="tocS_account_future_requirements">account_future_requirements</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccount_future_requirements"></a>
<a id="schema_account_future_requirements"></a>
<a id="tocSaccount_future_requirements"></a>
<a id="tocsaccount_future_requirements"></a>

```json
{
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "alternative_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ],
      "original_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "current_deadline": 0,
  "currently_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "disabled_reason": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "invalid_address_city_state_postal_code",
      "reason": "string",
      "requirement": "string"
    }
  ],
  "eventually_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "past_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "pending_verification": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alternatives|[[account_requirements_alternative](#schemaaccount_requirements_alternative)]|false|none|Fields that are due and can be satisfied by providing the corresponding alternative fields instead.|
|current_deadline|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date on which `future_requirements` merges with the main `requirements` hash and `future_requirements` becomes empty. After the transition, `currently_due` requirements may immediately become `past_due`, but the account may also be given a grace period depending on its enablement state prior to transitioning.|
|currently_due|[string]|false|none|Fields that need to be collected to keep the account enabled. If not collected by `future_requirements[current_deadline]`, these fields will transition to the main `requirements` hash.|
|disabled_reason|string \| null|false|none|This is typed as a string for consistency with `requirements.disabled_reason`, but it safe to assume `future_requirements.disabled_reason` is empty because fields in `future_requirements` will never disable the account.|
|errors|[[account_requirements_error](#schemaaccount_requirements_error)]|false|none|Fields that are `currently_due` and need to be collected again because validation or verification failed.|
|eventually_due|[string]|false|none|Fields that need to be collected assuming all volume thresholds are reached. As they become required, they appear in `currently_due` as well.|
|past_due|[string]|false|none|Fields that weren't collected by `requirements.current_deadline`. These fields need to be collected to enable the capability on the account. New fields will never appear here; `future_requirements.past_due` will always be a subset of `requirements.past_due`.|
|pending_verification|[string]|false|none|Fields that may become required depending on the results of verification or review. Will be an empty array unless an asynchronous verification is pending. If verification fails, these fields move to `eventually_due` or `currently_due`.|

<h2 id="tocS_account_link">account_link</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccount_link"></a>
<a id="schema_account_link"></a>
<a id="tocSaccount_link"></a>
<a id="tocsaccount_link"></a>

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "expires_at": 0,
  "object": "account_link",
  "url": "string"
}
```

Account Links are the means by which a Connect platform grants a connected account permission to access
Stripe-hosted applications, such as Connect Onboarding.

Related guide: [Connect Onboarding](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/connect-onboarding).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The timestamp at which this account link will expire.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL for the account link.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|account_link|

|statement_descriptor_kana|string \| null|false|none|The Kana variation of the default text that appears on credit card statements when a charge is made (Japan only)|
|statement_descriptor_kanji|string \| null|false|none|The Kanji variation of the default text that appears on credit card statements when a charge is made (Japan only)|
|statement_descriptor_prefix_kana|string \| null|false|none|The Kana variation of the default text that appears on credit card statements when a charge is made (Japan only). This field prefixes any dynamic `statement_descriptor_suffix_kana` specified on the charge. `statement_descriptor_prefix_kana` is useful for maximizing descriptor space for the dynamic portion.|
|statement_descriptor_prefix_kanji|string \| null|false|none|The Kanji variation of the default text that appears on credit card statements when a charge is made (Japan only). This field prefixes any dynamic `statement_descriptor_suffix_kanji` specified on the charge. `statement_descriptor_prefix_kanji` is useful for maximizing descriptor space for the dynamic portion.|

<h2 id="tocS_account_requirements">account_requirements</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccount_requirements"></a>
<a id="schema_account_requirements"></a>
<a id="tocSaccount_requirements"></a>
<a id="tocsaccount_requirements"></a>

```json
{
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "alternative_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ],
      "original_fields_due": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "current_deadline": 0,
  "currently_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "disabled_reason": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "invalid_address_city_state_postal_code",
      "reason": "string",
      "requirement": "string"
    }
  ],
  "eventually_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "past_due": [
    "string"
  ],
  "pending_verification": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alternatives|[[account_requirements_alternative](#schemaaccount_requirements_alternative)]|false|none|Fields that are due and can be satisfied by providing the corresponding alternative fields instead.|
|current_deadline|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date by which the fields in `currently_due` must be collected to keep the account enabled. These fields may disable the account sooner if the next threshold is reached before they are collected.|
|currently_due|[string]|false|none|Fields that need to be collected to keep the account enabled. If not collected by `current_deadline`, these fields appear in `past_due` as well, and the account is disabled.|
|disabled_reason|string \| null|false|none|If the account is disabled, this string describes why. Can be `requirements.past_due`, `requirements.pending_verification`, `listed`, `platform_paused`, `rejected.fraud`, `rejected.listed`, `rejected.terms_of_service`, `rejected.other`, `under_review`, or `other`.|
|errors|[[account_requirements_error](#schemaaccount_requirements_error)]|false|none|Fields that are `currently_due` and need to be collected again because validation or verification failed.|
|eventually_due|[string]|false|none|Fields that need to be collected assuming all volume thresholds are reached. As they become required, they appear in `currently_due` as well, and `current_deadline` becomes set.|
|past_due|[string]|false|none|Fields that weren't collected by `current_deadline`. These fields need to be collected to enable the account.|
|pending_verification|[string]|false|none|Fields that may become required depending on the results of verification or review. Will be an empty array unless an asynchronous verification is pending. If verification fails, these fields move to `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, or `past_due`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|charge|string|false|none|For card errors, the ID of the failed charge.|
|code|string|false|none|For some errors that could be handled programmatically, a short string indicating the [error code](https://stripe.com/docs/error-codes) reported.|
|decline_code|string|false|none|For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating the [card issuer's reason for the decline](https://stripe.com/docs/declines#issuer-declines) if they provide one.|
|doc_url|string|false|none|A URL to more information about the [error code](https://stripe.com/docs/error-codes) reported.|
|message|string|false|none|A human-readable message providing more details about the error. For card errors, these messages can be shown to your users.|
|param|string|false|none|If the error is parameter-specific, the parameter related to the error. For example, you can use this to display a message near the correct form field.|
|payment_intent|[payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|false|none|A PaymentIntent guides you through the process of collecting a payment from your customer.<br>We recommend that you create exactly one PaymentIntent for each order or<br>customer session in your system. You can reference the PaymentIntent later to<br>see the history of payment attempts for a particular session.<br><br>A PaymentIntent transitions through<br>[multiple statuses](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/intents#intent-statuses)<br>throughout its lifetime as it interfaces with Stripe.js to perform<br>authentication flows and ultimately creates at most one successful charge.<br><br>Related guide: [Payment Intents API](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/payment-intents).|
|payment_method|[payment_method](#schemapayment_method)|false|none|PaymentMethod objects represent your customer's payment instruments.<br>You can use them with [PaymentIntents](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/payment-intents) to collect payments or save them to<br>Customer objects to store instrument details for future payments.<br><br>Related guides: [Payment Methods](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/payment-methods) and [More Payment Scenarios](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/more-payment-scenarios).|
|payment_method_type|string|false|none|If the error is specific to the type of payment method, the payment method type that had a problem. This field is only populated for invoice-related errors.|
|request_log_url|string|false|none|A URL to the request log entry in your dashboard.|
|setup_intent|[setup_intent](#schemasetup_intent)|false|none|A SetupIntent guides you through the process of setting up and saving a customer's payment credentials for future payments.<br>For example, you could use a SetupIntent to set up and save your customer's card without immediately collecting a payment.<br>Later, you can use [PaymentIntents](https://stripe.com/docs/api#payment_intents) to drive the payment flow.<br><br>Create a SetupIntent as soon as you're ready to collect your customer's payment credentials.<br>Do not maintain long-lived, unconfirmed SetupIntents as they may no longer be valid.<br>The SetupIntent then transitions through multiple [statuses](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/intents#intent-statuses) as it guides<br>you through the setup process.<br><br>Successful SetupIntents result in payment credentials that are optimized for future payments.<br>For example, cardholders in [certain regions](/guides/strong-customer-authentication) may need to be run through<br>[Strong Customer Authentication](https://stripe.com/docs/strong-customer-authentication) at the time of payment method collection<br>in order to streamline later [off-session payments](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/setup-intents).<br>If the SetupIntent is used with a [Customer](https://stripe.com/docs/api#setup_intent_object-customer), upon success,<br>it will automatically attach the resulting payment method to that Customer.<br>We recommend using SetupIntents or [setup_future_usage](https://stripe.com/docs/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) on<br>PaymentIntents to save payment methods in order to prevent saving invalid or unoptimized payment methods.<br><br>By using SetupIntents, you ensure that your customers experience the minimum set of required friction,<br>even as regulations change over time.<br><br>Related guide: [Setup Intents API](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/setup-intents).|
|source|[bank_account](#schemabank_account) \| [card](#schemacard) \| [source](#schemasource)|false|none|The source object for errors returned on a request involving a source.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of error returned. One of `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, or `invalid_request_error`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|api_error|
|type|card_error|
|type|idempotency_error|
|type|invalid_request_error|

<h2 id="tocS_apps.secret">apps.secret</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaapps.secret"></a>
<a id="schema_apps.secret"></a>
<a id="tocSapps.secret"></a>
<a id="tocsapps.secret"></a>

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "deleted": true,
  "expires_at": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "name": "string",
  "object": "apps.secret",
  "payload": "string",
  "scope": {
    "type": "account",
    "user": "string"
  }
}
```

Secret Store is an API that allows Stripe Apps developers to securely persist secrets for use by UI Extensions and app backends.

The primary resource in Secret Store is a `secret`. Other apps can't view secrets created by an app. Additionally, secrets are scoped to provide further permission control.

All Dashboard users and the app backend share `account` scoped secrets. Use the `account` scope for secrets that don't change per-user, like a third-party API key.

A `user` scoped secret is accessible by the app backend and one specific Dashboard user. Use the `user` scope for per-user secrets like per-user OAuth tokens, where different users might have different permissions.

Related guide: [Store data between page reloads](https://stripe.com/docs/stripe-apps/store-auth-data-custom-objects).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|deleted|boolean|false|none|If true, indicates that this secret has been deleted|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|The Unix timestamp for the expiry time of the secret, after which the secret deletes.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|name|string|true|none|A name for the secret that's unique within the scope.|
