<h2 id="tocS_balance">balance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabalance"></a>
<a id="schema_balance"></a>
<a id="tocSbalance"></a>
<a id="tocsbalance"></a>

```json
{
  "available": [
    {
      "amount": 0,
      "currency": "string",
      "source_types": {
        "bank_account": 0,
        "card": 0,
        "fpx": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "connect_reserved": [
    {
      "amount": 0,
      "currency": "string",
      "source_types": {
        "bank_account": 0,
        "card": 0,
        "fpx": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "instant_available": [
    {
      "amount": 0,
      "currency": "string",
      "source_types": {
        "bank_account": 0,
        "card": 0,
        "fpx": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "issuing": {
    "available": [
      {
        "amount": 0,
        "currency": "string",
        "source_types": {
          "bank_account": 0,
          "card": 0,
          "fpx": 0
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "balance",
  "pending": [
    {
      "amount": 0,
      "currency": "string",
      "source_types": {
        "bank_account": 0,
        "card": 0,
        "fpx": 0
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

This is an object representing your Stripe balance. You can retrieve it to see
the balance currently on your Stripe account.

You can also retrieve the balance history, which contains a list of
[transactions](https://stripe.com/docs/reporting/balance-transaction-types) that contributed to the balance
(charges, payouts, and so forth).

The available and pending amounts for each currency are broken down further by
payment source types.

Related guide: [Understanding Connect Account Balances](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/account-balances).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|available|[[balance_amount](#schemabalance_amount)]|true|none|Funds that are available to be transferred or paid out, whether automatically by Stripe or explicitly via the [Transfers API](https://stripe.com/docs/api#transfers) or [Payouts API](https://stripe.com/docs/api#payouts). The available balance for each currency and payment type can be found in the `source_types` property.|
|connect_reserved|[[balance_amount](#schemabalance_amount)]|false|none|Funds held due to negative balances on connected Custom accounts. The connect reserve balance for each currency and payment type can be found in the `source_types` property.|
|instant_available|[[balance_amount](#schemabalance_amount)]|false|none|Funds that can be paid out using Instant Payouts.|
|issuing|[balance_detail](#schemabalance_detail)|false|none|none|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|pending|[[balance_amount](#schemabalance_amount)]|true|none|Funds that are not yet available in the balance, due to the 7-day rolling pay cycle. The pending balance for each currency, and for each payment type, can be found in the `source_types` property.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|balance|

<h2 id="tocS_balance_transaction">balance_transaction</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabalance_transaction"></a>
<a id="schema_balance_transaction"></a>
<a id="tocSbalance_transaction"></a>
<a id="tocsbalance_transaction"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "available_on": 0,
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "exchange_rate": 0,
  "fee": 0,
  "fee_details": [
    {
      "amount": 0,
      "application": "string",
      "currency": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "net": 0,
  "object": "balance_transaction",
  "reporting_category": "string",
  "source": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "type": "adjustment"
}
```

Balance transactions represent funds moving through your Stripe account.
They're created for every type of transaction that comes into or flows out of your Stripe account balance.

Related guide: [Balance Transaction Types](https://stripe.com/docs/reports/balance-transaction-types).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Gross amount of the transaction, in %s.|
|available_on|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The date the transaction's net funds will become available in the Stripe balance.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|exchange_rate|number \| null|false|none|The exchange rate used, if applicable, for this transaction. Specifically, if money was converted from currency A to currency B, then the `amount` in currency A, times `exchange_rate`, would be the `amount` in currency B. For example, suppose you charged a customer 10.00 EUR. Then the PaymentIntent's `amount` would be `1000` and `currency` would be `eur`. Suppose this was converted into 12.34 USD in your Stripe account. Then the BalanceTransaction's `amount` would be `1234`, `currency` would be `usd`, and `exchange_rate` would be `1.234`.|
|fee|integer|true|none|Fees (in %s) paid for this transaction.|
|fee_details|[[fee](#schemafee)]|true|none|Detailed breakdown of fees (in %s) paid for this transaction.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|net|integer|true|none|Net amount of the transaction, in %s.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|reporting_category|string|true|none|[Learn more](https://stripe.com/docs/reports/reporting-categories) about how reporting categories can help you understand balance transactions from an accounting perspective.|
|source|string \| [application_fee](#schemaapplication_fee) \| [charge](#schemacharge) \| [connect_collection_transfer](#schemaconnect_collection_transfer) \| [dispute](#schemadispute) \| [fee_refund](#schemafee_refund) \| [issuing.authorization](#schemaissuing.authorization) \| [issuing.dispute](#schemaissuing.dispute) \| [issuing.transaction](#schemaissuing.transaction) \| [payout](#schemapayout) \| [platform_tax_fee](#schemaplatform_tax_fee) \| [refund](#schemarefund) \| [reserve_transaction](#schemareserve_transaction) \| [tax_deducted_at_source](#schematax_deducted_at_source) \| [topup](#schematopup) \| [transfer](#schematransfer) \| [transfer_reversal](#schematransfer_reversal) \| null|false|none|The Stripe object to which this transaction is related.|
|status|string|true|none|If the transaction's net funds are available in the Stripe balance yet. Either `available` or `pending`.|
|type|string|true|none|Transaction type: `adjustment`, `advance`, `advance_funding`, `anticipation_repayment`, `application_fee`, `application_fee_refund`, `charge`, `connect_collection_transfer`, `contribution`, `issuing_authorization_hold`, `issuing_authorization_release`, `issuing_dispute`, `issuing_transaction`, `payment`, `payment_failure_refund`, `payment_refund`, `payout`, `payout_cancel`, `payout_failure`, `refund`, `refund_failure`, `reserve_transaction`, `reserved_funds`, `stripe_fee`, `stripe_fx_fee`, `tax_fee`, `topup`, `topup_reversal`, `transfer`, `transfer_cancel`, `transfer_failure`, or `transfer_refund`. [Learn more](https://stripe.com/docs/reports/balance-transaction-types) about balance transaction types and what they represent. If you are looking to classify transactions for accounting purposes, you might want to consider `reporting_category` instead.|

<h2 id="tocS_bank_account">bank_account</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabank_account"></a>
<a id="schema_bank_account"></a>
<a id="tocSbank_account"></a>
<a id="tocsbank_account"></a>

```json
{
  "account": "string",
  "account_holder_name": "string",
  "account_holder_type": "string",
  "account_type": "string",
  "available_payout_methods": [
    "instant"
  ],
  "bank_name": "string",
  "country": "string",
  "currency": "string",
  "customer": "string",
  "default_for_currency": true,
  "fingerprint": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "last4": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "bank_account",
  "routing_number": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

These bank accounts are payment methods on `Customer` objects.

On the other hand [External Accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/api#external_accounts) are transfer
destinations on `Account` objects for [Custom accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/custom-accounts).
They can be bank accounts or debit cards as well, and are documented in the links above.

Related guide: [Bank Debits and Transfers](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/bank-debits-transfers).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The ID of the account that the bank account is associated with.|
|account_holder_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the person or business that owns the bank account.|
|account_holder_type|string \| null|false|none|The type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`.|
|account_type|string \| null|false|none|The bank account type. This can only be `checking` or `savings` in most countries. In Japan, this can only be `futsu` or `toza`.|
|available_payout_methods|[string]|false|none|A set of available payout methods for this bank account. Only values from this set should be passed as the `method` when creating a payout.|
|bank_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the bank associated with the routing number (e.g., `WELLS FARGO`).|
|country|string|true|none|Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts) paid out to the bank account.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The ID of the customer that the bank account is associated with.|
|default_for_currency|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this bank account is the default external account for its currency.|
|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|last4|string|true|none|The last four digits of the bank account number.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|routing_number|string \| null|false|none|The routing transit number for the bank account.|
|status|string|true|none|For bank accounts, possible values are `new`, `validated`, `verified`, `verification_failed`, or `errored`. A bank account that hasn't had any activity or validation performed is `new`. If Stripe can determine that the bank account exists, its status will be `validated`. Note that there often isn’t enough information to know (e.g., for smaller credit unions), and the validation is not always run. If customer bank account verification has succeeded, the bank account status will be `verified`. If the verification failed for any reason, such as microdeposit failure, the status will be `verification_failed`. If a transfer sent to this bank account fails, we'll set the status to `errored` and will not continue to send transfers until the bank details are updated.<br><br>For external accounts, possible values are `new` and `errored`. Validations aren't run against external accounts because they're only used for payouts. This means the other statuses don't apply. If a transfer fails, the status is set to `errored` and transfers are stopped until account details are updated.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|available_payout_methods|instant|
|available_payout_methods|standard|
|object|bank_account|

<h2 id="tocS_billing_portal.session">billing_portal.session</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabilling_portal.session"></a>
<a id="schema_billing_portal.session"></a>

```json
  "created": 0,
  "customer": "string",
  "flow": {
    "after_completion": {
      "hosted_confirmation": {
        "custom_message": "string"
      },
      "redirect": {
        "return_url": "string"
      },

    },
    "subscription_cancel": {
      "subscription": "string"
    },
    "type": "payment_method_update"
  },
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "locale": "auto",
  "object": "billing_portal.session",
  "on_behalf_of": "string",
  "return_url": "string",
  "url": "string"
}
```

The Billing customer portal is a Stripe-hosted UI for subscription and
billing management.

A portal configuration describes the functionality and features that you
want to provide to your customers through the portal.

A portal session describes the instantiation of the customer portal for
a particular customer. By visiting the session's URL, the customer
can manage their subscriptions and billing details. For security reasons,
sessions are short-lived and will expire if the customer does not visit the URL.
Create sessions on-demand when customers intend to manage their subscriptions
and billing details.

Learn more in the [integration guide](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/integrating-customer-portal).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|configuration|string \| [billing_portal.configuration](#schemabilling_portal.configuration)|true|none|The configuration used by this session, describing the features available.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer|string|true|none|The ID of the customer for this session.|
|flow|[portal_flows_flow](#schemaportal_flows_flow) \| null|false|none|Information about a specific flow for the customer to go through. See the [docs](https://stripe.com/docs/customer-management/portal-deep-links) to learn more about using customer portal deep links and flows.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|locale|string \| null|false|none|The IETF language tag of the locale Customer Portal is displayed in. If blank or auto, the customer’s `preferred_locales` or browser’s locale is used.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| null|false|none|The account for which the session was created on behalf of. When specified, only subscriptions and invoices with this `on_behalf_of` account appear in the portal. For more information, see the [docs](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers#on-behalf-of). Use the [Accounts API](https://stripe.com/docs/api/accounts/object#account_object-settings-branding) to modify the `on_behalf_of` account's branding settings, which the portal displays.|
|return_url|string \| null|false|none|The URL to redirect customers to when they click on the portal's link to return to your website.|
|url|string|true|none|The short-lived URL of the session that gives customers access to the customer portal.|

You can store multiple cards on a customer in order to charge the customer
later. You can also store multiple debit cards on a recipient in order to
transfer to those cards later.

Related guide: [Card Payments with Sources](https://stripe.com/docs/sources/cards).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account this card belongs to. This attribute will not be in the card object if the card belongs to a customer or recipient instead.|
|address_city|string \| null|false|none|City/District/Suburb/Town/Village.|
|address_country|string \| null|false|none|Billing address country, if provided when creating card.|
|address_line1|string \| null|false|none|Address line 1 (Street address/PO Box/Company name).|
|address_line1_check|string \| null|false|none|If `address_line1` was provided, results of the check: `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.|
|address_line2|string \| null|false|none|Address line 2 (Apartment/Suite/Unit/Building).|
|address_state|string \| null|false|none|State/County/Province/Region.|
|address_zip|string \| null|false|none|ZIP or postal code.|
|address_zip_check|string \| null|false|none|If `address_zip` was provided, results of the check: `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.|
|available_payout_methods|[string]|false|none|A set of available payout methods for this card. Only values from this set should be passed as the `method` when creating a payout.|
|brand|string|true|none|Card brand. Can be `American Express`, `Diners Club`, `Discover`, `JCB`, `MasterCard`, `UnionPay`, `Visa`, or `Unknown`.|
|country|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.|
|currency|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter [ISO code for currency](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts). Only applicable on accounts (not customers or recipients). The card can be used as a transfer destination for funds in this currency.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The customer that this card belongs to. This attribute will not be in the card object if the card belongs to an account or recipient instead.|
|cvc_check|string \| null|false|none|If a CVC was provided, results of the check: `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`. A result of unchecked indicates that CVC was provided but hasn't been checked yet. Checks are typically performed when attaching a card to a Customer object, or when creating a charge. For more details, see [Check if a card is valid without a charge](https://support.stripe.com/questions/check-if-a-card-is-valid-without-a-charge).|
|default_for_currency|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this card is the default external account for its currency.|
|dynamic_last4|string \| null|false|none|(For tokenized numbers only.) The last four digits of the device account number.|
|exp_month|integer|true|none|Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.|
|exp_year|integer|true|none|Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.|
|fingerprint|string \| null|false|none|Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.<br><br>*Starting May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect will change to allow two fingerprints for the same card --- one for India and one for the rest of the world.*|
|funding|string|true|none|Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|last4|string|true|none|The last four digits of the card.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|Cardholder name.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|status|string \| null|false|none|For external accounts, possible values are `new` and `errored`. If a transfer fails, the status is set to `errored` and transfers are stopped until account details are updated.|
|tokenization_method|string \| null|false|none|If the card number is tokenized, this is the method that was used. Can be `android_pay` (includes Google Pay), `apple_pay`, `masterpass`, `visa_checkout`, or null.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|available_payout_methods|instant|
|available_payout_methods|standard|
|object|card|

To charge a credit or a debit card, you create a `Charge` object. You can
retrieve and refund individual charges as well as list all charges. Charges
are identified by a unique, random ID.

Related guide: [Accept a payment with the Charges API](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/accept-a-payment-charges).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount intended to be collected by this payment. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).|
|amount_captured|integer|true|none|Amount in %s captured (can be less than the amount attribute on the charge if a partial capture was made).|
|amount_refunded|integer|true|none|Amount in %s refunded (can be less than the amount attribute on the charge if a partial refund was issued).|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect application that created the charge.|
|application_fee|string \| [application_fee](#schemaapplication_fee) \| null|false|none|The application fee (if any) for the charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/direct-charges#collecting-fees) for details.|
|application_fee_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The amount of the application fee (if any) requested for the charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/direct-charges#collecting-fees) for details.|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this charge on your account balance (not including refunds or disputes).|
|billing_details|[billing_details](#schemabilling_details)|true|none|none|
|calculated_statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|The full statement descriptor that is passed to card networks, and that is displayed on your customers' credit card and bank statements. Allows you to see what the statement descriptor looks like after the static and dynamic portions are combined.|
|captured|boolean|true|none|If the charge was created without capturing, this Boolean represents whether it is still uncaptured or has since been captured.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|ID of the customer this charge is for if one exists.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|disputed|boolean|true|none|Whether the charge has been disputed.|
|failure_balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|ID of the balance transaction that describes the reversal of the balance on your account due to payment failure.|
|failure_code|string \| null|false|none|Error code explaining reason for charge failure if available (see [the errors section](https://stripe.com/docs/error-codes) for a list of codes).|
|failure_message|string \| null|false|none|Message to user further explaining reason for charge failure if available.|
|fraud_details|[charge_fraud_details](#schemacharge_fraud_details) \| null|false|none|Information on fraud assessments for the charge.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice|string \| [invoice](#schemainvoice) \| null|false|none|ID of the invoice this charge is for if one exists.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the charge was made on behalf of without triggering an automatic transfer. See the [Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers) for details.|
|outcome|[charge_outcome](#schemacharge_outcome) \| null|false|none|Details about whether the payment was accepted, and why. See [understanding declines](https://stripe.com/docs/declines) for details.|
|paid|boolean|true|none|`true` if the charge succeeded, or was successfully authorized for later capture.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent) \| null|false|none|ID of the PaymentIntent associated with this charge, if one exists.|
|payment_method|string \| null|false|none|ID of the payment method used in this charge.|
|payment_method_details|[payment_method_details](#schemapayment_method_details) \| null|false|none|Details about the payment method at the time of the transaction.|
|radar_options|[radar_radar_options](#schemaradar_radar_options)|false|none|Options to configure Radar. See [Radar Session](https://stripe.com/docs/radar/radar-session) for more information.|
|receipt_email|string \| null|false|none|This is the email address that the receipt for this charge was sent to.|
|receipt_number|string \| null|false|none|This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this charge. This attribute will be `null` until a receipt has been sent.|
|receipt_url|string \| null|false|none|This is the URL to view the receipt for this charge. The receipt is kept up-to-date to the latest state of the charge, including any refunds. If the charge is for an Invoice, the receipt will be stylized as an Invoice receipt.|
|refunded|boolean|true|none|Whether the charge has been fully refunded. If the charge is only partially refunded, this attribute will still be false.|
|refunds|object \| null|false|none|A list of refunds that have been applied to the charge.|
|review|string \| [review](#schemareview) \| null|false|none|ID of the review associated with this charge if one exists.|
|shipping|[shipping](#schemashipping) \| null|false|none|Shipping information for the charge.|
|source_transfer|string \| [transfer](#schematransfer) \| null|false|none|The transfer ID which created this charge. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account. [See the Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/destination-charges) for details.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|For card charges, use `statement_descriptor_suffix` instead. Otherwise, you can use this value as the complete description of a charge on your customers’ statements. Must contain at least one letter, maximum 22 characters.|
|statement_descriptor_suffix|string \| null|false|none|Provides information about the charge that customers see on their statements. Concatenated with the prefix (shortened descriptor) or statement descriptor that’s set on the account to form the complete statement descriptor. Maximum 22 characters for the concatenated descriptor.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the payment is either `succeeded`, `pending`, or `failed`.|
|transfer|string \| [transfer](#schematransfer)|false|none|ID of the transfer to the `destination` account (only applicable if the charge was created using the `destination` parameter).|
|transfer_data|[charge_transfer_data](#schemacharge_transfer_data) \| null|false|none|An optional dictionary including the account to automatically transfer to as part of a destination charge. [See the Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/destination-charges) for details.|
|transfer_group|string \| null|false|none|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. See the [Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|charge|
|status|failed|
|status|pending|
|status|succeeded|

<h2 id="tocS_charge_fraud_details">charge_fraud_details</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacharge_fraud_details"></a>
<a id="schema_charge_fraud_details"></a>
<a id="tocScharge_fraud_details"></a>
<a id="tocscharge_fraud_details"></a>

```json
{
  "stripe_report": "string",
  "user_report": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stripe_report|string|false|none|Assessments from Stripe. If set, the value is `fraudulent`.|
|user_report|string|false|none|Assessments reported by you. If set, possible values of are `safe` and `fraudulent`.|

<h2 id="tocS_charge_outcome">charge_outcome</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacharge_outcome"></a>
<a id="schema_charge_outcome"></a>
<a id="tocScharge_outcome"></a>
<a id="tocscharge_outcome"></a>

```json
{
  "network_status": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "risk_level": "string",
  "risk_score": 0,
  "rule": "string",
  "seller_message": "string",
  "type": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|network_status|string \| null|false|none|Possible values are `approved_by_network`, `declined_by_network`, `not_sent_to_network`, and `reversed_after_approval`. The value `reversed_after_approval` indicates the payment was [blocked by Stripe](https://stripe.com/docs/declines#blocked-payments) after bank authorization, and may temporarily appear as "pending" on a cardholder's statement.|
|reason|string \| null|false|none|An enumerated value providing a more detailed explanation of the outcome's `type`. Charges blocked by Radar's default block rule have the value `highest_risk_level`. Charges placed in review by Radar's default review rule have the value `elevated_risk_level`. Charges authorized, blocked, or placed in review by custom rules have the value `rule`. See [understanding declines](https://stripe.com/docs/declines) for more details.|
|risk_level|string|false|none|Stripe Radar's evaluation of the riskiness of the payment. Possible values for evaluated payments are `normal`, `elevated`, `highest`. For non-card payments, and card-based payments predating the public assignment of risk levels, this field will have the value `not_assessed`. In the event of an error in the evaluation, this field will have the value `unknown`. This field is only available with Radar.|
|risk_score|integer|false|none|Stripe Radar's evaluation of the riskiness of the payment. Possible values for evaluated payments are between 0 and 100. For non-card payments, card-based payments predating the public assignment of risk scores, or in the event of an error during evaluation, this field will not be present. This field is only available with Radar for Fraud Teams.|
|rule|string \| [rule](#schemarule)|false|none|The ID of the Radar rule that matched the payment, if applicable.|
|seller_message|string \| null|false|none|A human-readable description of the outcome type and reason, designed for you (the recipient of the payment), not your customer.|
|type|string|true|none|Possible values are `authorized`, `manual_review`, `issuer_declined`, `blocked`, and `invalid`. See [understanding declines](https://stripe.com/docs/declines) and [Radar reviews](https://stripe.com/docs/radar/reviews) for details.|

<h2 id="tocS_charge_transfer_data">charge_transfer_data</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacharge_transfer_data"></a>
<a id="schema_charge_transfer_data"></a>
<a id="tocScharge_transfer_data"></a>
<a id="tocscharge_transfer_data"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "destination": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer \| null|false|none|The amount transferred to the destination account, if specified. By default, the entire charge amount is transferred to the destination account.|
|destination|string \| [account](#schemaaccount)|true|none|ID of an existing, connected Stripe account to transfer funds to if `transfer_data` was specified in the charge request.|

A Checkout Session represents your customer's session as they pay for
one-time purchases or subscriptions through [Checkout](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/checkout)
or [Payment Links](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/payment-links). We recommend creating a
new Session each time your customer attempts to pay.

Once payment is successful, the Checkout Session will contain a reference
to the [Customer](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers), and either the successful
[PaymentIntent](https://stripe.com/docs/api/payment_intents) or an active
[Subscription](https://stripe.com/docs/api/subscriptions).

You can create a Checkout Session on your server and redirect to its URL
to begin Checkout.

Related guide: [Checkout Quickstart](https://stripe.com/docs/checkout/quickstart).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_expiration|[payment_pages_checkout_session_after_expiration](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_after_expiration) \| null|false|none|When set, provides configuration for actions to take if this Checkout Session expires.|
|allow_promotion_codes|boolean \| null|false|none|Enables user redeemable promotion codes.|
|amount_subtotal|integer \| null|false|none|Total of all items before discounts or taxes are applied.|
|amount_total|integer \| null|false|none|Total of all items after discounts and taxes are applied.|
|automatic_tax|[payment_pages_checkout_session_automatic_tax](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_automatic_tax)|true|none|none|
|billing_address_collection|string \| null|false|none|Describes whether Checkout should collect the customer's billing address.|
|cancel_url|string \| null|false|none|If set, Checkout displays a back button and customers will be directed to this URL if they decide to cancel payment and return to your website.|
|client_reference_id|string \| null|false|none|A unique string to reference the Checkout Session. This can be a<br>customer ID, a cart ID, or similar, and can be used to reconcile the<br>Session with your internal systems.|
|consent|[payment_pages_checkout_session_consent](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_consent) \| null|false|none|Results of `consent_collection` for this session.|
|consent_collection|[payment_pages_checkout_session_consent_collection](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_consent_collection) \| null|false|none|When set, provides configuration for the Checkout Session to gather active consent from customers.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|custom_fields|[[payment_pages_checkout_session_custom_fields](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_custom_fields)]|true|none|Collect additional information from your customer using custom fields. Up to 2 fields are supported.|
|custom_text|[payment_pages_checkout_session_custom_text](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_custom_text)|true|none|none|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The ID of the customer for this Session.<br>For Checkout Sessions in `payment` or `subscription` mode, Checkout<br>will create a new customer object based on information provided<br>during the payment flow unless an existing customer was provided when<br>the Session was created.|
|customer_creation|string \| null|false|none|Configure whether a Checkout Session creates a Customer when the Checkout Session completes.|
|customer_details|[payment_pages_checkout_session_customer_details](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_customer_details) \| null|false|none|The customer details including the customer's tax exempt status and the customer's tax IDs. Only the customer's email is present on Sessions in `setup` mode.|
|customer_email|string \| null|false|none|If provided, this value will be used when the Customer object is created.<br>If not provided, customers will be asked to enter their email address.<br>Use this parameter to prefill customer data if you already have an email<br>on file. To access information about the customer once the payment flow is<br>complete, use the `customer` attribute.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The timestamp at which the Checkout Session will expire.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice|string \| [invoice](#schemainvoice) \| null|false|none|ID of the invoice created by the Checkout Session, if it exists.|
|invoice_creation|[payment_pages_checkout_session_invoice_creation](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_invoice_creation) \| null|false|none|Details on the state of invoice creation for the Checkout Session.|
|line_items|object|false|none|The line items purchased by the customer.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|locale|string \| null|false|none|The IETF language tag of the locale Checkout is displayed in. If blank or `auto`, the browser's locale is used.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|mode|string|true|none|The mode of the Checkout Session.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent) \| null|false|none|The ID of the PaymentIntent for Checkout Sessions in `payment` mode.|
|payment_link|string \| [payment_link](#schemapayment_link) \| null|false|none|The ID of the Payment Link that created this Session.|
|payment_method_collection|string \| null|false|none|Configure whether a Checkout Session should collect a payment method.|
|payment_method_options|[checkout_session_payment_method_options](#schemacheckout_session_payment_method_options) \| null|false|none|Payment-method-specific configuration for the PaymentIntent or SetupIntent of this CheckoutSession.|
|payment_method_types|[string]|true|none|A list of the types of payment methods (e.g. card) this Checkout<br>Session is allowed to accept.|
|payment_status|string|true|none|The payment status of the Checkout Session, one of `paid`, `unpaid`, or `no_payment_required`.<br>You can use this value to decide when to fulfill your customer's order.|
|phone_number_collection|[payment_pages_checkout_session_phone_number_collection](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_phone_number_collection)|false|none|none|
|recovered_from|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the original expired Checkout Session that triggered the recovery flow.|
|setup_intent|string \| [setup_intent](#schemasetup_intent) \| null|false|none|The ID of the SetupIntent for Checkout Sessions in `setup` mode.|
|shipping_address_collection|[payment_pages_checkout_session_shipping_address_collection](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_shipping_address_collection) \| null|false|none|When set, provides configuration for Checkout to collect a shipping address from a customer.|
|shipping_cost|[payment_pages_checkout_session_shipping_cost](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_shipping_cost) \| null|false|none|The details of the customer cost of shipping, including the customer chosen ShippingRate.|
|shipping_details|[shipping](#schemashipping) \| null|false|none|Shipping information for this Checkout Session.|
|shipping_options|[[payment_pages_checkout_session_shipping_option](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_shipping_option)]|true|none|The shipping rate options applied to this Session.|
|status|string \| null|false|none|The status of the Checkout Session, one of `open`, `complete`, or `expired`.|
|submit_type|string \| null|false|none|Describes the type of transaction being performed by Checkout in order to customize<br>relevant text on the page, such as the submit button. `submit_type` can only be<br>specified on Checkout Sessions in `payment` mode, but not Checkout Sessions<br>in `subscription` or `setup` mode.|
|subscription|string \| [subscription](#schemasubscription) \| null|false|none|The ID of the subscription for Checkout Sessions in `subscription` mode.|
|success_url|string|true|none|The URL the customer will be directed to after the payment or<br>subscription creation is successful.|
|tax_id_collection|[payment_pages_checkout_session_tax_id_collection](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_tax_id_collection)|false|none|none|
|total_details|[payment_pages_checkout_session_total_details](#schemapayment_pages_checkout_session_total_details) \| null|false|none|Tax and discount details for the computed total amount.|
|url|string \| null|false|none|The URL to the Checkout Session. Redirect customers to this URL to take them to Checkout. If you’re using [Custom Domains](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/checkout/custom-domains), the URL will use your subdomain. Otherwise, it’ll use `checkout.stripe.com.`<br>This value is only present when the session is active.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expires_after_days|integer|true|none|The number of calendar days before a Boleto voucher expires. For example, if you create a Boleto voucher on Monday and you set expires_after_days to 2, the Boleto voucher will expire on Wednesday at 23:59 America/Sao_Paulo time.|
|setup_future_usage|string|false|none|Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.<br><br>Providing this parameter will [attach the payment method](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/save-during-payment) to the PaymentIntent's Customer, if present, after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete. If no Customer was provided, the payment method can still be [attached](https://stripe.com/docs/api/payment_methods/attach) to a Customer after the transaction completes.<br><br>When processing card payments, Stripe also uses `setup_future_usage` to dynamically optimize your payment flow and comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](https://stripe.com/docs/strong-customer-authentication).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|setup_future_usage|none|
|setup_future_usage|off_session|
|setup_future_usage|on_session|

Stripe needs to collect certain pieces of information about each account
created. These requirements can differ depending on the account's country. The
Country Specs API makes these rules available to your integration.

You can also view the information from this API call as [an online
guide](/docs/connect/required-verification-information).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|default_currency|string|true|none|The default currency for this country. This applies to both payment methods and bank accounts.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object. Represented as the ISO country code for this country.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|supported_bank_account_currencies|object|true|none|Currencies that can be accepted in the specific country (for transfers).|
|supported_payment_currencies|[string]|true|none|Currencies that can be accepted in the specified country (for payments).|
|supported_payment_methods|[string]|true|none|Payment methods available in the specified country. You may need to enable some payment methods (e.g., [ACH](https://stripe.com/docs/ach)) on your account before they appear in this list. The `stripe` payment method refers to [charging through your platform](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/destination-charges).|
|supported_transfer_countries|[string]|true|none|Countries that can accept transfers from the specified country.|
|verification_fields|[country_spec_verification_fields](#schemacountry_spec_verification_fields)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|country_spec|

<h2 id="tocS_coupon">coupon</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacoupon"></a>

```json
    }

  "duration_in_months": 0,

  "times_redeemed": 0,
  "valid": true
}
```

A coupon contains information about a percent-off or amount-off discount you
might want to apply to a customer. Coupons may be applied to [subscriptions](https://stripe.com/docs/api#subscriptions), [invoices](https://stripe.com/docs/api#invoices),
[checkout sessions](https://stripe.com/docs/api/checkout/sessions), [quotes](https://stripe.com/docs/api#quotes), and more. Coupons do not work with conventional one-off [charges](https://stripe.com/docs/api#create_charge) or [payment intents](https://stripe.com/docs/api/payment_intents).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount_off|integer \| null|false|none|Amount (in the `currency` specified) that will be taken off the subtotal of any invoices for this customer.|
|applies_to|[coupon_applies_to](#schemacoupon_applies_to)|false|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string \| null|false|none|If `amount_off` has been set, the three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies) of the amount to take off.|
|currency_options|object|false|none|Coupons defined in each available currency option. Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|duration|string|true|none|One of `forever`, `once`, and `repeating`. Describes how long a customer who applies this coupon will get the discount.|
|duration_in_months|integer \| null|false|none|If `duration` is `repeating`, the number of months the coupon applies. Null if coupon `duration` is `forever` or `once`.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|max_redemptions|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum number of times this coupon can be redeemed, in total, across all customers, before it is no longer valid.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the coupon displayed to customers on for instance invoices or receipts.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|percent_off|number \| null|false|none|Percent that will be taken off the subtotal of any invoices for this customer for the duration of the coupon. For example, a coupon with percent_off of 50 will make a %s100 invoice %s50 instead.|
|redeem_by|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date after which the coupon can no longer be redeemed.|
|times_redeemed|integer|true|none|Number of times this coupon has been applied to a customer.|
|valid|boolean|true|none|Taking account of the above properties, whether this coupon can still be applied to a customer.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|duration|forever|
|duration|once|
|duration|repeating|
|object|coupon|

Issue a credit note to adjust an invoice's amount after the invoice is finalized.

Related guide: [Credit Notes](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/invoices/credit-notes).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|The integer amount in %s representing the total amount of the credit note, including tax.|
|amount_shipping|integer|true|none|This is the sum of all the shipping amounts.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer)|true|none|ID of the customer.|
|customer_balance_transaction|string \| [customer_balance_transaction](#schemacustomer_balance_transaction) \| null|false|none|Customer balance transaction related to this credit note.|
|discount_amount|integer|true|none|The integer amount in %s representing the total amount of discount that was credited.|
|discount_amounts|[[discounts_resource_discount_amount](#schemadiscounts_resource_discount_amount)]|true|none|The aggregate amounts calculated per discount for all line items.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice|string \| [invoice](#schemainvoice)|true|none|ID of the invoice.|
|lines|object|true|none|Line items that make up the credit note|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|memo|string \| null|false|none|Customer-facing text that appears on the credit note PDF.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|number|string|true|none|A unique number that identifies this particular credit note and appears on the PDF of the credit note and its associated invoice.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|out_of_band_amount|integer \| null|false|none|Amount that was credited outside of Stripe.|
|pdf|string|true|none|The link to download the PDF of the credit note.|
|reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason for issuing this credit note, one of `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `order_change`, or `product_unsatisfactory`|
|refund|string \| [refund](#schemarefund) \| null|false|none|Refund related to this credit note.|
|shipping_cost|[invoices_shipping_cost](#schemainvoices_shipping_cost) \| null|false|none|The details of the cost of shipping, including the ShippingRate applied to the invoice.|
|status|string|true|none|Status of this credit note, one of `issued` or `void`. Learn more about [voiding credit notes](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/invoices/credit-notes#voiding).|
|subtotal|integer|true|none|The integer amount in %s representing the amount of the credit note, excluding exclusive tax and invoice level discounts.|
|subtotal_excluding_tax|integer \| null|false|none|The integer amount in %s representing the amount of the credit note, excluding all tax and invoice level discounts.|
|tax_amounts|[[credit_note_tax_amount](#schemacredit_note_tax_amount)]|true|none|The aggregate amounts calculated per tax rate for all line items.|
|total|integer|true|none|The integer amount in %s representing the total amount of the credit note, including tax and all discount.|
|total_excluding_tax|integer \| null|false|none|The integer amount in %s representing the total amount of the credit note, excluding tax, but including discounts.|

This object represents a customer of your business. It lets you create recurring charges and track payments that belong to the same customer.

Related guide: [Save a card during payment](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/save-during-payment).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|[address](#schemaaddress) \| null|false|none|The customer's address.|
|balance|integer|false|none|Current balance, if any, being stored on the customer. If negative, the customer has credit to apply to their next invoice. If positive, the customer has an amount owed that will be added to their next invoice. The balance does not refer to any unpaid invoices; it solely takes into account amounts that have yet to be successfully applied to any invoice. This balance is only taken into account as invoices are finalized.|
|cash_balance|[cash_balance](#schemacash_balance) \| null|false|none|The current funds being held by Stripe on behalf of the customer. These funds can be applied towards payment intents with source "cash_balance". The settings[reconciliation_mode] field describes whether these funds are applied to such payment intents manually or automatically.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies) the customer can be charged in for recurring billing purposes.|
|default_source|string \| [bank_account](#schemabank_account) \| [card](#schemacard) \| [source](#schemasource) \| null|false|none|ID of the default payment source for the customer.<br><br>If you are using payment methods created via the PaymentMethods API, see the [invoice_settings.default_payment_method](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-invoice_settings-default_payment_method) field instead.|
|delinquent|boolean \| null|false|none|When the customer's latest invoice is billed by charging automatically, `delinquent` is `true` if the invoice's latest charge failed. When the customer's latest invoice is billed by sending an invoice, `delinquent` is `true` if the invoice isn't paid by its due date.<br><br>If an invoice is marked uncollectible by [dunning](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/automatic-collection), `delinquent` doesn't get reset to `false`.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|discount|[discount](#schemadiscount) \| null|false|none|Describes the current discount active on the customer, if there is one.|
|email|string \| null|false|none|The customer's email address.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice_credit_balance|object|false|none|The current multi-currency balances, if any, being stored on the customer. If positive in a currency, the customer has a credit to apply to their next invoice denominated in that currency. If negative, the customer has an amount owed that will be added to their next invoice denominated in that currency. These balances do not refer to any unpaid invoices. They solely track amounts that have yet to be successfully applied to any invoice. A balance in a particular currency is only applied to any invoice as an invoice in that currency is finalized.|
|invoice_prefix|string \| null|false|none|The prefix for the customer used to generate unique invoice numbers.|
|invoice_settings|[invoice_setting_customer_setting](#schemainvoice_setting_customer_setting)|false|none|none|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The customer's full name or business name.|
|next_invoice_sequence|integer|false|none|The suffix of the customer's next invoice number, e.g., 0001.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|phone|string \| null|false|none|The customer's phone number.|
|preferred_locales|[string]|false|none|The customer's preferred locales (languages), ordered by preference.|
|shipping|[shipping](#schemashipping) \| null|false|none|Mailing and shipping address for the customer. Appears on invoices emailed to this customer.|
|sources|object|false|none|The customer's payment sources, if any.|
|subscriptions|object|false|none|The customer's current subscriptions, if any.|
|tax|[customer_tax](#schemacustomer_tax)|false|none|none|
|tax_exempt|string \| null|false|none|Describes the customer's tax exemption status. One of `none`, `exempt`, or `reverse`. When set to `reverse`, invoice and receipt PDFs include the text **"Reverse charge"**.|
|tax_ids|object|false|none|The customer's tax IDs.|
|test_clock|string \| [test_helpers.test_clock](#schematest_helpers.test_clock) \| null|false|none|ID of the test clock this customer belongs to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|customer|
|tax_exempt|exempt|
|tax_exempt|none|
|tax_exempt|reverse|

<h2 id="tocS_customer_balance_transaction">customer_balance_transaction</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomer_balance_transaction"></a>
<a id="schema_customer_balance_transaction"></a>
<a id="tocScustomer_balance_transaction"></a>
<a id="tocscustomer_balance_transaction"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "created": 0,
  "credit_note": "string",
  "currency": "string",
  "customer": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "ending_balance": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "invoice": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "customer_balance_transaction",
  "type": "adjustment"
}
```

Each customer has a [`balance`](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-balance) value,
which denotes a debit or credit that's automatically applied to their next invoice upon finalization.
You may modify the value directly by using the [update customer API](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/update),
or by creating a Customer Balance Transaction, which increments or decrements the customer's `balance` by the specified `amount`.

Related guide: [Customer Balance](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/customer/balance) to learn more.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|The amount of the transaction. A negative value is a credit for the customer's balance, and a positive value is a debit to the customer's `balance`.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|credit_note|string \| [credit_note](#schemacredit_note) \| null|false|none|The ID of the credit note (if any) related to the transaction.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer)|true|none|The ID of the customer the transaction belongs to.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|ending_balance|integer|true|none|The customer's `balance` after the transaction was applied. A negative value decreases the amount due on the customer's next invoice. A positive value increases the amount due on the customer's next invoice.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice|string \| [invoice](#schemainvoice) \| null|false|none|The ID of the invoice (if any) related to the transaction.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|type|string|true|none|Transaction type: `adjustment`, `applied_to_invoice`, `credit_note`, `initial`, `invoice_overpaid`, `invoice_too_large`, `invoice_too_small`, `unspent_receiver_credit`, or `unapplied_from_invoice`. See the [Customer Balance page](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/customer/balance#types) to learn more about transaction types.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|customer_balance_transaction|
|type|adjustment|
|type|applied_to_invoice|
|type|credit_note|
|type|initial|
|type|invoice_overpaid|
|type|invoice_too_large|
|type|invoice_too_small|
|type|migration|
|type|unapplied_from_invoice|
|type|unspent_receiver_credit|

<h2 id="tocS_customer_cash_balance_transaction">customer_cash_balance_transaction</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomer_cash_balance_transaction"></a>
<a id="schema_customer_cash_balance_transaction"></a>
<a id="tocScustomer_cash_balance_transaction"></a>
<a id="tocscustomer_cash_balance_transaction"></a>

```json
{
  "applied_to_payment": {
    "payment_intent": "string"
  },
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "customer": "string",
  "ending_balance": 0,
  "funded": {
    "bank_transfer": {
      "eu_bank_transfer": {
        "bic": "string",
        "iban_last4": "string",
        "sender_name": "string"
      },
      "reference": "string",
      "type": "eu_bank_transfer"
    }
  },
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "net_amount": 0,
  "object": "customer_cash_balance_transaction",
  "refunded_from_payment": {
    "refund": "string"
  },
  "type": "applied_to_payment",
  "unapplied_from_payment": {
    "payment_intent": "string"
  }
}
```

Customers with certain payments enabled have a cash balance, representing funds that were paid
by the customer to a merchant, but have not yet been allocated to a payment. Cash Balance Transactions
represent when funds are moved into or out of this balance. This includes funding by the customer, allocation
to payments, and refunds to the customer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applied_to_payment|[customer_balance_resource_cash_balance_transaction_resource_applied_to_payment_transaction](#schemacustomer_balance_resource_cash_balance_transaction_resource_applied_to_payment_transaction)|false|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer)|true|none|The customer whose available cash balance changed as a result of this transaction.|
|ending_balance|integer|true|none|The total available cash balance for the specified currency after this transaction was applied. Represented in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal).|
|funded|[customer_balance_resource_cash_balance_transaction_resource_funded_transaction](#schemacustomer_balance_resource_cash_balance_transaction_resource_funded_transaction)|false|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|net_amount|integer|true|none|The amount by which the cash balance changed, represented in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal). A positive value represents funds being added to the cash balance, a negative value represents funds being removed from the cash balance.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|refunded_from_payment|[customer_balance_resource_cash_balance_transaction_resource_refunded_from_payment_transaction](#schemacustomer_balance_resource_cash_balance_transaction_resource_refunded_from_payment_transaction)|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the cash balance transaction. One of `applied_to_payment`, `unapplied_from_payment`, `refunded_from_payment`, `funded`, `return_initiated`, or `return_canceled`. New types may be added in future. See [Customer Balance](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/customer-balance#types) to learn more about these types.|
|unapplied_from_payment|[customer_balance_resource_cash_balance_transaction_resource_unapplied_from_payment_transaction](#schemacustomer_balance_resource_cash_balance_transaction_resource_unapplied_from_payment_transaction)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|customer_cash_balance_transaction|
|type|applied_to_payment|
|type|funded|
|type|funding_reversed|
|type|refunded_from_payment|
|type|return_canceled|
|type|return_initiated|
|type|unapplied_from_payment|

<h2 id="tocS_discount">discount</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadiscount"></a>
<a id="schema_discount"></a>
<a id="tocSdiscount"></a>
<a id="tocsdiscount"></a>

```json
{
  "checkout_session": "string",
  "coupon": {
    "amount_off": 0,
    "applies_to": {
      "products": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "created": 0,
    "currency": "string",
    "currency_options": {
      "property1": {
        "amount_off": 0
      },
      "property2": {
        "amount_off": 0
      }
    },
    "duration": "forever",
    "duration_in_months": 0,
    "id": "string",
    "livemode": true,
    "max_redemptions": 0,
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "name": "string",
    "object": "coupon",
    "percent_off": 0,
    "redeem_by": 0,
    "times_redeemed": 0,
    "valid": true
  },
  "customer": "string",
  "end": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "invoice": "string",
  "invoice_item": "string",
  "object": "discount",
  "promotion_code": "string",
  "start": 0,
  "subscription": "string"
}
```

A discount represents the actual application of a [coupon](https://stripe.com/docs/api#coupons) or [promotion code](https://stripe.com/docs/api#promotion_codes).
It contains information about when the discount began, when it will end, and what it is applied to.

Related guide: [Applying Discounts to Subscriptions](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/discounts).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|checkout_session|string \| null|false|none|The Checkout session that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular session in payment mode. Will not be present for subscription mode.|
|coupon|[coupon](#schemacoupon)|true|none|A coupon contains information about a percent-off or amount-off discount you<br>might want to apply to a customer. Coupons may be applied to [subscriptions](https://stripe.com/docs/api#subscriptions), [invoices](https://stripe.com/docs/api#invoices),<br>[checkout sessions](https://stripe.com/docs/api/checkout/sessions), [quotes](https://stripe.com/docs/api#quotes), and more. Coupons do not work with conventional one-off [charges](https://stripe.com/docs/api#create_charge) or [payment intents](https://stripe.com/docs/api/payment_intents).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The ID of the customer associated with this discount.|
|end|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the coupon has a duration of `repeating`, the date that this discount will end. If the coupon has a duration of `once` or `forever`, this attribute will be null.|
|id|string|true|none|The ID of the discount object. Discounts cannot be fetched by ID. Use `expand[]=discounts` in API calls to expand discount IDs in an array.|
|invoice|string \| null|false|none|The invoice that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice.|
|invoice_item|string \| null|false|none|The invoice item `id` (or invoice line item `id` for invoice line items of type='subscription') that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice item or invoice line item.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|promotion_code|string \| [promotion_code](#schemapromotion_code) \| null|false|none|The promotion code applied to create this discount.|
|start|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Date that the coupon was applied.|
|subscription|string \| null|false|none|The subscription that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|discount|

<h2 id="tocS_dispute">dispute</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadispute"></a>
<a id="schema_dispute"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "balance_transactions": [
    {
      "amount": 0,
      "available_on": 0,
      "created": 0,
      "currency": "string",
      "description": "string",

        {
          "amount": 0,

          "description": "string",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ],
      "id": "string",
      "net": 0,
      "object": "balance_transaction",
      "reporting_category": "string",
      "source": "string",
      "status": "string",
      "type": "adjustment"
    }
  ],
  "charge": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "evidence": {
    "access_activity_log": "string",
    "billing_address": "string",
    "cancellation_policy": "string",
    "cancellation_policy_disclosure": "string",
    "cancellation_rebuttal": "string",
    "customer_communication": "string",
    "customer_email_address": "string",
    "customer_name": "string",
    "customer_purchase_ip": "string",
    "customer_signature": "string",
    "duplicate_charge_documentation": "string",
    "duplicate_charge_explanation": "string",
    "duplicate_charge_id": "string",
    "product_description": "string",
    "receipt": "string",
    "refund_policy": "string",
    "refund_policy_disclosure": "string",
    "refund_refusal_explanation": "string",
    "service_date": "string",
    "service_documentation": "string",
    "shipping_address": "string",
    "shipping_carrier": "string",
    "shipping_date": "string",
    "shipping_documentation": "string",
    "shipping_tracking_number": "string",
    "uncategorized_file": "string",
    "uncategorized_text": "string"
  },
  "evidence_details": {
    "due_by": 0,
    "has_evidence": true,
    "past_due": true,
    "submission_count": 0
  },
  "id": "string",
  "is_charge_refundable": true,
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "dispute",
  "payment_intent": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "status": "charge_refunded"
}
```

A dispute occurs when a customer questions your charge with their card issuer.
When this happens, you're given the opportunity to respond to the dispute with
evidence that shows that the charge is legitimate. You can find more
information about the dispute process in our [Disputes and
Fraud](/docs/disputes) documentation.

Related guide: [Disputes and Fraud](https://stripe.com/docs/disputes).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Disputed amount. Usually the amount of the charge, but can differ (usually because of currency fluctuation or because only part of the order is disputed).|
|balance_transactions|[[balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction)]|true|none|List of zero, one, or two balance transactions that show funds withdrawn and reinstated to your Stripe account as a result of this dispute.|
|charge|string \| [charge](#schemacharge)|true|none|ID of the charge that was disputed.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|evidence|[dispute_evidence](#schemadispute_evidence)|true|none|none|
|evidence_details|[dispute_evidence_details](#schemadispute_evidence_details)|true|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|is_charge_refundable|boolean|true|none|If true, it is still possible to refund the disputed payment. Once the payment has been fully refunded, no further funds will be withdrawn from your Stripe account as a result of this dispute.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent) \| null|false|none|ID of the PaymentIntent that was disputed.|
|reason|string|true|none|Reason given by cardholder for dispute. Possible values are `bank_cannot_process`, `check_returned`, `credit_not_processed`, `customer_initiated`, `debit_not_authorized`, `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `general`, `incorrect_account_details`, `insufficient_funds`, `product_not_received`, `product_unacceptable`, `subscription_canceled`, or `unrecognized`. Read more about [dispute reasons](https://stripe.com/docs/disputes/categories).|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of dispute. Possible values are `warning_needs_response`, `warning_under_review`, `warning_closed`, `needs_response`, `under_review`, `charge_refunded`, `won`, or `lost`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|status|lost|
|status|needs_response|
|status|under_review|
|status|warning_closed|
|status|warning_needs_response|
|status|warning_under_review|
