### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|This is an object representing a Stripe account. You can retrieve it to see<br>properties on the account like its current requirements or if the account is<br>enabled to make live charges or receive payouts.<br><br>For Custom accounts, the properties below are always returned. For other accounts, some properties are returned until that<br>account has started to go through Connect Onboarding. Once you create an [Account Link](https://stripe.com/docs/api/account_links)<br>for a Standard or Express account, some parameters are no longer returned. These are marked as **Custom Only** or **Custom and Express**<br>below. Learn about the differences [between accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/accounts).|
|*anyOf*|[bank_account](#schemabank_account)|false|none|These bank accounts are payment methods on `Customer` objects.<br><br>On the other hand [External Accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/api#external_accounts) are transfer<br>destinations on `Account` objects for [Custom accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/custom-accounts).<br>They can be bank accounts or debit cards as well, and are documented in the links above.<br><br>Related guide: [Bank Debits and Transfers](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/bank-debits-transfers).|
|*anyOf*|[card](#schemacard)|false|none|You can store multiple cards on a customer in order to charge the customer<br>later. You can also store multiple debit cards on a recipient in order to<br>transfer to those cards later.<br><br>Related guide: [Card Payments with Sources](https://stripe.com/docs/sources/cards).|
|*anyOf*|[source](#schemasource)|false|none|`Source` objects allow you to accept a variety of payment methods. They<br>represent a customer's payment instrument, and can be used with the Stripe API<br>just like a `Card` object: once chargeable, they can be charged, or can be<br>attached to customers.<br><br>Stripe doesn't recommend using the deprecated [Sources API](https://stripe.com/docs/api/sources).<br>We recommend that you adopt the [PaymentMethods API](https://stripe.com/docs/api/payment_methods).<br>This newer API provides access to our latest features and payment method types.<br><br>Related guides: [Sources API](https://stripe.com/docs/sources) and [Sources & Customers](https://stripe.com/docs/sources/customers).|

<h2 id="tocS_payout">payout</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapayout"></a>
<a id="schema_payout"></a>
<a id="tocSpayout"></a>
<a id="tocspayout"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "arrival_date": 0,
  "automatic": true,
  "balance_transaction": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "destination": "string",
  "failure_balance_transaction": "string",
  "failure_code": "string",
  "failure_message": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "method": "string",
  "object": "payout",
  "original_payout": "string",
  "reconciliation_status": "completed",
  "reversed_by": "string",
  "source_type": "string",
  "statement_descriptor": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "type": "bank_account"
}
```

A `Payout` object is created when you receive funds from Stripe, or when you
initiate a payout to either a bank account or debit card of a [connected
Stripe account](/docs/connect/bank-debit-card-payouts). You can retrieve individual payouts,
as well as list all payouts. Payouts are made on [varying
schedules](/docs/connect/manage-payout-schedule), depending on your country and
industry.

Related guide: [Receiving Payouts](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount (in %s) to be transferred to your bank account or debit card.|
|arrival_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Date the payout is expected to arrive in the bank. This factors in delays like weekends or bank holidays.|
|automatic|boolean|true|none|Returns `true` if the payout was created by an [automated payout schedule](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts#payout-schedule), and `false` if it was [requested manually](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts#manual-payouts).|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this payout on your account balance.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|destination|string \| [bank_account](#schemabank_account) \| [card](#schemacard) \| [deleted_bank_account](#schemadeleted_bank_account) \| [deleted_card](#schemadeleted_card) \| null|false|none|ID of the bank account or card the payout was sent to.|
|failure_balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|If the payout failed or was canceled, this will be the ID of the balance transaction that reversed the initial balance transaction, and puts the funds from the failed payout back in your balance.|
|failure_code|string \| null|false|none|Error code explaining reason for payout failure if available. See [Types of payout failures](https://stripe.com/docs/api#payout_failures) for a list of failure codes.|
|failure_message|string \| null|false|none|Message to user further explaining reason for payout failure if available.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|method|string|true|none|The method used to send this payout, which can be `standard` or `instant`. `instant` is only supported for payouts to debit cards. (See [Instant payouts for marketplaces](https://stripe.com/blog/instant-payouts-for-marketplaces) for more information.)|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|original_payout|string \| [payout](#schemapayout) \| null|false|none|If the payout reverses another, this is the ID of the original payout.|
|reconciliation_status|string|true|none|If `completed`, the [Balance Transactions API](https://stripe.com/docs/api/balance_transactions/list#balance_transaction_list-payout) may be used to list all Balance Transactions that were paid out in this payout.|
|reversed_by|string \| [payout](#schemapayout) \| null|false|none|If the payout was reversed, this is the ID of the payout that reverses this payout.|
|source_type|string|true|none|The source balance this payout came from. One of `card`, `fpx`, or `bank_account`.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|Extra information about a payout to be displayed on the user's bank statement.|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the payout: `paid`, `pending`, `in_transit`, `canceled` or `failed`. A payout is `pending` until it is submitted to the bank, when it becomes `in_transit`. The status then changes to `paid` if the transaction goes through, or to `failed` or `canceled` (within 5 business days). Some failed payouts may initially show as `paid` but then change to `failed`.|
|type|string|true|none|Can be `bank_account` or `card`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|payout|
|reconciliation_status|completed|
|reconciliation_status|in_progress|
|reconciliation_status|not_applicable|
|type|bank_account|
|type|card|

This is an object representing a person associated with a Stripe account.

A platform cannot access a Standard or Express account's persons after the account starts onboarding, such as after generating an account link for the account.
See the [Standard onboarding](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/standard-accounts) or [Express onboarding documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/express-accounts) for information about platform pre-filling and account onboarding steps.

Related guide: [Handling Identity Verification with the API](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/identity-verification-api#person-information).

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|alternatives|[[account_requirements_alternative](#schemaaccount_requirements_alternative)]|false|none|Fields that are due and can be satisfied by providing the corresponding alternative fields instead.|

If not collected by the account's `future_requirements[current_deadline]`, these fields will transition to the main `requirements` hash, and may immediately become `past_due`, but the account may also be given a grace period depending on the account's enablement state prior to transition.|

|past_due|[string]|true|none|Fields that weren't collected by the account's `requirements.current_deadline`. These fields need to be collected to enable the person's account. New fields will never appear here; `future_requirements.past_due` will always be a subset of `requirements.past_due`.|
|pending_verification|[string]|true|none|Fields that may become required depending on the results of verification or review. Will be an empty array unless an asynchronous verification is pending. If verification fails, these fields move to `eventually_due` or `currently_due`.|

<h2 id="tocS_plan">plan</h2>

```json
      "unit_amount": 0,
      "unit_amount_decimal": "string",
      "up_to": 0
    }
  ],

  "transform_usage": {

    "round": "down"
  },

  "usage_type": "licensed"
}
```

You can now model subscriptions more flexibly using the [Prices API](https://stripe.com/docs/api#prices). It replaces the Plans API and is backwards compatible to simplify your migration.

Plans define the base price, currency, and billing cycle for recurring purchases of products.
[Products](https://stripe.com/docs/api#products) help you track inventory or provisioning, and plans help you track pricing. Different physical goods or levels of service should be represented by products, and pricing options should be represented by plans. This approach lets you change prices without having to change your provisioning scheme.

For example, you might have a single "gold" product that has plans for $10/month, $100/year, €9/month, and €90/year.

Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription) and more about [products and prices](https://stripe.com/docs/products-prices/overview).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the plan can be used for new purchases.|
|aggregate_usage|string \| null|false|none|Specifies a usage aggregation strategy for plans of `usage_type=metered`. Allowed values are `sum` for summing up all usage during a period, `last_during_period` for using the last usage record reported within a period, `last_ever` for using the last usage record ever (across period bounds) or `max` which uses the usage record with the maximum reported usage during a period. Defaults to `sum`.|
|amount|integer \| null|false|none|The unit amount in %s to be charged, represented as a whole integer if possible. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.|
|amount_decimal|string(decimal) \| null|false|none|The unit amount in %s to be charged, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.|
|billing_scheme|string|true|none|Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `amount`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for plans with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for plans with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|interval|string|true|none|The frequency at which a subscription is billed. One of `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`.|
|interval_count|integer|true|none|The number of intervals (specified in the `interval` attribute) between subscription billings. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|nickname|string \| null|false|none|A brief description of the plan, hidden from customers.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|product|string \| [product](#schemaproduct) \| [deleted_product](#schemadeleted_product) \| null|false|none|The product whose pricing this plan determines.|
|tiers|[[plan_tier](#schemaplan_tier)]|false|none|Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`.|
|tiers_mode|string \| null|false|none|Defines if the tiering price should be `graduated` or `volume` based. In `volume`-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price. In `graduated` tiering, pricing can change as the quantity grows.|
|transform_usage|[transform_usage](#schematransform_usage) \| null|false|none|Apply a transformation to the reported usage or set quantity before computing the amount billed. Cannot be combined with `tiers`.|
|trial_period_days|integer \| null|false|none|Default number of trial days when subscribing a customer to this plan using [`trial_from_plan=true`](https://stripe.com/docs/api#create_subscription-trial_from_plan).|
|usage_type|string|true|none|Configures how the quantity per period should be determined. Can be either `metered` or `licensed`. `licensed` automatically bills the `quantity` set when adding it to a subscription. `metered` aggregates the total usage based on usage records. Defaults to `licensed`.|

<h2 id="tocS_price">price</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprice"></a>
<a id="schema_price"></a>
<a id="tocSprice"></a>
<a id="tocsprice"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "billing_scheme": "per_unit",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "currency_options": {
    "property1": {
      "custom_unit_amount": {

        {
          "flat_amount": 0,

          "unit_amount": 0,

        }
      ],

      },

      "tiers": [
        {
          "flat_amount": 0,
          "flat_amount_decimal": "string",
          "unit_amount": 0,
          "unit_amount_decimal": "string",
          "up_to": 0
        }
      ],
      "unit_amount": 0,
      "unit_amount_decimal": "string"
    }
  },
  "custom_unit_amount": {
    "maximum": 0,
    "minimum": 0,
    "preset": 0
  },
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "lookup_key": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "nickname": "string",
  "object": "price",
  "product": "string",
  "recurring": {
    "aggregate_usage": "last_during_period",
    "interval": "day",
    "interval_count": 0,
    "usage_type": "licensed"
  },
  "tax_behavior": "exclusive",
  "tiers": [
    {
      "flat_amount": 0,
      "flat_amount_decimal": "string",

      "unit_amount_decimal": "string",

    }
  ],
  "tiers_mode": "graduated",
  "transform_quantity": {
    "divide_by": 0,
    "round": "down"
  },
  "type": "one_time",
  "unit_amount": 0,
  "unit_amount_decimal": "string"
}
```

Prices define the unit cost, currency, and (optional) billing cycle for both recurring and one-time purchases of products.
[Products](https://stripe.com/docs/api#products) help you track inventory or provisioning, and prices help you track payment terms. Different physical goods or levels of service should be represented by products, and pricing options should be represented by prices. This approach lets you change prices without having to change your provisioning scheme.

For example, you might have a single "gold" product that has prices for $10/month, $100/year, and €9 once.

Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription), [create an invoice](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/invoices/create), and more about [products and prices](https://stripe.com/docs/products-prices/overview).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the price can be used for new purchases.|
|billing_scheme|string|true|none|Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `unit_amount` or `unit_amount_decimal`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for prices with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for prices with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|currency_options|object|false|none|Prices defined in each available currency option. Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|custom_unit_amount|[custom_unit_amount](#schemacustom_unit_amount) \| null|false|none|When set, provides configuration for the amount to be adjusted by the customer during Checkout Sessions and Payment Links.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|lookup_key|string \| null|false|none|A lookup key used to retrieve prices dynamically from a static string. This may be up to 200 characters.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|nickname|string \| null|false|none|A brief description of the price, hidden from customers.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|product|string \| [product](#schemaproduct) \| [deleted_product](#schemadeleted_product)|true|none|The ID of the product this price is associated with.|
|recurring|[recurring](#schemarecurring) \| null|false|none|The recurring components of a price such as `interval` and `usage_type`.|
|tax_behavior|string \| null|false|none|Specifies whether the price is considered inclusive of taxes or exclusive of taxes. One of `inclusive`, `exclusive`, or `unspecified`. Once specified as either `inclusive` or `exclusive`, it cannot be changed.|
|tiers|[[price_tier](#schemaprice_tier)]|false|none|Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`.|
|tiers_mode|string \| null|false|none|Defines if the tiering price should be `graduated` or `volume` based. In `volume`-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price. In `graduated` tiering, pricing can change as the quantity grows.|
|transform_quantity|[transform_quantity](#schematransform_quantity) \| null|false|none|Apply a transformation to the reported usage or set quantity before computing the amount billed. Cannot be combined with `tiers`.|
|type|string|true|none|One of `one_time` or `recurring` depending on whether the price is for a one-time purchase or a recurring (subscription) purchase.|
|unit_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The unit amount in %s to be charged, represented as a whole integer if possible. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.|
|unit_amount_decimal|string(decimal) \| null|false|none|The unit amount in %s to be charged, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|billing_scheme|per_unit|
|billing_scheme|tiered|
|object|price|
|tax_behavior|exclusive|
|tax_behavior|inclusive|
|tax_behavior|unspecified|
|tiers_mode|graduated|
|tiers_mode|volume|
|type|one_time|
|type|recurring|

<h2 id="tocS_product">product</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaproduct"></a>
<a id="schema_product"></a>
<a id="tocSproduct"></a>
<a id="tocsproduct"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "created": 0,
  "default_price": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "images": [
    "string"
  ],
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },

  "object": "product",

    "height": 0,
    "length": 0,
    "weight": 0,
    "width": 0
  },

  "statement_descriptor": "string",
  "tax_code": "string",
  "unit_label": "string",
  "updated": 0,
  "url": "string"

```

Products describe the specific goods or services you offer to your customers.
For example, you might offer a Standard and Premium version of your goods or service; each version would be a separate Product.
They can be used in conjunction with [Prices](https://stripe.com/docs/api#prices) to configure pricing in Payment Links, Checkout, and Subscriptions.

Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription),
[share a Payment Link](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/payment-links/overview),
[accept payments with Checkout](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/accept-a-payment#create-product-prices-upfront),
and more about [Products and Prices](https://stripe.com/docs/products-prices/overview)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the product is currently available for purchase.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|default_price|string \| [price](#schemaprice) \| null|false|none|The ID of the [Price](https://stripe.com/docs/api/prices) object that is the default price for this product.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The product's description, meant to be displayable to the customer. Use this field to optionally store a long form explanation of the product being sold for your own rendering purposes.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|images|[string]|true|none|A list of up to 8 URLs of images for this product, meant to be displayable to the customer.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|name|string|true|none|The product's name, meant to be displayable to the customer.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|package_dimensions|[package_dimensions](#schemapackage_dimensions) \| null|false|none|The dimensions of this product for shipping purposes.|
|shippable|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this product is shipped (i.e., physical goods).|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|Extra information about a product which will appear on your customer's credit card statement. In the case that multiple products are billed at once, the first statement descriptor will be used.|
|tax_code|string \| [tax_code](#schematax_code) \| null|false|none|A [tax code](https://stripe.com/docs/tax/tax-categories) ID.|
|unit_label|string \| null|false|none|A label that represents units of this product. When set, this will be included in customers' receipts, invoices, Checkout, and the customer portal.|
|updated|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|url|string \| null|false|none|A URL of a publicly-accessible webpage for this product.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|product|

A Promotion Code represents a customer-redeemable code for a [coupon](https://stripe.com/docs/api#coupons). It can be used to
create multiple codes for a single coupon.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the promotion code is currently active. A promotion code is only active if the coupon is also valid.|
|code|string|true|none|The customer-facing code. Regardless of case, this code must be unique across all active promotion codes for each customer.|
|coupon|[coupon](#schemacoupon)|true|none|A coupon contains information about a percent-off or amount-off discount you<br>might want to apply to a customer. Coupons may be applied to [subscriptions](https://stripe.com/docs/api#subscriptions), [invoices](https://stripe.com/docs/api#invoices),<br>[checkout sessions](https://stripe.com/docs/api/checkout/sessions), [quotes](https://stripe.com/docs/api#quotes), and more. Coupons do not work with conventional one-off [charges](https://stripe.com/docs/api#create_charge) or [payment intents](https://stripe.com/docs/api/payment_intents).|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The customer that this promotion code can be used by.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Date at which the promotion code can no longer be redeemed.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|max_redemptions|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum number of times this promotion code can be redeemed.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|restrictions|[promotion_codes_resource_restrictions](#schemapromotion_codes_resource_restrictions)|true|none|none|
|times_redeemed|integer|true|none|Number of times this promotion code has been used.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

A Quote is a way to model prices that you'd like to provide to a customer.
Once accepted, it will automatically create an invoice, subscription or subscription schedule.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount_subtotal|integer|true|none|Total before any discounts or taxes are applied.|
|amount_total|integer|true|none|Total after discounts and taxes are applied.|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| [deleted_application](#schemadeleted_application) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect Application that created the quote.|
|application_fee_amount|integer \| null|false|none|The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. Only applicable if there are no line items with recurring prices on the quote.|
|application_fee_percent|number \| null|false|none|A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice subtotal that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. Only applicable if there are line items with recurring prices on the quote.|
|automatic_tax|[quotes_resource_automatic_tax](#schemaquotes_resource_automatic_tax)|true|none|none|
|collection_method|string|true|none|Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay invoices at the end of the subscription cycle or on finalization using the default payment method attached to the subscription or customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`. Defaults to `charge_automatically`.|
|computed|[quotes_resource_computed](#schemaquotes_resource_computed)|true|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string \| null|false|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The customer which this quote belongs to. A customer is required before finalizing the quote. Once specified, it cannot be changed.|
|default_tax_rates|[string \| [tax_rate](#schematax_rate)]|false|none|The tax rates applied to this quote.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|A description that will be displayed on the quote PDF.|
|discounts|[string \| [discount](#schemadiscount)]|true|none|The discounts applied to this quote.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The date on which the quote will be canceled if in `open` or `draft` status. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|footer|string \| null|false|none|A footer that will be displayed on the quote PDF.|
|from_quote|[quotes_resource_from_quote](#schemaquotes_resource_from_quote) \| null|false|none|Details of the quote that was cloned. See the [cloning documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/quotes/clone) for more details.|
|header|string \| null|false|none|A header that will be displayed on the quote PDF.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|invoice|string \| [invoice](#schemainvoice) \| [deleted_invoice](#schemadeleted_invoice) \| null|false|none|The invoice that was created from this quote.|
|invoice_settings|[invoice_setting_quote_setting](#schemainvoice_setting_quote_setting) \| null|false|none|All invoices will be billed using the specified settings.|
|line_items|object|false|none|A list of items the customer is being quoted for.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|number|string \| null|false|none|A unique number that identifies this particular quote. This number is assigned once the quote is [finalized](https://stripe.com/docs/quotes/overview#finalize).|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account on behalf of which to charge. See the [Connect documentation](https://support.stripe.com/questions/sending-invoices-on-behalf-of-connected-accounts) for details.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the quote.|
|status_transitions|[quotes_resource_status_transitions](#schemaquotes_resource_status_transitions)|true|none|none|
|subscription|string \| [subscription](#schemasubscription) \| null|false|none|The subscription that was created or updated from this quote.|
|subscription_data|[quotes_resource_subscription_data_subscription_data](#schemaquotes_resource_subscription_data_subscription_data)|true|none|none|
|subscription_schedule|string \| [subscription_schedule](#schemasubscription_schedule) \| null|false|none|The subscription schedule that was created or updated from this quote.|
|test_clock|string \| [test_helpers.test_clock](#schematest_helpers.test_clock) \| null|false|none|ID of the test clock this quote belongs to.|
|total_details|[quotes_resource_total_details](#schemaquotes_resource_total_details)|true|none|none|
|transfer_data|[quotes_resource_transfer_data](#schemaquotes_resource_transfer_data) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the payments will be attributed to for tax reporting, and where funds from each payment will be transferred to for each of the invoices.|

An early fraud warning indicates that the card issuer has notified us that a
charge may be fraudulent.

Related guide: [Early Fraud Warnings](https://stripe.com/docs/disputes/measuring#early-fraud-warnings).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actionable|boolean|true|none|An EFW is actionable if it has not received a dispute and has not been fully refunded. You may wish to proactively refund a charge that receives an EFW, in order to avoid receiving a dispute later.|
|charge|string \| [charge](#schemacharge)|true|none|ID of the charge this early fraud warning is for, optionally expanded.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|fraud_type|string|true|none|The type of fraud labelled by the issuer. One of `card_never_received`, `fraudulent_card_application`, `made_with_counterfeit_card`, `made_with_lost_card`, `made_with_stolen_card`, `misc`, `unauthorized_use_of_card`.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent)|false|none|ID of the Payment Intent this early fraud warning is for, optionally expanded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|radar.early_fraud_warning|

<h2 id="tocS_refund">refund</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarefund"></a>
<a id="schema_refund"></a>
<a id="tocSrefund"></a>
<a id="tocsrefund"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "balance_transaction": "string",
  "charge": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "failure_balance_transaction": "string",
  "failure_reason": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "instructions_email": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "next_action": {
    "display_details": {
      "email_sent": {
        "email_sent_at": 0,
        "email_sent_to": "string"
      },
      "expires_at": 0
    },
    "type": "string"
  },
  "object": "refund",
  "payment_intent": "string",
  "reason": "duplicate",
  "receipt_number": "string",
  "source_transfer_reversal": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "transfer_reversal": "string"
}
```

`Refund` objects allow you to refund a charge that has previously been created
but not yet refunded. Funds will be refunded to the credit or debit card that
was originally charged.

Related guide: [Refunds](https://stripe.com/docs/refunds).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount, in %s.|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.|
|charge|string \| [charge](#schemacharge) \| null|false|none|ID of the charge that was refunded.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. (Available on non-card refunds only)|
|failure_balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction)|false|none|If the refund failed, this balance transaction describes the adjustment made on your account balance that reverses the initial balance transaction.|
|failure_reason|string|false|none|If the refund failed, the reason for refund failure if known. Possible values are `lost_or_stolen_card`, `expired_or_canceled_card`, `charge_for_pending_refund_disputed`, `insufficient_funds`, `declined`, `merchant_request` or `unknown`.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|instructions_email|string|false|none|Email to which refund instructions, if required, are sent to.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|next_action|[refund_next_action](#schemarefund_next_action)|false|none|none|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|payment_intent|string \| [payment_intent](#schemapayment_intent) \| null|false|none|ID of the PaymentIntent that was refunded.|
|reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason for the refund, either user-provided (`duplicate`, `fraudulent`, or `requested_by_customer`) or generated by Stripe internally (`expired_uncaptured_charge`).|
|receipt_number|string \| null|false|none|This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this refund.|
|source_transfer_reversal|string \| [transfer_reversal](#schematransfer_reversal) \| null|false|none|The transfer reversal that is associated with the refund. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account. See the Connect documentation for details.|
|status|string \| null|false|none|Status of the refund. For credit card refunds, this can be `pending`, `succeeded`, or `failed`. For other types of refunds, it can be `pending`, `requires_action`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `canceled`. Refer to our [refunds](https://stripe.com/docs/refunds#failed-refunds) documentation for more details.|
|transfer_reversal|string \| [transfer_reversal](#schematransfer_reversal) \| null|false|none|If the accompanying transfer was reversed, the transfer reversal object. Only applicable if the charge was created using the destination parameter.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|refund|
|reason|duplicate|
|reason|expired_uncaptured_charge|
|reason|fraudulent|
|reason|requested_by_customer|

```json
    "size": 0,

    "type": "string",
    "url": "string"
  },
  "status": "string",
  "succeeded_at": 0
}
```

The Report Run object represents an instance of a report type generated with
specific run parameters. Once the object is created, Stripe begins processing the report.
When the report has finished running, it will give you a reference to a file
where you can retrieve your results. For an overview, see
[API Access to Reports](https://stripe.com/docs/reporting/statements/api).

Note that certain report types can only be run based on your live-mode data (not test-mode
data), and will error when queried without a [live-mode API key](https://stripe.com/docs/keys#test-live-modes).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|error|string \| null|false|none|If something should go wrong during the run, a message about the failure (populated when<br> `status=failed`).|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|`true` if the report is run on live mode data and `false` if it is run on test mode data.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|parameters|[financial_reporting_finance_report_run_run_parameters](#schemafinancial_reporting_finance_report_run_run_parameters)|true|none|none|
|report_type|string|true|none|The ID of the [report type](https://stripe.com/docs/reports/report-types) to run, such as `"balance.summary.1"`.|
|result|[file](#schemafile) \| null|false|none|The file object representing the result of the report run (populated when<br> `status=succeeded`).|
|status|string|true|none|Status of this report run. This will be `pending` when the run is initially created.<br> When the run finishes, this will be set to `succeeded` and the `result` field will be populated.<br> Rarely, we may encounter an error, at which point this will be set to `failed` and the `error` field will be populated.|
|succeeded_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Timestamp at which this run successfully finished (populated when<br> `status=succeeded`). Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|reporting.report_run|

<h2 id="tocS_reporting.report_type">reporting.report_type</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
  ],

  "object": "reporting.report_type",
  "updated": 0,
  "version": 0
}
```

The Report Type resource corresponds to a particular type of report, such as
the "Activity summary" or "Itemized payouts" reports. These objects are
identified by an ID belonging to a set of enumerated values. See
[API Access to Reports documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/reporting/statements/api)
for those Report Type IDs, along with required and optional parameters.

Note that certain report types can only be run based on your live-mode data (not test-mode
data), and will error when queried without a [live-mode API key](https://stripe.com/docs/keys#test-live-modes).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data_available_end|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Most recent time for which this Report Type is available. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|data_available_start|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Earliest time for which this Report Type is available. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|default_columns|[string]|false|none|List of column names that are included by default when this Report Type gets run. (If the Report Type doesn't support the `columns` parameter, this will be null.)|
|id|string|true|none|The [ID of the Report Type](https://stripe.com/docs/reporting/statements/api#available-report-types), such as `balance.summary.1`.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable name of the Report Type|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|updated|integer(unix-time)|true|none|When this Report Type was latest updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|version|integer|true|none|Version of the Report Type. Different versions report with the same ID will have the same purpose, but may take different run parameters or have different result schemas.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|reporting.report_type|


If you have [scheduled a Sigma query](https://stripe.com/docs/sigma/scheduled-queries), you'll
receive a `sigma.scheduled_query_run.created` webhook each time the query
runs. The webhook contains a `ScheduledQueryRun` object, which you can use to
retrieve the query results.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|data_load_time|integer(unix-time)|true|none|When the query was run, Sigma contained a snapshot of your Stripe data at this time.|
|error|[sigma_scheduled_query_run_error](#schemasigma_scheduled_query_run_error)|false|none|none|
|file|[file](#schemafile) \| null|false|none|The file object representing the results of the query.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|result_available_until|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the result expires and is no longer available for download.|
|sql|string|true|none|SQL for the query.|
|status|string|true|none|The query's execution status, which will be `completed` for successful runs, and `canceled`, `failed`, or `timed_out` otherwise.|
|title|string|true|none|Title of the query.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|scheduled_query_run|

```json
  "status": "string",
  "usage": "string"

```

A SetupAttempt describes one attempted confirmation of a SetupIntent,
whether that confirmation was successful or unsuccessful. You can use
SetupAttempts to inspect details of a specific attempt at setting up a
payment method using a SetupIntent.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| null|false|none|The value of [application](https://stripe.com/docs/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-application) on the SetupIntent at the time of this confirmation.|
|attach_to_self|boolean|false|none|If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account.<br><br>It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|The value of [customer](https://stripe.com/docs/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-customer) on the SetupIntent at the time of this confirmation.|
|flow_directions|[string]|false|none|Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used.<br><br>Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The value of [on_behalf_of](https://stripe.com/docs/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-on_behalf_of) on the SetupIntent at the time of this confirmation.|
|payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method)|true|none|ID of the payment method used with this SetupAttempt.|
|payment_method_details|[setup_attempt_payment_method_details](#schemasetup_attempt_payment_method_details)|true|none|none|
|setup_error|[api_errors](#schemaapi_errors) \| null|false|none|The error encountered during this attempt to confirm the SetupIntent, if any.|
|setup_intent|string \| [setup_intent](#schemasetup_intent)|true|none|ID of the SetupIntent that this attempt belongs to.|
|status|string|true|none|Status of this SetupAttempt, one of `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `abandoned`.|
|usage|string|true|none|The value of [usage](https://stripe.com/docs/api/setup_intents/object#setup_intent_object-usage) on the SetupIntent at the time of this confirmation, one of `off_session` or `on_session`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|flow_directions|inbound|
|flow_directions|outbound|
|object|setup_attempt|

A SetupIntent guides you through the process of setting up and saving a customer's payment credentials for future payments.
For example, you could use a SetupIntent to set up and save your customer's card without immediately collecting a payment.
Later, you can use [PaymentIntents](https://stripe.com/docs/api#payment_intents) to drive the payment flow.

Create a SetupIntent as soon as you're ready to collect your customer's payment credentials.
Do not maintain long-lived, unconfirmed SetupIntents as they may no longer be valid.
The SetupIntent then transitions through multiple [statuses](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/intents#intent-statuses) as it guides
you through the setup process.

Successful SetupIntents result in payment credentials that are optimized for future payments.
For example, cardholders in [certain regions](/guides/strong-customer-authentication) may need to be run through
[Strong Customer Authentication](https://stripe.com/docs/strong-customer-authentication) at the time of payment method collection
in order to streamline later [off-session payments](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/setup-intents).
If the SetupIntent is used with a [Customer](https://stripe.com/docs/api#setup_intent_object-customer), upon success,
it will automatically attach the resulting payment method to that Customer.
We recommend using SetupIntents or [setup_future_usage](https://stripe.com/docs/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) on
PaymentIntents to save payment methods in order to prevent saving invalid or unoptimized payment methods.

By using SetupIntents, you ensure that your customers experience the minimum set of required friction,
even as regulations change over time.

Related guide: [Setup Intents API](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/setup-intents).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect application that created the SetupIntent.|
|attach_to_self|boolean|false|none|If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account.<br><br>It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer.|
|cancellation_reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason for cancellation of this SetupIntent, one of `abandoned`, `requested_by_customer`, or `duplicate`.|
|client_secret|string \| null|false|none|The client secret of this SetupIntent. Used for client-side retrieval using a publishable key.<br><br>The client secret can be used to complete payment setup from your frontend. It should not be stored, logged, or exposed to anyone other than the customer. Make sure that you have TLS enabled on any page that includes the client secret.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer) \| null|false|none|ID of the Customer this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists.<br><br>If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Customer on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this SetupIntent.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|flow_directions|[string]|false|none|Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used.<br><br>Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|last_setup_error|[api_errors](#schemaapi_errors) \| null|false|none|The error encountered in the previous SetupIntent confirmation.|
|latest_attempt|string \| [setup_attempt](#schemasetup_attempt) \| null|false|none|The most recent SetupAttempt for this SetupIntent.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|mandate|string \| [mandate](#schemamandate) \| null|false|none|ID of the multi use Mandate generated by the SetupIntent.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|next_action|[setup_intent_next_action](#schemasetup_intent_next_action) \| null|false|none|If present, this property tells you what actions you need to take in order for your customer to continue payment setup.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) for which the setup is intended.|
|payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|ID of the payment method used with this SetupIntent.|
|payment_method_options|[setup_intent_payment_method_options](#schemasetup_intent_payment_method_options) \| null|false|none|Payment-method-specific configuration for this SetupIntent.|
|payment_method_types|[string]|true|none|The list of payment method types (e.g. card) that this SetupIntent is allowed to set up.|
|single_use_mandate|string \| [mandate](#schemamandate) \| null|false|none|ID of the single_use Mandate generated by the SetupIntent.|
|status|string|true|none|[Status](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/intents#intent-statuses) of this SetupIntent, one of `requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `canceled`, or `succeeded`.|
|usage|string|true|none|Indicates how the payment method is intended to be used in the future.<br><br>Use `on_session` if you intend to only reuse the payment method when the customer is in your checkout flow. Use `off_session` if your customer may or may not be in your checkout flow. If not provided, this value defaults to `off_session`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|cancellation_reason|abandoned|
|cancellation_reason|duplicate|
|cancellation_reason|requested_by_customer|
|flow_directions|inbound|
|flow_directions|outbound|
|object|setup_intent|
|status|canceled|
|status|processing|
|status|requires_action|
|status|requires_confirmation|
|status|requires_payment_method|
|status|succeeded|

<h2 id="tocS_shipping_rate">shipping_rate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemashipping_rate"></a>
<a id="schema_shipping_rate"></a>
<a id="tocSshipping_rate"></a>
<a id="tocsshipping_rate"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "created": 0,
  "delivery_estimate": {
    "maximum": {
      "unit": "business_day",
      "value": 0
    },
    "minimum": {
      "unit": "business_day",
      "value": 0
    }
  },
  "display_name": "string",
  "fixed_amount": {
    "amount": 0,
    "currency": "string",
    "currency_options": {
      "property1": {
        "amount": 0,
        "tax_behavior": "exclusive"
      },
      "property2": {
        "amount": 0,
        "tax_behavior": "exclusive"
      }
    }
  },
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "shipping_rate",
  "tax_behavior": "exclusive",
  "tax_code": "string",
  "type": "fixed_amount"
}
```

Shipping rates describe the price of shipping presented to your customers and can be
applied to [Checkout Sessions](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/checkout/shipping)
and [Orders](https://stripe.com/docs/orders/shipping) to collect shipping costs.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Whether the shipping rate can be used for new purchases. Defaults to `true`.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|delivery_estimate|[shipping_rate_delivery_estimate](#schemashipping_rate_delivery_estimate) \| null|false|none|The estimated range for how long shipping will take, meant to be displayable to the customer. This will appear on CheckoutSessions.|
|display_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the shipping rate, meant to be displayable to the customer. This will appear on CheckoutSessions.|
|fixed_amount|[shipping_rate_fixed_amount](#schemashipping_rate_fixed_amount)|false|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|tax_behavior|string \| null|false|none|Specifies whether the rate is considered inclusive of taxes or exclusive of taxes. One of `inclusive`, `exclusive`, or `unspecified`.|
|tax_code|string \| [tax_code](#schematax_code) \| null|false|none|A [tax code](https://stripe.com/docs/tax/tax-categories) ID. The Shipping tax code is `txcd_92010001`.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of calculation to use on the shipping rate. Can only be `fixed_amount` for now.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|shipping_rate|
|tax_behavior|exclusive|
|tax_behavior|inclusive|
|tax_behavior|unspecified|
|type|fixed_amount|

`Source` objects allow you to accept a variety of payment methods. They
represent a customer's payment instrument, and can be used with the Stripe API
just like a `Card` object: once chargeable, they can be charged, or can be
attached to customers.

Stripe doesn't recommend using the deprecated [Sources API](https://stripe.com/docs/api/sources).
We recommend that you adopt the [PaymentMethods API](https://stripe.com/docs/api/payment_methods).
This newer API provides access to our latest features and payment method types.

Related guides: [Sources API](https://stripe.com/docs/sources) and [Sources & Customers](https://stripe.com/docs/sources/customers).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ach_credit_transfer|[source_type_ach_credit_transfer](#schemasource_type_ach_credit_transfer)|false|none|none|
|ach_debit|[source_type_ach_debit](#schemasource_type_ach_debit)|false|none|none|
|acss_debit|[source_type_acss_debit](#schemasource_type_acss_debit)|false|none|none|
|alipay|[source_type_alipay](#schemasource_type_alipay)|false|none|none|
|amount|integer \| null|false|none|A positive integer in the smallest currency unit (that is, 100 cents for $1.00, or 1 for ¥1, Japanese Yen being a zero-decimal currency) representing the total amount associated with the source. This is the amount for which the source will be chargeable once ready. Required for `single_use` sources.|
|au_becs_debit|[source_type_au_becs_debit](#schemasource_type_au_becs_debit)|false|none|none|
|bancontact|[source_type_bancontact](#schemasource_type_bancontact)|false|none|none|
|card|[source_type_card](#schemasource_type_card)|false|none|none|

Source mandate notifications should be created when a notification related to
a source mandate must be sent to the payer. They will trigger a webhook or
deliver an email to the customer.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acss_debit|[source_mandate_notification_acss_debit_data](#schemasource_mandate_notification_acss_debit_data)|false|none|none|
|amount|integer \| null|false|none|A positive integer in the smallest currency unit (that is, 100 cents for $1.00, or 1 for ¥1, Japanese Yen being a zero-decimal currency) representing the amount associated with the mandate notification. The amount is expressed in the currency of the underlying source. Required if the notification type is `debit_initiated`.|
|bacs_debit|[source_mandate_notification_bacs_debit_data](#schemasource_mandate_notification_bacs_debit_data)|false|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|reason|string|true|none|The reason of the mandate notification. Valid reasons are `mandate_confirmed` or `debit_initiated`.|
|sepa_debit|[source_mandate_notification_sepa_debit_data](#schemasource_mandate_notification_sepa_debit_data)|false|none|none|
|source|[source](#schemasource)|true|none|`Source` objects allow you to accept a variety of payment methods. They<br>represent a customer's payment instrument, and can be used with the Stripe API<br>just like a `Card` object: once chargeable, they can be charged, or can be<br>attached to customers.<br><br>Stripe doesn't recommend using the deprecated [Sources API](https://stripe.com/docs/api/sources).<br>We recommend that you adopt the [PaymentMethods API](https://stripe.com/docs/api/payment_methods).<br>This newer API provides access to our latest features and payment method types.<br><br>Related guides: [Sources API](https://stripe.com/docs/sources) and [Sources & Customers](https://stripe.com/docs/sources/customers).|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the mandate notification. Valid statuses are `pending` or `submitted`.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of source this mandate notification is attached to. Should be the source type identifier code for the payment method, such as `three_d_secure`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|source_mandate_notification|

In rare cases when customers deposit excess funds and we are unable to refund those, those funds get moved to your balance and show up in amount_charged as well. The amount charged is expressed in the source's currency.|
|amount_received|integer|true|none|The total amount received by the receiver source. `amount_received = amount_returned + amount_charged` should be true for consumed sources unless customers deposit excess funds. The amount received is expressed in the source's currency.|
|amount_returned|integer|true|none|The total amount that was returned to the customer. The amount returned is expressed in the source's currency.|
|refund_attributes_method|string|true|none|Type of refund attribute method, one of `email`, `manual`, or `none`.|
|refund_attributes_status|string|true|none|Type of refund attribute status, one of `missing`, `requested`, or `available`.|

Present only if the redirect status is `failed`.|
|return_url|string|true|none|The URL you provide to redirect the customer to after they authenticated their payment.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the redirect, either `pending` (ready to be used by your customer to authenticate the transaction), `succeeded` (succesful authentication, cannot be reused) or `not_required` (redirect should not be used) or `failed` (failed authentication, cannot be reused).|
|url|string|true|none|The URL provided to you to redirect a customer to as part of a `redirect` authentication flow.|

Some payment methods have no required amount that a customer must send.
Customers can be instructed to send any amount, and it can be made up of
multiple transactions. As such, sources can have multiple associated
transactions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|ach_credit_transfer|[source_transaction_ach_credit_transfer_data](#schemasource_transaction_ach_credit_transfer_data)|false|none|none|
|amount|integer|true|none|A positive integer in the smallest currency unit (that is, 100 cents for $1.00, or 1 for ¥1, Japanese Yen being a zero-decimal currency) representing the amount your customer has pushed to the receiver.|
|chf_credit_transfer|[source_transaction_chf_credit_transfer_data](#schemasource_transaction_chf_credit_transfer_data)|false|none|none|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|gbp_credit_transfer|[source_transaction_gbp_credit_transfer_data](#schemasource_transaction_gbp_credit_transfer_data)|false|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|paper_check|[source_transaction_paper_check_data](#schemasource_transaction_paper_check_data)|false|none|none|
|sepa_credit_transfer|[source_transaction_sepa_credit_transfer_data](#schemasource_transaction_sepa_credit_transfer_data)|false|none|none|
|source|string|true|none|The ID of the source this transaction is attached to.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the transaction, one of `succeeded`, `pending`, or `failed`.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of source this transaction is attached to.|

Subscriptions allow you to charge a customer on a recurring basis.

Related guide: [Creating Subscriptions](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/creating).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| [deleted_application](#schemadeleted_application) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect Application that created the subscription.|
|application_fee_percent|number \| null|false|none|A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice subtotal that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account.|
|automatic_tax|[subscription_automatic_tax](#schemasubscription_automatic_tax)|true|none|none|
|billing_cycle_anchor|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Determines the date of the first full invoice, and, for plans with `month` or `year` intervals, the day of the month for subsequent invoices. The timestamp is in UTC format.|
|billing_thresholds|[subscription_billing_thresholds](#schemasubscription_billing_thresholds) \| null|false|none|Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the subscription advanced to a new billing period|
|cancel_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|A date in the future at which the subscription will automatically get canceled|
|cancel_at_period_end|boolean|true|none|If the subscription has been canceled with the `at_period_end` flag set to `true`, `cancel_at_period_end` on the subscription will be true. You can use this attribute to determine whether a subscription that has a status of active is scheduled to be canceled at the end of the current period.|
|canceled_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the subscription has been canceled, the date of that cancellation. If the subscription was canceled with `cancel_at_period_end`, `canceled_at` will reflect the time of the most recent update request, not the end of the subscription period when the subscription is automatically moved to a canceled state.|
|cancellation_details|[cancellation_details](#schemacancellation_details) \| null|false|none|Details about why this subscription was cancelled|
|collection_method|string|true|none|Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay this subscription at the end of the cycle using the default source attached to the customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|current_period_end|integer(unix-time)|true|none|End of the current period that the subscription has been invoiced for. At the end of this period, a new invoice will be created.|
|current_period_start|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Start of the current period that the subscription has been invoiced for.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer)|true|none|ID of the customer who owns the subscription.|
|days_until_due|integer \| null|false|none|Number of days a customer has to pay invoices generated by this subscription. This value will be `null` for subscriptions where `collection_method=charge_automatically`.|
|default_payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|ID of the default payment method for the subscription. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription. This takes precedence over `default_source`. If neither are set, invoices will use the customer's [invoice_settings.default_payment_method](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-invoice_settings-default_payment_method) or [default_source](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-default_source).|
|default_source|string \| [bank_account](#schemabank_account) \| [card](#schemacard) \| [source](#schemasource) \| null|false|none|ID of the default payment source for the subscription. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription and be in a chargeable state. If `default_payment_method` is also set, `default_payment_method` will take precedence. If neither are set, invoices will use the customer's [invoice_settings.default_payment_method](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-invoice_settings-default_payment_method) or [default_source](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers/object#customer_object-default_source).|
|default_tax_rates|[[tax_rate](#schematax_rate)]|false|none|The tax rates that will apply to any subscription item that does not have `tax_rates` set. Invoices created will have their `default_tax_rates` populated from the subscription.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The subscription's description, meant to be displayable to the customer. Use this field to optionally store an explanation of the subscription for rendering in Stripe surfaces.|
|discount|[discount](#schemadiscount) \| null|false|none|Describes the current discount applied to this subscription, if there is one. When billing, a discount applied to a subscription overrides a discount applied on a customer-wide basis.|
|ended_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the subscription has ended, the date the subscription ended.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|items|object|true|none|List of subscription items, each with an attached price.|
|latest_invoice|string \| [invoice](#schemainvoice) \| null|false|none|The most recent invoice this subscription has generated.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|next_pending_invoice_item_invoice|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Specifies the approximate timestamp on which any pending invoice items will be billed according to the schedule provided at `pending_invoice_item_interval`.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the charge was made on behalf of for charges associated with this subscription. See the Connect documentation for details.|
|pause_collection|[subscriptions_resource_pause_collection](#schemasubscriptions_resource_pause_collection) \| null|false|none|If specified, payment collection for this subscription will be paused.|
|payment_settings|[subscriptions_resource_payment_settings](#schemasubscriptions_resource_payment_settings) \| null|false|none|Payment settings passed on to invoices created by the subscription.|
|pending_invoice_item_interval|[subscription_pending_invoice_item_interval](#schemasubscription_pending_invoice_item_interval) \| null|false|none|Specifies an interval for how often to bill for any pending invoice items. It is analogous to calling [Create an invoice](https://stripe.com/docs/api#create_invoice) for the given subscription at the specified interval.|
|pending_setup_intent|string \| [setup_intent](#schemasetup_intent) \| null|false|none|You can use this [SetupIntent](https://stripe.com/docs/api/setup_intents) to collect user authentication when creating a subscription without immediate payment or updating a subscription's payment method, allowing you to optimize for off-session payments. Learn more in the [SCA Migration Guide](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/migration/strong-customer-authentication#scenario-2).|
|pending_update|[subscriptions_resource_pending_update](#schemasubscriptions_resource_pending_update) \| null|false|none|If specified, [pending updates](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/pending-updates) that will be applied to the subscription once the `latest_invoice` has been paid.|
|schedule|string \| [subscription_schedule](#schemasubscription_schedule) \| null|false|none|The schedule attached to the subscription|
|start_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Date when the subscription was first created. The date might differ from the `created` date due to backdating.|
|status|string|true|none|Possible values are `incomplete`, `incomplete_expired`, `trialing`, `active`, `past_due`, `canceled`, or `unpaid`. <br><br>For `collection_method=charge_automatically` a subscription moves into `incomplete` if the initial payment attempt fails. A subscription in this state can only have metadata and default_source updated. Once the first invoice is paid, the subscription moves into an `active` state. If the first invoice is not paid within 23 hours, the subscription transitions to `incomplete_expired`. This is a terminal state, the open invoice will be voided and no further invoices will be generated. <br><br>A subscription that is currently in a trial period is `trialing` and moves to `active` when the trial period is over. <br><br>If subscription `collection_method=charge_automatically` it becomes `past_due` when payment to renew it fails and `canceled` or `unpaid` (depending on your subscriptions settings) when Stripe has exhausted all payment retry attempts. <br><br>If subscription `collection_method=send_invoice` it becomes `past_due` when its invoice is not paid by the due date, and `canceled` or `unpaid` if it is still not paid by an additional deadline after that. Note that when a subscription has a status of `unpaid`, no subsequent invoices will be attempted (invoices will be created, but then immediately automatically closed). After receiving updated payment information from a customer, you may choose to reopen and pay their closed invoices.|
|test_clock|string \| [test_helpers.test_clock](#schematest_helpers.test_clock) \| null|false|none|ID of the test clock this subscription belongs to.|
|transfer_data|[subscription_transfer_data](#schemasubscription_transfer_data) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the subscription's payments will be attributed to for tax reporting, and where funds from each payment will be transferred to for each of the subscription's invoices.|
|trial_end|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the subscription has a trial, the end of that trial.|
|trial_settings|[subscriptions_trials_resource_trial_settings](#schemasubscriptions_trials_resource_trial_settings) \| null|false|none|Settings related to subscription trials.|
|trial_start|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the subscription has a trial, the beginning of that trial.|
