Subscription items allow you to create customer subscriptions with more than
one plan, making it easy to represent complex billing relationships.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|billing_thresholds|[subscription_item_billing_thresholds](#schemasubscription_item_billing_thresholds) \| null|false|none|Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the related subscription advanced to a new billing period|
|created|integer|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|price|[price](#schemaprice)|true|none|Prices define the unit cost, currency, and (optional) billing cycle for both recurring and one-time purchases of products.<br>[Products](https://stripe.com/docs/api#products) help you track inventory or provisioning, and prices help you track payment terms. Different physical goods or levels of service should be represented by products, and pricing options should be represented by prices. This approach lets you change prices without having to change your provisioning scheme.<br><br>For example, you might have a single "gold" product that has prices for $10/month, $100/year, and €9 once.<br><br>Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription), [create an invoice](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/invoices/create), and more about [products and prices](https://stripe.com/docs/products-prices/overview).|
|quantity|integer|false|none|The [quantity](https://stripe.com/docs/subscriptions/quantities) of the plan to which the customer should be subscribed.|
|subscription|string|true|none|The `subscription` this `subscription_item` belongs to.|
|tax_rates|[[tax_rate](#schematax_rate)]|false|none|The tax rates which apply to this `subscription_item`. When set, the `default_tax_rates` on the subscription do not apply to this `subscription_item`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|subscription_item|

A subscription schedule allows you to create and manage the lifecycle of a subscription by predefining expected changes.

Related guide: [Subscription Schedules](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|application|string \| [application](#schemaapplication) \| [deleted_application](#schemadeleted_application) \| null|false|none|ID of the Connect Application that created the schedule.|
|canceled_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the subscription schedule was canceled. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|completed_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the subscription schedule was completed. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|current_phase|[subscription_schedule_current_phase](#schemasubscription_schedule_current_phase) \| null|false|none|Object representing the start and end dates for the current phase of the subscription schedule, if it is `active`.|
|customer|string \| [customer](#schemacustomer) \| [deleted_customer](#schemadeleted_customer)|true|none|ID of the customer who owns the subscription schedule.|
|default_settings|[subscription_schedules_resource_default_settings](#schemasubscription_schedules_resource_default_settings)|true|none|none|
|end_behavior|string|true|none|Behavior of the subscription schedule and underlying subscription when it ends. Possible values are `release` or `cancel` with the default being `release`. `release` will end the subscription schedule and keep the underlying subscription running.`cancel` will end the subscription schedule and cancel the underlying subscription.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|phases|[[subscription_schedule_phase_configuration](#schemasubscription_schedule_phase_configuration)]|true|none|Configuration for the subscription schedule's phases.|
|released_at|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Time at which the subscription schedule was released. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|released_subscription|string \| null|false|none|ID of the subscription once managed by the subscription schedule (if it is released).|
|status|string|true|none|The present status of the subscription schedule. Possible values are `not_started`, `active`, `completed`, `released`, and `canceled`. You can read more about the different states in our [behavior guide](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules).|
|subscription|string \| [subscription](#schemasubscription) \| null|false|none|ID of the subscription managed by the subscription schedule.|
|test_clock|string \| [test_helpers.test_clock](#schematest_helpers.test_clock) \| null|false|none|ID of the test clock this subscription schedule belongs to.|

A phase describes the plans, coupon, and trialing status of a subscription for a predefined time period.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|add_invoice_items|[[subscription_schedule_add_invoice_item](#schemasubscription_schedule_add_invoice_item)]|true|none|A list of prices and quantities that will generate invoice items appended to the next invoice for this phase.|
|application_fee_percent|number \| null|false|none|A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice subtotal that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account during this phase of the schedule.|
|automatic_tax|[schedules_phase_automatic_tax](#schemaschedules_phase_automatic_tax)|false|none|none|
|billing_cycle_anchor|string \| null|false|none|Possible values are `phase_start` or `automatic`. If `phase_start` then billing cycle anchor of the subscription is set to the start of the phase when entering the phase. If `automatic` then the billing cycle anchor is automatically modified as needed when entering the phase. For more information, see the billing cycle [documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/billing-cycle).|
|billing_thresholds|[subscription_billing_thresholds](#schemasubscription_billing_thresholds) \| null|false|none|Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the subscription advanced to a new billing period|
|collection_method|string \| null|false|none|Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay the underlying subscription at the end of each billing cycle using the default source attached to the customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`.|
|coupon|string \| [coupon](#schemacoupon) \| [deleted_coupon](#schemadeleted_coupon) \| null|false|none|ID of the coupon to use during this phase of the subscription schedule.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|default_payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|ID of the default payment method for the subscription schedule. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription schedule. If not set, invoices will use the default payment method in the customer's invoice settings.|
|default_tax_rates|[[tax_rate](#schematax_rate)]|false|none|The default tax rates to apply to the subscription during this phase of the subscription schedule.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Subscription description, meant to be displayable to the customer. Use this field to optionally store an explanation of the subscription.|
|end_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The end of this phase of the subscription schedule.|
|invoice_settings|[invoice_setting_subscription_schedule_setting](#schemainvoice_setting_subscription_schedule_setting) \| null|false|none|The invoice settings applicable during this phase.|
|items|[[subscription_schedule_configuration_item](#schemasubscription_schedule_configuration_item)]|true|none|Subscription items to configure the subscription to during this phase of the subscription schedule.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to a phase. Metadata on a schedule's phase will update the underlying subscription's `metadata` when the phase is entered. Updating the underlying subscription's `metadata` directly will not affect the current phase's `metadata`.|
|on_behalf_of|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the charge was made on behalf of for charges associated with the schedule's subscription. See the Connect documentation for details.|
|proration_behavior|string|true|none|If the subscription schedule will prorate when transitioning to this phase. Possible values are `create_prorations` and `none`.|
|start_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The start of this phase of the subscription schedule.|
|transfer_data|[subscription_transfer_data](#schemasubscription_transfer_data) \| null|false|none|The account (if any) the associated subscription's payments will be attributed to for tax reporting, and where funds from each payment will be transferred to for each of the subscription's invoices.|
|trial_end|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|When the trial ends within the phase.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|billing_cycle_anchor|automatic|
|billing_cycle_anchor|phase_start|
|collection_method|charge_automatically|
|collection_method|send_invoice|
|proration_behavior|always_invoice|
|proration_behavior|create_prorations|
|proration_behavior|none|

|default_payment_method|string \| [payment_method](#schemapayment_method) \| null|false|none|ID of the default payment method for the subscription schedule. If not set, invoices will use the default payment method in the customer's invoice settings.|

The Pause Collection settings determine how we will pause collection for this subscription and for how long the subscription
should be paused.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|behavior|string|true|none|The payment collection behavior for this subscription while paused. One of `keep_as_draft`, `mark_uncollectible`, or `void`.|

|behavior|mark_uncollectible|

Pending Updates store the changes pending from a previous update that will be applied
to the Subscription upon successful payment.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|billing_cycle_anchor|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|If the update is applied, determines the date of the first full invoice, and, for plans with `month` or `year` intervals, the day of the month for subsequent invoices. The timestamp is in UTC format.|
|expires_at|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The point after which the changes reflected by this update will be discarded and no longer applied.|
|subscription_items|[[subscription_item](#schemasubscription_item)]|false|none|List of subscription items, each with an attached plan, that will be set if the update is applied.|
|trial_end|integer(unix-time) \| null|false|none|Unix timestamp representing the end of the trial period the customer will get before being charged for the first time, if the update is applied.|
|trial_from_plan|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates if a plan's `trial_period_days` should be applied to the subscription. Setting `trial_end` per subscription is preferred, and this defaults to `false`. Setting this flag to `true` together with `trial_end` is not allowed. See [Using trial periods on subscriptions](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/trials) to learn more.|

<h2 id="tocS_tax_rate">tax_rate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematax_rate"></a>
<a id="schema_tax_rate"></a>
<a id="tocStax_rate"></a>
<a id="tocstax_rate"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "country": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "description": "string",
  "display_name": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "inclusive": true,
  "jurisdiction": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "tax_rate",
  "percentage": 0,
  "state": "string",
  "tax_type": "gst"
}
```

Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/invoices/tax-rates), [subscriptions](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/taxes) and [Checkout Sessions](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/checkout/set-up-a-subscription#tax-rates) to collect tax.

Related guide: [Tax Rates](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/taxes/tax-rates).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|none|Defaults to `true`. When set to `false`, this tax rate cannot be used with new applications or Checkout Sessions, but will still work for subscriptions and invoices that already have it set.|
|country|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the tax rate for your internal use only. It will not be visible to your customers.|
|display_name|string|true|none|The display name of the tax rates as it will appear to your customer on their receipt email, PDF, and the hosted invoice page.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|inclusive|boolean|true|none|This specifies if the tax rate is inclusive or exclusive.|
|jurisdiction|string \| null|false|none|The jurisdiction for the tax rate. You can use this label field for tax reporting purposes. It also appears on your customer’s invoice.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|percentage|number|true|none|This represents the tax rate percent out of 100.|
|state|string \| null|false|none|[ISO 3166-2 subdivision code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2:US), without country prefix. For example, "NY" for New York, United States.|
|tax_type|string \| null|false|none|The high-level tax type, such as `vat` or `sales_tax`.|

<h2 id="tocS_test_helpers.test_clock">test_helpers.test_clock</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematest_helpers.test_clock"></a>
<a id="schema_test_helpers.test_clock"></a>
<a id="tocStest_helpers.test_clock"></a>
<a id="tocstest_helpers.test_clock"></a>

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "deletes_after": 0,
  "frozen_time": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "name": "string",
  "object": "test_helpers.test_clock",
  "status": "advancing"
}
```

A test clock enables deterministic control over objects in testmode. With a test clock, you can create
objects at a frozen time in the past or future, and advance to a specific future time to observe webhooks and state changes. After the clock advances,
you can either validate the current state of your scenario (and test your assumptions), change the current state of your scenario (and test more complex scenarios), or keep advancing forward in time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|deletes_after|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which this clock is scheduled to auto delete.|
|frozen_time|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which all objects belonging to this clock are frozen.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The custom name supplied at creation.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the Test Clock.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|test_helpers.test_clock|
|status|advancing|
|status|internal_failure|
|status|ready|

<h2 id="tocS_token">token</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematoken"></a>
<a id="schema_token"></a>
<a id="tocStoken"></a>
<a id="tocstoken"></a>

```json
{
  "bank_account": {
    "account": "string",
    "account_holder_name": "string",
    "account_holder_type": "string",
    "account_type": "string",
    "available_payout_methods": [
      "instant"
    ],
    "bank_name": "string",
    "country": "string",
    "currency": "string",
    "customer": "string",
    "default_for_currency": true,
    "fingerprint": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "last4": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "object": "bank_account",
    "routing_number": "string",
    "status": "string"
  },
  "card": {
    "account": "string",
    "address_city": "string",
    "address_country": "string",
    "address_line1": "string",
    "address_line1_check": "string",
    "address_line2": "string",
    "address_state": "string",
    "address_zip": "string",
    "address_zip_check": "string",
    "available_payout_methods": [
      "instant"
    ],
    "brand": "string",
    "country": "string",
    "currency": "string",
    "customer": "string",
    "cvc_check": "string",
    "default_for_currency": true,
    "dynamic_last4": "string",
    "exp_month": 0,
    "exp_year": 0,
    "fingerprint": "string",
    "funding": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "last4": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "name": "string",
    "object": "card",
    "status": "string",
    "tokenization_method": "string"
  },
  "client_ip": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "token",
  "type": "string",
  "used": true
}
```

Tokenization is the process Stripe uses to collect sensitive card or bank
account details, or personally identifiable information (PII), directly from
your customers in a secure manner. A token representing this information is
returned to your server to use. You should use our
[recommended payments integrations](https://stripe.com/docs/payments) to perform this process
client-side. This ensures that no sensitive card data touches your server,
and allows your integration to operate in a PCI-compliant way.

If you cannot use client-side tokenization, you can also create tokens using
the API with either your publishable or secret API key. Keep in mind that if
your integration uses this method, you are responsible for any PCI compliance
that may be required, and you must keep your secret API key safe. Unlike with
client-side tokenization, your customer's information is not sent directly to
Stripe, so we cannot determine how it is handled or stored.

Tokens cannot be stored or used more than once. To store card or bank account
information for later use, you can create [Customer](https://stripe.com/docs/api#customers)
objects or [Custom accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/api#external_accounts). Note that
[Radar](https://stripe.com/docs/radar), our integrated solution for automatic fraud protection,
performs best with integrations that use client-side tokenization.

Related guide: [Accept a payment](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/accept-a-payment-charges#web-create-token)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bank_account|[bank_account](#schemabank_account)|false|none|These bank accounts are payment methods on `Customer` objects.<br><br>On the other hand [External Accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/api#external_accounts) are transfer<br>destinations on `Account` objects for [Custom accounts](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/custom-accounts).<br>They can be bank accounts or debit cards as well, and are documented in the links above.<br><br>Related guide: [Bank Debits and Transfers](https://stripe.com/docs/payments/bank-debits-transfers).|
|card|[card](#schemacard)|false|none|You can store multiple cards on a customer in order to charge the customer<br>later. You can also store multiple debit cards on a recipient in order to<br>transfer to those cards later.<br><br>Related guide: [Card Payments with Sources](https://stripe.com/docs/sources/cards).|
|client_ip|string \| null|false|none|IP address of the client that generated the token.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|type|string|true|none|Type of the token: `account`, `bank_account`, `card`, or `pii`.|
|used|boolean|true|none|Whether this token has already been used (tokens can be used only once).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|token|

To top up your Stripe balance, you create a top-up object. You can retrieve
individual top-ups, as well as list all top-ups. Top-ups are identified by a
unique, random ID.

Related guide: [Topping Up your Platform Account](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/top-ups).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount transferred.|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this top-up on your account balance. May not be specified depending on status of top-up.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|expected_availability_date|integer \| null|false|none|Date the funds are expected to arrive in your Stripe account for payouts. This factors in delays like weekends or bank holidays. May not be specified depending on status of top-up.|
|failure_code|string \| null|false|none|Error code explaining reason for top-up failure if available (see [the errors section](https://stripe.com/docs/api#errors) for a list of codes).|
|failure_message|string \| null|false|none|Message to user further explaining reason for top-up failure if available.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|source|[source](#schemasource) \| null|false|none|For most Stripe users, the source of every top-up is a bank account. This hash is then the [source object](https://stripe.com/docs/api#source_object) describing that bank account.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|Extra information about a top-up. This will appear on your source's bank statement. It must contain at least one letter.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the top-up is either `canceled`, `failed`, `pending`, `reversed`, or `succeeded`.|
|transfer_group|string \| null|false|none|A string that identifies this top-up as part of a group.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|topup|
|status|canceled|
|status|failed|
|status|pending|
|status|reversed|
|status|succeeded|

<h2 id="tocS_transfer">transfer</h2>


A `Transfer` object is created when you move funds between Stripe accounts as
part of Connect.

Before April 6, 2017, transfers also represented movement of funds from a
Stripe account to a card or bank account. This behavior has since been split
out into a [Payout](https://stripe.com/docs/api#payout_object) object, with corresponding payout endpoints. For more
information, read about the
[transfer/payout split](https://stripe.com/docs/transfer-payout-split).

Related guide: [Creating Separate Charges and Transfers](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount in %s to be transferred.|
|amount_reversed|integer|true|none|Amount in %s reversed (can be less than the amount attribute on the transfer if a partial reversal was issued).|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|Balance transaction that describes the impact of this transfer on your account balance.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time that this record of the transfer was first created.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|destination|string \| [account](#schemaaccount) \| null|false|none|ID of the Stripe account the transfer was sent to.|
|destination_payment|string \| [charge](#schemacharge)|false|none|If the destination is a Stripe account, this will be the ID of the payment that the destination account received for the transfer.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|reversals|object|true|none|A list of reversals that have been applied to the transfer.|
|reversed|boolean|true|none|Whether the transfer has been fully reversed. If the transfer is only partially reversed, this attribute will still be false.|
|source_transaction|string \| [charge](#schemacharge) \| null|false|none|ID of the charge or payment that was used to fund the transfer. If null, the transfer was funded from the available balance.|
|source_type|string|false|none|The source balance this transfer came from. One of `card`, `fpx`, or `bank_account`.|
|transfer_group|string \| null|false|none|A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. See the [Connect documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers#transfer-options) for details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|transfer|

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|false|none|Amount intended to be collected by this PaymentIntent. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).|
|destination|string \| [account](#schemaaccount)|true|none|The account (if any) the payment will be attributed to for tax<br>reporting, and where funds from the payment will be transferred to upon<br>payment success.|

<h2 id="tocS_transfer_reversal">transfer_reversal</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransfer_reversal"></a>
<a id="schema_transfer_reversal"></a>
<a id="tocStransfer_reversal"></a>
<a id="tocstransfer_reversal"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "balance_transaction": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "currency": "string",
  "destination_payment_refund": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "transfer_reversal",
  "source_refund": "string",
  "transfer": "string"
}
```

[Stripe Connect](https://stripe.com/docs/connect) platforms can reverse transfers made to a
connected account, either entirely or partially, and can also specify whether
to refund any related application fees. Transfer reversals add to the
platform's balance and subtract from the destination account's balance.

Reversing a transfer that was made for a [destination
charge](/docs/connect/destination-charges) is allowed only up to the amount of
the charge. It is possible to reverse a
[transfer_group](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers#transfer-options)
transfer only if the destination account has enough balance to cover the
reversal.

Related guide: [Reversing Transfers](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/charges-transfers#reversing-transfers).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount, in %s.|
|balance_transaction|string \| [balance_transaction](#schemabalance_transaction) \| null|false|none|Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|destination_payment_refund|string \| [refund](#schemarefund) \| null|false|none|Linked payment refund for the transfer reversal.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|source_refund|string \| [refund](#schemarefund) \| null|false|none|ID of the refund responsible for the transfer reversal.|
|transfer|string \| [transfer](#schematransfer)|true|none|ID of the transfer that was reversed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|transfer_reversal|


You can reverse some [ReceivedCredits](https://stripe.com/docs/api#received_credits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedCredit leads to the creation of a new object known as a CreditReversal.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount (in cents) transferred.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|financial_account|string|true|none|The FinancialAccount to reverse funds from.|
|hosted_regulatory_receipt_url|string \| null|false|none|A [hosted transaction receipt](https://stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|network|string|true|none|The rails used to reverse the funds.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|received_credit|string|true|none|The ReceivedCredit being reversed.|
|status|string|true|none|Status of the CreditReversal|
|status_transitions|[treasury_received_credits_resource_status_transitions](#schematreasury_received_credits_resource_status_transitions)|true|none|none|
|transaction|string \| [treasury.transaction](#schematreasury.transaction) \| null|false|none|The Transaction associated with this object.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|network|ach|
|network|stripe|
|object|treasury.credit_reversal|
|status|canceled|
|status|posted|
|status|processing|

You can reverse some [ReceivedDebits](https://stripe.com/docs/api#received_debits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedDebit leads to the creation of a new object known as a DebitReversal.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount (in cents) transferred.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|financial_account|string \| null|false|none|The FinancialAccount to reverse funds from.|
|hosted_regulatory_receipt_url|string \| null|false|none|A [hosted transaction receipt](https://stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|linked_flows|[treasury_received_debits_resource_debit_reversal_linked_flows](#schematreasury_received_debits_resource_debit_reversal_linked_flows) \| null|false|none|Other flows linked to a DebitReversal.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|network|string|true|none|The rails used to reverse the funds.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|received_debit|string|true|none|The ReceivedDebit being reversed.|
|status|string|true|none|Status of the DebitReversal|
|status_transitions|[treasury_received_debits_resource_status_transitions](#schematreasury_received_debits_resource_status_transitions)|true|none|none|
|transaction|string \| [treasury.transaction](#schematreasury.transaction) \| null|false|none|The Transaction associated with this object.|

|---|---|

|network|card|
|object|treasury.debit_reversal|
|status|failed|
|status|processing|
|status|succeeded|

Stripe Treasury provides users with a container for money called a FinancialAccount that is separate from their Payments balance.
FinancialAccounts serve as the source and destination of Treasury’s money movement APIs.

|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|

Use [InboundTransfers](https://stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/into/inbound-transfers) to add funds to your [FinancialAccount](https://stripe.com/docs/api#financial_accounts) via a PaymentMethod that is owned by you. The funds will be transferred via an ACH debit.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount (in cents) transferred.|
|cancelable|boolean|true|none|Returns `true` if the InboundTransfer is able to be canceled.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|failure_details|[treasury_inbound_transfers_resource_failure_details](#schematreasury_inbound_transfers_resource_failure_details) \| null|false|none|Details about this InboundTransfer's failure. Only set when status is `failed`.|
|financial_account|string|true|none|The FinancialAccount that received the funds.|
|hosted_regulatory_receipt_url|string \| null|false|none|A [hosted transaction receipt](https://stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|linked_flows|[treasury_inbound_transfers_resource_inbound_transfer_resource_linked_flows](#schematreasury_inbound_transfers_resource_inbound_transfer_resource_linked_flows)|true|none|none|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|origin_payment_method|string|true|none|The origin payment method to be debited for an InboundTransfer.|
|origin_payment_method_details|[inbound_transfers](#schemainbound_transfers) \| null|false|none|Details about the PaymentMethod for an InboundTransfer.|
|returned|boolean \| null|false|none|Returns `true` if the funds for an InboundTransfer were returned after the InboundTransfer went to the `succeeded` state.|
|statement_descriptor|string|true|none|Statement descriptor shown when funds are debited from the source. Not all payment networks support `statement_descriptor`.|
|status|string|true|none|Status of the InboundTransfer: `processing`, `succeeded`, `failed`, and `canceled`. An InboundTransfer is `processing` if it is created and pending. The status changes to `succeeded` once the funds have been "confirmed" and a `transaction` is created and posted. The status changes to `failed` if the transfer fails.|
|status_transitions|[treasury_inbound_transfers_resource_inbound_transfer_resource_status_transitions](#schematreasury_inbound_transfers_resource_inbound_transfer_resource_status_transitions)|true|none|none|

Use OutboundPayments to send funds to another party's external bank account or [FinancialAccount](https://stripe.com/docs/api#financial_accounts). To send money to an account belonging to the same user, use an [OutboundTransfer](https://stripe.com/docs/api#outbound_transfers).

Simulate OutboundPayment state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_payments` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Amount (in cents) transferred.|
|cancelable|boolean|true|none|Returns `true` if the object can be canceled, and `false` otherwise.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|customer|string \| null|false|none|ID of the [customer](https://stripe.com/docs/api/customers) to whom an OutboundPayment is sent.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|destination_payment_method|string \| null|false|none|The PaymentMethod via which an OutboundPayment is sent. This field can be empty if the OutboundPayment was created using `destination_payment_method_data`.|
|destination_payment_method_details|[outbound_payments_payment_method_details](#schemaoutbound_payments_payment_method_details) \| null|false|none|Details about the PaymentMethod for an OutboundPayment.|

Use OutboundTransfers to transfer funds from a [FinancialAccount](https://stripe.com/docs/api#financial_accounts) to a PaymentMethod belonging to the same entity. To send funds to a different party, use [OutboundPayments](https://stripe.com/docs/api#outbound_payments) instead. You can send funds over ACH rails or through a domestic wire transfer to a user's own external bank account.

Simulate OutboundTransfer state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_transfers` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects.

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|

|cancelable|boolean|true|none|Returns `true` if the object can be canceled, and `false` otherwise.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|currency|string|true|none|Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.|
|destination_payment_method|string \| null|false|none|The PaymentMethod used as the payment instrument for an OutboundTransfer.|
|destination_payment_method_details|[outbound_transfers_payment_method_details](#schemaoutbound_transfers_payment_method_details)|true|none|none|
|expected_arrival_date|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The date when funds are expected to arrive in the destination account.|
|financial_account|string|true|none|The FinancialAccount that funds were pulled from.|
|hosted_regulatory_receipt_url|string \| null|false|none|A [hosted transaction receipt](https://stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|returned_details|[treasury_outbound_transfers_resource_returned_details](#schematreasury_outbound_transfers_resource_returned_details) \| null|false|none|Details about a returned OutboundTransfer. Only set when the status is `returned`.|
|statement_descriptor|string|true|none|Information about the OutboundTransfer to be sent to the recipient account.|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the OutboundTransfer: `processing`, `failed`, `canceled`, `posted`, `returned`. An OutboundTransfer is `processing` if it has been created and is pending. The status changes to `posted` once the OutboundTransfer has been "confirmed" and funds have left the account, or to `failed` or `canceled`. If an OutboundTransfer fails to arrive at its destination, its status will change to `returned`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|credit_reversal|[treasury.credit_reversal](#schematreasury.credit_reversal)|false|none|You can reverse some [ReceivedCredits](https://stripe.com/docs/api#received_credits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedCredit leads to the creation of a new object known as a CreditReversal.|
|debit_reversal|[treasury.debit_reversal](#schematreasury.debit_reversal)|false|none|You can reverse some [ReceivedDebits](https://stripe.com/docs/api#received_debits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedDebit leads to the creation of a new object known as a DebitReversal.|
|inbound_transfer|[treasury.inbound_transfer](#schematreasury.inbound_transfer)|false|none|Use [InboundTransfers](https://stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/into/inbound-transfers) to add funds to your [FinancialAccount](https://stripe.com/docs/api#financial_accounts) via a PaymentMethod that is owned by you. The funds will be transferred via an ACH debit.|
|issuing_authorization|[issuing.authorization](#schemaissuing.authorization)|false|none|When an [issued card](https://stripe.com/docs/issuing) is used to make a purchase, an Issuing `Authorization`<br>object is created. [Authorizations](https://stripe.com/docs/issuing/purchases/authorizations) must be approved for the<br>purchase to be completed successfully.<br><br>Related guide: [Issued Card Authorizations](https://stripe.com/docs/issuing/purchases/authorizations).|
|outbound_payment|[treasury.outbound_payment](#schematreasury.outbound_payment)|false|none|Use OutboundPayments to send funds to another party's external bank account or [FinancialAccount](https://stripe.com/docs/api#financial_accounts). To send money to an account belonging to the same user, use an [OutboundTransfer](https://stripe.com/docs/api#outbound_transfers).<br><br>Simulate OutboundPayment state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_payments` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects.|
|outbound_transfer|[treasury.outbound_transfer](#schematreasury.outbound_transfer)|false|none|Use OutboundTransfers to transfer funds from a [FinancialAccount](https://stripe.com/docs/api#financial_accounts) to a PaymentMethod belonging to the same entity. To send funds to a different party, use [OutboundPayments](https://stripe.com/docs/api#outbound_payments) instead. You can send funds over ACH rails or through a domestic wire transfer to a user's own external bank account.<br><br>Simulate OutboundTransfer state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_transfers` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects.|
|received_credit|[treasury.received_credit](#schematreasury.received_credit)|false|none|ReceivedCredits represent funds sent to a [FinancialAccount](https://stripe.com/docs/api#financial_accounts) (for example, via ACH or wire). These money movements are not initiated from the FinancialAccount.|
|received_debit|[treasury.received_debit](#schematreasury.received_debit)|false|none|ReceivedDebits represent funds pulled from a [FinancialAccount](https://stripe.com/docs/api#financial_accounts). These are not initiated from the FinancialAccount.|
|type|string|true|none|Type of the flow that created the Transaction. Set to the same value as `flow_type`.|

|type|outbound_transfer|

<h2 id="tocS_usage_record">usage_record</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemausage_record"></a>
<a id="schema_usage_record"></a>
<a id="tocSusage_record"></a>
<a id="tocsusage_record"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "object": "usage_record",
  "quantity": 0,
  "subscription_item": "string",
  "timestamp": 0
}
```

Usage records allow you to report customer usage and metrics to Stripe for
metered billing of subscription prices.

Related guide: [Metered Billing](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/metered-billing).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|quantity|integer|true|none|The usage quantity for the specified date.|
|subscription_item|string|true|none|The ID of the subscription item this usage record contains data for.|
|timestamp|integer(unix-time)|true|none|The timestamp when this usage occurred.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|usage_record|

<h2 id="tocS_webhook_endpoint">webhook_endpoint</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawebhook_endpoint"></a>
<a id="schema_webhook_endpoint"></a>
<a id="tocSwebhook_endpoint"></a>
<a id="tocswebhook_endpoint"></a>

```json
{
  "api_version": "string",
  "application": "string",
  "created": 0,
  "description": "string",
  "enabled_events": [
    "string"
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "livemode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "object": "webhook_endpoint",
  "secret": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "url": "string"
}
```

You can configure [webhook endpoints](https://stripe.com/docs/webhooks/) via the API to be
notified about events that happen in your Stripe account or connected
accounts.

Most users configure webhooks from [the dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks), which provides a user interface for registering and testing your webhook endpoints.

Related guide: [Setting up Webhooks](https://stripe.com/docs/webhooks/configure).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|api_version|string \| null|false|none|The API version events are rendered as for this webhook endpoint.|
|application|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the associated Connect application.|
|created|integer(unix-time)|true|none|Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An optional description of what the webhook is used for.|
|enabled_events|[string]|true|none|The list of events to enable for this endpoint. `['*']` indicates that all events are enabled, except those that require explicit selection.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the object.|
|livemode|boolean|true|none|Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Set of [key-value pairs](https://stripe.com/docs/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|secret|string|false|none|The endpoint's secret, used to generate [webhook signatures](https://stripe.com/docs/webhooks/signatures). Only returned at creation.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the webhook. It can be `enabled` or `disabled`.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL of the webhook endpoint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|webhook_endpoint|
